prompt-pgp-passphrase.py makes a dummy PGP call to prompt for the user's passphrase early in the execution. This ensures the user is prompted at the beginning rather than waiting until signing is needed near the end of a process.

The script: Creates a temporary dummy file Attempts to sign it with GPG (which prompts for passphrase) Cleans up the temporary files Returns success even if GPG is not available (to avoid breaking workflows)
python3 scripts/prompt-pgp-passphrase.py

This script is typically called by other scripts (like push.py and release.py) at the beginning of their execution to: Prompt for PGP passphrase early Avoid delays later when signing is actually needed Provide a better user experience
Always returns 0 (success) to avoid breaking workflows Prints warnings if GPG is not available or if the prompt times out
Python 3.6 or higher GPG (optional, script handles gracefully if not available) No external Python dependencies (uses only standard library)

The script is designed to fail gracefully If GPG is not found, it prints a warning and continues If the prompt times out, it's treated as okay (user may not need signing) The dummy file and signature are automatically cleaned up

push.py runs Juneau's build and test gates and then commits and pushes what you have staged. It never stages anything: the index is the record of what you have reviewed, so the script commits the index exactly as it finds it and refuses to run while anything in the tree is unstaged or untracked. It runs on juneau-run, which draws its rows and keeps its logs and timing history.

Each step is a row in the console view. In order: Row What it does Prechecks Refuses before any gate unless git's user.email is the ASF committer address, the tree has no unreviewed changes, and the branch isn't behind its upstream (git fetch, then compare; no upstream passes, and a failed fetch refuses). When the sibling juneau-docs has something staged or unpushed commits, the same three checks run there too. Sonar Only with --sonarqube. See Optional gates. Tracker Only with --tracker-audit. See Optional gates. Tags scripts/check-container-tags.py: every test class that boots a container uses @SpringbootTest, @JettyMicroserviceTest or @TomcatMicroserviceTest. BOM scripts/check-bom-completeness.py: juneau-bom lists every consumer-facing module. Compile test.py --full's mvn clean install -DskipTests build. Java tests test.py's Maven test run. test.py adds its Perf row after it. Python tests test.py's run of scripts/tests, the tooling's own pytest suite. Browser tests test.py's *_BrowserTest run under -Pjs-tests. See Browser tests. Timing scripts/push-timings.py: compares this run's timings with the run history and writes the full table to test-timings.txt beside it. Advisory only; it never stops the push. Install Skipped, because test.py --full has already installed. With --skip-tests it runs mvn clean package install -DskipTests. Commit git commit -m <message> on the index as staged. Skipped when nothing is staged. Push git push to the branch's tracked upstream. Docs build, Docs, Docs push The juneau-docs follow-up. Tags through Timing are the test step; --skip-tests replaces them with one skipped Java tests row. A failed row stops the run, and nothing after it runs.

Stage each file as you review it, then run push.py. Just before it commits, the script checks the tree again: Something unstaged or untracked: it refuses and commits and pushes nothing, not even the staged part. Untracked files that git ignores don't count. The refusal lists the paths and the commands to set them aside for the run: git stash push -- <paths>, then git stash pop afterwards. There is no override flag. Nothing staged, but unpushed commits: it skips the commit and pushes those commits. Nothing staged and nothing to push: it says so and exits 0. Behind the upstream: it refuses. The upstream is checked again here because it can move during the build.

When a juneau-docs checkout sits beside juneau, a successful juneau push is followed by the same commit and push in juneau-docs, with the same commit message: Docs build runs scripts/build-docs.py --skip-maven there (a Docusaurus build, which runs verify-docs.py), only when something is staged. Docs commits the juneau-docs index as staged. Docs push pushes it, or pushes earlier unpushed commits when nothing is staged. The same rules apply there: an unstaged or untracked file in juneau-docs refuses the follow-up. Prechecks cover juneau-docs only when it has something staged or unpushed, so an idle juneau-docs with stray edits doesn't block a juneau push. If it becomes active during the build, its identity is checked just before its commit. The follow-up runs only after juneau itself committed or pushed something. To push juneau-docs on its own, use --docs-only.

cd /path/to/juneau python3 scripts/push.py "Your commit message here" Without a message, the script asks for one; an empty answer aborts. python3 scripts/push.py "Updated README" --skip-tests # no test step; Install builds instead python3 scripts/push.py "Testing changes" --dry-run # list the steps and evaluate the Prechecks only python3 scripts/push.py --test-only # gates only; no commit or push python3 scripts/push.py "Updated topic page" --docs-only # juneau-docs only

Option Effect message The commit message. Prompted for when omitted. Not used with --test-only. --test-only Runs only the build and test gates (Tags, BOM, the test step and Install). No Prechecks, commit, push or juneau-docs follow-up. Not the same as test.py --test-only, which means tests without the build. Can't be combined with --docs-only, --sonarqube, --tracker-audit or --skip-tests. --skip-tests Skips the test step (Tags through Timing). Install then runs mvn clean package install -DskipTests. --dry-run Prints the steps that would run and evaluates the Prechecks, then exits without building, committing or pushing. --docs-only Works on the sibling juneau-docs only: Prechecks there, then Docs build, Commit and Push. Skips everything on the juneau side, so --skip-tests and --sonarqube are ignored. Exits 0 when juneau-docs has nothing to commit or push. --js-tests Forces the Browser tests. Fails the push if Node or npm is missing. --no-js-tests Never runs the Browser tests. Can't be combined with --js-tests. --console full|board|none The console view. Default board; also JUNEAU_RUN_CONSOLE, and the flag wins. See Console view. --detail summary|actionable|modules|all How many sub-rows a finished row keeps. Default actionable; also JUNEAU_RUN_DETAIL. --sonarqube, --sonar Adds the Sonar gate. --tracker-audit, --todo-audit Adds the Tracker gate.

With neither --js-tests nor --no-js-tests, test.py decides: it runs the Browser tests when a .js, .cjs, .css or .ftl file under a src/ tree differs from origin/master, and otherwise marks the row skipped. If Node or npm is missing, an automatic run is skipped with a notice. push.py passes either flag through to test.py.

Both run right after the Prechecks, before any build, so they fail fast. Sonar (--sonarqube) runs scripts/sonarqube.py --all --run --fail-on-issues (with --branch <name> off master) and blocks the push if SonarCloud reports any open issue, of any severity. It reflects SonarCloud's last CI analysis of the branch, not your local diff. A branch SonarCloud hasn't analyzed yet passes with a warning. It needs Python 3.10 or later, which the script looks for on the PATH. Tracker (--tracker-audit) runs a maintainer's local work-tracker audit (~/Project Work/scripts/todo-status-audit.py) and blocks the push if it flags a plan file. It is a local check with no network access, and it fails when that tracker isn't present.

Python 3, and the juneau-run sources in the checkout (juneau-run/src/main/python/), which the script loads directly. Maven and Git on the PATH. Node and npm for the Browser tests, and Python 3.10 or later for --sonarqube. git's user.email set to the ASF committer address in juneau (and in juneau-docs when it is pushed). The script never writes git config; the refusal prints the command to run.
0 - Success, including a run with nothing to commit or push. 1 - A precheck, gate, build, test, commit or push failed. 2 - Invalid options. 130 - Cancelled with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM.
test.py juneau-run Scripts
release.py automates the complete release process for Apache Juneau, including prerequisite checks, building, testing, Maven release, binary artifact creation, and SVN distribution upload.

The script performs the following steps: Check Prerequisites - Verifies required tools are available Check Java Version - Automatically detects and verifies Java 17+ Check Maven Version - Automatically detects and verifies Maven 3+ Clean Maven Repository - Cleans local Maven repo (only on first run for a version) Make Git Folder - Creates staging directory Clone Juneau - Clones the repository to staging directory Configure Git - Sets up git user and email Run Clean Verify - Builds and verifies the project Run Deploy - Deploys to Maven staging repository Run Release Prepare - Prepares the Maven release Review Git Diff - Shows, in the pager, what release:prepare changed against the release tag, before release:perform Run Release Perform - Performs the Maven release Create Binary Artifacts - Downloads and processes source/binary artifacts Verify Distribution - Verifies files on Apache distribution site
python3 scripts/release.py The script will prompt you for the release candidate number.
python3 scripts/release.py --start-step run_release_perform
python3 scripts/release.py --list-steps
python3 scripts/release.py --skip-step clean_maven_repo
python3 scripts/release.py --resume

python3 scripts/release.py --revert The revert option will: Delete the git tag (both local and remote) Revert Maven versions back to the development snapshot Clean up SVN files (remove RC directories from dist.apache.org) The script will automatically detect the version and RC number from state files or history, or prompt you if needed.

--start-step STEP_NAME - Start execution from the specified step --list-steps - List all available steps and exit --skip-step STEP_NAME - Skip a specific step (can be used multiple times) --resume - Resume from the last checkpoint (if available) --revert - Revert a release by deleting the git tag, reverting Maven versions, and cleaning up SVN files

The script prompts for and sets the following environment variables: X_VERSION - Current release version (detected from pom.xml) X_NEXT_VERSION - Next version (calculated) X_RELEASE - Full release name (e.g., "juneau-9.2.0-RC1") X_RELEASE_CANDIDATE - Release candidate number (prompted for at start) X_STAGING - Staging directory path X_USERNAME - Apache username X_EMAIL - Apache email X_GIT_BRANCH - Git branch name X_JAVA_HOME - Java home directory X_CLEANM2 - Whether to clean Maven repo (Y/N)

The script maintains history files (release-history-{version}.json) that store: X_VERSION - The release version X_RELEASE_CANDIDATE - Release candidate number Default values for prompts (staging directory, username, email, etc.) Last run date Previous configuration values This allows the script to provide intelligent defaults on subsequent runs and enables the --revert option to automatically detect what needs to be reverted.

The script supports checkpoint/resume functionality: State is saved to ~/.juneau-release-state.json You can resume from any step using --resume or --start-step The release candidate number is prompted for at start, or extracted from state/history when resuming

After successful distribution verification, the script automatically generates a vote email body with: Version and RC number Distribution URLs SHA-512 checksums (fetched from URLs) Git commit hash Vote end date (72 hours from now) The email is printed to the console.
Python 3.6 or higher Java 17 or higher Maven 3 or higher Git GPG (for signing) SVN client (for distribution upload) wget (for downloading artifacts)

The script automatically excludes docs from the source release zip (via maven-source-plugin configuration) Source and binary artifacts are downloaded from Maven staging repository SHA512 checksum files are copied as-is from the Maven repository (they are automatically generated by Maven during deployment) Distribution verification checks for expected files on Apache distribution site The script uses current-release.py and maven-version.py for version detection Javadoc generation and test workspace creation have been removed from the release process The --revert option can be used to undo a release candidate if needed before voting
release-docs.py promotes documentation from the asf-staging branch to the asf-site branch, making it live on the production website.

The script: Checks that git is configured with the ASF committer identity Clones (or updates) a sibling ../asf-site/ checkout and fetches the asf-staging branch Switches to a detached HEAD at origin/asf-staging Force pushes to the asf-site branch
python3 scripts/release-docs.py ⚠️ WARNING: This will make the documentation live on the production website.
python3 scripts/release-docs.py --no-push

--no-push - Perform all steps except the final git push --juneau-root DIR - Juneau source checkout whose juneau-run draws the live view (default: JUNEAU_ROOT, then a sibling ../master/, then a sibling ../juneau/) --console full|board|none - Console output when the live view is available (default: JUNEAU_RUN_CONSOLE, then board)

When a Juneau checkout with juneau-run is found, the run is one live view with two rows: Prechecks (identity) and Promote (fetch, switch, and push, with the push shown as skipped under --no-push). Without juneau-run the script prints plain output.
Python 3.10 or higher Git (git command must be in PATH) Write access to the remote repository
0 - Success 1 - Error occurred

The script uses a persistent sibling ../asf-site/ checkout for git operations, reused by later runs If --no-push is used, the checkout is left at origin/asf-staging for manual inspection A success sound is played when the script completes successfully This script does NOT build documentation - it only promotes what's already in asf-staging

This script is typically used as the final step in the documentation release workflow: Make documentation changes Run release-docs-stage.py to deploy to staging Review the staging site at https://juneau.staged.apache.org Run release-docs.py to promote to production at https://juneau.apache.org
The script includes a warning message before promoting to production to ensure you understand the impact.
release-docs-stage.py builds the documentation and deploys it to the asf-staging branch, making it available on the staging website.

python3 scripts/release-docs-stage.py
python3 scripts/release-docs-stage.py --commit-message "Updated API documentation"
python3 scripts/release-docs-stage.py --no-push

--no-push - Build and commit but don't push to remote --commit-message MESSAGE - Custom commit message (default: "Deploy documentation staging") --juneau-root DIR - Juneau source checkout, passed on to build-docs.py (default: JUNEAU_ROOT, then a sibling ../master/, then a sibling ../juneau/) --console full|board|none - Console output when the live view is available (default: JUNEAU_RUN_CONSOLE, then board)

When the Juneau checkout includes juneau-run, the whole run is one live view: Prechecks (identity and branch), the rows of build-docs.py (Clean through Links), Stage push (fetch, copy, commit and push, with the push shown as skipped under --no-push), and URL, the staged site. Without juneau-run the script prints plain output, as build-docs.py does.
Python 3.10 or higher Git (git command must be in PATH) All prerequisites for build-docs.py (Node.js, npm, Maven, Java) Write access to the remote repository
0 - Success 1 - Error occurred

The script uses a persistent sibling ../asf-staging/ checkout for git operations, reused by later runs With --no-push the commit stays in ../asf-staging/ for manual inspection; nothing changes on the remote The script sets SITE_URL environment variable to https://juneau.staged.apache.org when building A success sound is played when the script completes successfully

This script is typically used as part of the documentation release workflow: Make documentation changes Run release-docs-stage.py to deploy to staging Review the staging site Run release-docs.py to promote to production
revert-staged.py reverts both staged AND unstaged changes for a file back to the last committed version (HEAD).

The script: Parses the arguments, so --help and bad arguments never reach git Verifies the file is tracked by git Warns the user about discarding changes Runs git restore --source=HEAD -- <file> to revert the file (the -- makes the path literal, so a name that starts with - or matches a ref is still read as a path)
python3 scripts/revert-staged.py <file_path> To restore a file whose name starts with -, put -- before it: python3 scripts/revert-staged.py -- -notes.txt
file_path - the file to restore (required, exactly one) -h, --help - print the usage text and exit without calling git
python3 scripts/revert-staged.py juneau-core/juneau-marshall/src/main/java/org/apache/juneau/ClassMeta.java
This will discard ALL changes (both staged and unstaged) for the specified file, reverting it back to the last commit.
0 - Success 1 - Error (file not tracked, git command failed) 2 - Bad arguments (usage text printed to stderr)
Python 3.6 or higher Git (git command must be in PATH) No external Python dependencies (uses only standard library)

The file must be tracked by git (the script verifies this) This is a destructive operation - changes cannot be recovered Use revert-unstaged.py if you only want to revert unstaged changes while preserving staged changes
revert-unstaged.py reverts working directory changes back to what's in the staging area (INDEX), preserving any staged changes.

The script: Parses the arguments, so --help and bad arguments never reach git Verifies the file exists Verifies the file is tracked by git (an untracked file has no staged version) Stops with "Nothing to revert" if the file already matches the staged version Runs git restore --worktree -- <file> to revert unstaged changes Preserves any staged changes
python3 scripts/revert-unstaged.py <file_path> To restore a file whose name starts with -, put -- before it: python3 scripts/revert-unstaged.py -- -notes.txt
file_path - the file to restore (required, exactly one) -h, --help - print the usage text and exit without calling git
python3 scripts/revert-unstaged.py juneau-core/juneau-marshall/src/main/java/org/apache/juneau/ClassMeta.java

This is useful when you have: Staged changes that you've tested and want to keep Unstaged changes that you want to discard The script will revert the working directory to match the staged version, effectively discarding only the unstaged changes.

0 - Success, or nothing to revert (the file already matches the staged version) 1 - Error (file not found, file not tracked by git, git restore failed) 2 - Bad arguments (usage text printed to stderr)
Python 3.6 or higher Git (git command must be in PATH) No external Python dependencies (uses only standard library)

This only affects unstaged changes - staged changes are preserved Use revert-staged.py if you want to revert both staged and unstaged changes The file must exist and be tracked by git (the script verifies both)
start-docusaurus.py starts the Docusaurus development server with automatic cleanup and process management.

The script performs these operations before starting the server: Kills Existing Processes - Automatically terminates any process running on port 3000 Clears Caches - Removes .docusaurus, build, and node_modules/.cache directories Starts Fresh Server - Launches the Docusaurus development server Cross-Platform - Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows
cd /path/to/juneau-docs python3 scripts/start-docusaurus.py The server will start at http://localhost:3000/ Press Ctrl+C to stop the server.
Use this script when: Starting development on documentation The server is acting strangely (cache issues) Need a clean server start Testing documentation changes locally
Python 3.6 or higher Node.js 18+ and npm Dependencies installed (npm install in juneau-docs directory) No external Python dependencies (uses only standard library)

The script resolves its working directory relative to its own location (scripts/../), i.e. the juneau-docs repository root it lives in - it does not need to be run from any particular directory itself Cache clearing is automatic - no flags needed The server supports hot-reloading (changes appear immediately in browser) Port 3000 must be available (script will kill existing processes)

start-petstore-jetty.py starts the Juneau petstore sample application using the embedded Jetty/Microservice container. It is a convenience launcher equivalent to running the org.apache.juneau.petstore.jetty.App main class via Maven's exec plugin.

The script: Locates the project root from its own filesystem position. Confirms juneau-petstore/juneau-petstore-jetty/target/classes exists; if not, runs mvn clean compile first. Invokes mvn exec:java -Dexec.mainClass=org.apache.juneau.petstore.jetty.App from the petstore-jetty module directory.

python3 scripts/start-petstore-jetty.py [--port N] --port N sets the port to listen on (default 10000); use it when another server already holds 10000. The script passes it to the petstore as the petstore.port system property, which juneau-petstore-jetty.cfg's [Jetty]/port entry reads, so the cfg file is never edited. The petstore boots on http://localhost:10000 by default. The microservice console is enabled — type help for available commands or exit to stop.

GET http://localhost:10000/petstore/pets — full pet listing. GET http://localhost:10000/petstore/pets/1 — single seeded pet (Mr. Frisky). GET http://localhost:10000/console/store, /console/pets — the petstore admin console; /console/dev/flavors/mustache shows the Mustache-rendered flavor. GET http://localhost:10000/petstore-ui/static/petstore-ui.html — React SPA demo. GET http://localhost:10000/console/dev/secure — bearer-token demo (secure API calls use Authorization: Bearer petstore-user). GET http://localhost:10000/petstore — Swagger UI for the petstore API.
Python 3.6 or higher Maven (must be on PATH) Java 17+
See juneau-petstore Overview for the application architecture. See start-petstore-springboot.py for the Spring Boot variant.

start-petstore-springboot.py starts the Juneau petstore sample application using Spring Boot's embedded servlet container. It is a convenience launcher equivalent to running mvn spring-boot:run from the petstore-springboot module.

The script: Locates the project root from its own filesystem position. Confirms juneau-petstore/juneau-petstore-springboot/target/classes exists; if not, runs mvn clean compile first. Invokes mvn spring-boot:run from the petstore-springboot module directory.
python3 scripts/start-petstore-springboot.py The petstore boots on http://localhost:5000 by default (configurable via application.properties's server.port or the PORT environment variable).

GET http://localhost:5000/petstore/pets — full pet listing. GET http://localhost:5000/petstore/pets/1 — single seeded pet (Mr. Frisky). GET http://localhost:5000/console/store, /console/pets — the petstore admin console; /console/dev/flavors/mustache shows the Mustache-rendered flavor. GET http://localhost:5000/petstore-ui/static/petstore-ui.html — React SPA demo. GET http://localhost:5000/console/dev/secure — bearer-token demo (secure API calls use Authorization: Bearer petstore-user). GET http://localhost:5000/petstore — Swagger UI for the petstore API. GET http://localhost:5000/hello — Spring @Autowired injection demo (deployment-specific).
Python 3.6 or higher Maven (must be on PATH) Java 17+
See juneau-petstore Overview for the application architecture. See start-petstore-jetty.py for the Jetty/Microservice variant.

test.py is the build and test helper script for Apache Juneau. It runs the Maven build, the Java tests, a performance guard, the tooling's own Python tests and the browser tests, each as a row on juneau-run, which also keeps the logs and the run history. push.py runs it as its test step.

A full run (the default) takes these steps in order, and stops at the first one that fails: Row What it runs Compile mvn clean install -T1C -DskipTests. Java tests mvn test -T1C -Drat.skip=true, one block per module. Perf The performance guard. Python tests scripts/tests, the tooling's own pytest suite, through python3 -m pytest when pytest is importable, else uv run --native-tls --with pytest. With neither, it prints a notice and skips. Nothing is installed. Browser tests The *_BrowserTest classes in juneau-rest-server-views, juneau-petstore-core and juneau-rest-server-terminal, under -Pjs-tests. See Browser tests. --build-only runs Compile alone. --test-only runs everything after Compile.
python3 scripts/test.py # or python3 scripts/test.py --full # or python3 scripts/test.py -f
python3 scripts/test.py --build-only # or python3 scripts/test.py -b
python3 scripts/test.py --test-only # or python3 scripts/test.py -t
python3 scripts/test.py --console board Draws one row per step instead of streaming Maven's output, and writes the raw output to a full log whose tail -f command the header prints. See Console view.

python3 scripts/test.py --no-container Adds -DexcludedGroups=container to the test run, leaving out tests tagged @Tag("container") (the Spring Boot, Jetty and Tomcat container tests), for a faster local loop when you only need core coverage.

python3 scripts/test.py --js-tests # always run them python3 scripts/test.py --no-js-tests # never run them The browser tests are excluded from the main test pass and run in their own step, as CI's js-tests, js-tests-petstore and js-tests-terminal jobs do. With neither flag, they run when a .js, .cjs, .css or .ftl file under a src/ tree differs from origin/master (committed, uncommitted or untracked), and otherwise the row shows as skipped. If Node or npm is missing, an automatic run is skipped with a notice, but --js-tests fails. The first run downloads Playwright and Chromium (it needs the network); later runs reuse target/js.

After the Java tests pass, the Perf row compares the wall-clock time of mvn test with the suite entry in the project-root perf-baseline.txt, and each module's time from Maven's Reactor Summary with its entry under [modules]. The suite breaches above its baseline plus JUNEAU_CI_PERF_THRESHOLD (default 0.20, so 20%). A module breaches only when it is over that and also more than JUNEAU_CI_PERF_MIN_SECONDS (default 3) seconds over its baseline. A module with no entry is reported and never fails. The report goes to target/perf-guard.txt. Breaches are warnings unless you pass --enforce-perf: python3 scripts/test.py --enforce-perf

python3 scripts/test.py --rebaseline Rewrites the suite line and the [modules] section of perf-baseline.txt from this repository's run history (~/.cache/juneau-run/history, see Run history and estimates), prints what changed, and exits without building. Each value is the median of the last --window passing runs (default 20) of the same command shape, rounded up to a tenth of a second, after dropping runs over three times the median. A module whose runs spread by more than 50% takes the 75th percentile instead. Keys with fewer than --min-runs runs (default 5) keep their value, and a module with no history is removed. The rest of the file is kept as it is.

python3 scripts/test.py --profile juneau-core/juneau-marshall Runs mvn test -pl <module> with a Java Flight Recorder recording and writes it to target/profile-results/<module>-<timestamp>.jfr. It replaces the test argLine, so the JaCoCo agent doesn't skew the profile. It runs instead of the build and tests.

Option Effect --full, -f Clean build, then the tests. The default. --build-only, -b Only the build. Can't be combined with --test-only. --test-only, -t Only the tests (Java, Perf, Python and Browser), with no build. --no-container Excludes @Tag("container") tests. --js-tests Also runs the browser tests. Fails if Node or npm is missing. --no-js-tests Never runs the browser tests. Can't be combined with --js-tests. --enforce-perf Fails the run on a performance-guard breach. --rebaseline Rewrites perf-baseline.txt from the run history, then exits. --window <n> With --rebaseline: the number of recent runs per key (default 20). --min-runs <n> With --rebaseline: skips keys with fewer runs than this (default 5). --console full|board|none The console view. Default full, which streams Maven's output live; also JUNEAU_RUN_CONSOLE, and the flag wins. --detail summary|actionable|modules|all How many sub-rows a finished row keeps. Default actionable; also JUNEAU_RUN_DETAIL. --full-log <path> Also appends every byte Maven prints to this file. --board-log <path> Also appends the board one-line-per-event stream to this file. --profile <module> Runs a one-shot JFR profile of the module's tests. --verbose, -v Accepted for compatibility and has no effect: Maven's output always streams live. --timing-log <path> Ignored, with a warning: timings are in the run history now. It will be removed in a later release. --help, -h Shows the help message.

Variable Effect JUNEAU_MVN_WRAPPER A prefix for every mvn command, such as a lock script that serializes concurrent runs on one checkout. JUNEAU_CI_PERF_THRESHOLD The performance guard's tolerance (default 0.20). JUNEAU_CI_PERF_MIN_SECONDS The seconds a module must also exceed its baseline by (default 3). JUNEAU_PUSH_NO_SOUND=1 Silences the bell at the end of a run. Under push.py, only push.py rings it.

0 - Success. 1 - An unknown option, a conflicting pair of options, or a failed performance guard (with --enforce-perf), Python test run or browser test run. 2 - An invalid --detail value. 130 - Cancelled with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. Otherwise, Maven's own exit code when the build or Java tests fail.

Python 3, and the juneau-run sources in the checkout (juneau-run/src/main/python/), which the script loads directly. Maven on the PATH. Node and npm for the browser tests, and pytest or uv for the Python tests.
push.py juneau-run Scripts

Apache Juneau includes a collection of Python scripts in the scripts/ directory that automate various development, build, test, and release tasks. These scripts help maintain code quality, streamline workflows, and ensure consistency across the project.

Scripts are organized into two categories based on which branch/repo checkout they're located in. This index covers the most commonly-used developer scripts; a handful of narrowly-scoped or CI-internal scripts are listed without dedicated pages.

These scripts are located in the master branch (the juneau repository/checkout) and are used for code development, testing, and releases: Script Description Details test.py Build and test helper script Learn more → push.py Build, test, and push to repository Learn more → release.py Complete release automation Learn more → prompt-pgp-passphrase.py Prompt for PGP passphrase early Learn more → current-release.py Get current release version Learn more → maven-version.py Get Maven version Learn more → apply-eclipse-prefs.py Apply Eclipse preferences Learn more → cleanup-whitespace.py Clean up whitespace in Java files Learn more → check-fluent-setter-overrides.py Check fluent setter overrides Learn more → revert-staged.py Revert staged git changes Learn more → revert-unstaged.py Revert unstaged git changes Learn more → start-petstore-jetty.py Start the petstore showcase under Jetty/Microservice Learn more → start-petstore-springboot.py Start the petstore showcase under Spring Boot Learn more → check-bom-completeness.py Verifies the published juneau-bom lists all reactor modules — check-container-tags.py Guardrail that verifies container-backed tests are tagged correctly — ci-perf-guard.py CI wall-clock performance regression guard, per module/bucket — coverage.py Generates and reports JaCoCo test coverage — microbench.py Runs JMH micro-benchmarks — normalize-generic-commas.py Normalizes comma spacing in generic type arguments — push-timings.py Reports timing deltas from test.py's run history (the push.py Timing row) — slack-notify.py Sends build/release notifications to Slack — sonarqube.py Reports SonarQube/SonarCloud findings from the command line — surefire-rollup.py Rolls up Surefire XML results into per-module/bucket timing summaries — view-sonar-category.py Views SonarQube issue categories non-interactively —

These scripts are located in the docs branch (the juneau-docs repository/checkout) and are used for documentation building, validation, and deployment: Script Description Details verify-docs.py Docs integrity checker - validates frontmatter, slugs, sidebar structure, and internal links; the primary "does the site check out?" gate See check-topic-links.py for a related, narrower link-only check release-docs-stage.py Stage documentation to asf-staging Learn more → release-docs.py Promote documentation to production Learn more → build-docs.py Build complete documentation Learn more → create-mvn-site.py Generate Maven site for testing Learn more → start-docusaurus.py Start Docusaurus dev server Learn more → check-topic-links.py Validate documentation links Learn more → generate-ai-artifacts.py / check-ai-artifacts.py Generate and validate machine-consumable AI knowledge artifacts Learn more → apply-renames.py Mechanical bulk URL/text substitution pass across pages/ — normalize-headings.py Normalizes Markdown heading structure under pages/topics/ — Note: verify-docs.py is the primary docs-integrity gate - run python3 scripts/verify-docs.py --strict --anchors from the juneau-docs repository root before publishing any documentation change. See the script's --help output for the full list of checks and flags.

All scripts share the following characteristics: Python 3.6+ - Written in Python using only the standard library No External Dependencies - All scripts use only Python standard library modules Cross-Platform - Work on macOS, Linux, and Windows Error Handling - Provide clear error messages and exit codes Documentation - Each script has detailed documentation in the Docusaurus topics
Each script supports a --help flag to display usage information: python3 scripts/<script-name>.py --help For detailed documentation, see the individual script topic pages linked above.

Most scripts require: Python 3.6 or higher Maven (for build/test/release scripts) Git (for version control scripts) Node.js and npm (for documentation scripts) Specific requirements are documented in each script's topic page.

Date: TBD Juneau 10.0.0 is a major version release representing a significant milestone for the Apache Juneau project. This release folds in the never-shipped 9.5 development line and also delivers a broad code-quality and maintainability uplift via an extensive SonarQube/SonarLint cleanup pass across the entire codebase.

This is the first release in the 10.x line. The jump from 9.x to 10.0 reflects accumulated breaking changes in the API surface and internal architecture that warranted a major version boundary, following Semantic Versioning conventions. Consumers upgrading from 9.4.x or earlier should consult the V10.0 Migration Guide for a complete list of breaking changes.

This release includes an extensive SonarQube / SonarLint cleanup pass across the entire Juneau codebase, addressing hundreds of code-quality findings including: Removed dead/unreachable code and unused variables. Fixed resource-leak issues (try-with-resources, explicit close calls). Resolved potentially null-dereference paths and improved null-safety. Replaced raw types with proper generic parameterization. Addressed improper exception handling patterns (swallowed exceptions, overly broad catch blocks). Cleaned up redundant casts, unnecessary object creation, and other minor inefficiencies. Suppressed or resolved remaining SonarQube rule violations with documented rationale. No functional behavior was changed as part of this cleanup; all changes were purely mechanical code-quality improvements.

Juneau now supports view-based projection: declare named views on bean properties and select an active view per serialize/parse call so only the in-view properties are emitted or consumed. This is the Juneau equivalent of Jackson's @JsonView / MapperFeature.DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION. Tag a property with one or more string view names via the new view member on @MarshalledProp: public class Person { public String id; // untagged — visible in every view @MarshalledProp(view = "summary") public String name; @MarshalledProp(view = "detail") public String description; } Activate a view on any serializer or parser builder, or override it per call on a session: // Context-level default: var s = Json5Serializer.DEFAULT.copy().activeView("summary").build(); s.write(person); // → {id:'1',name:'Alice'} // Per-call session override: s.createSession().activeView("detail").build().write(person); // → {description:'A person',id:'1'} Key behaviours: Default-view policy: untagged properties are included in all views by default (mirrors Jackson's DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION=true). Call disableDefaultViewInclusion() to reverse. Union semantics: @MarshalledProp(view = {"A","B"}) makes a property visible when A or B is active. Flat string names: no marker-class hierarchy required. Parse-side: out-of-view input properties are routed through the existing unknown/ignored-property mechanism (silently ignored by default; ignoreUnknownBeanProperties(false) makes them throw). Mix-in support: view membership can be applied to unmodifiable classes via @MarshalledPropApply / applyAnnotations(), just like any other @MarshalledProp attribute. Cross-format: projection is model-level and behaves identically across JSON, XML, HTML, MsgPack, and all other Juneau formats. See the View-Based Projection topic page for full documentation and a Jackson migration table.

Marshalling now deproxifies objects whose runtime class ClassUtils.getProxyFor recognizes, including Hibernate 6/7 lazy association proxies ($HibernateProxy$ in the class name). Serializers use the unwrapped class (immediate superclass for subclass proxies; first interface for JDK proxies) so handler fields and proxy _type names are not emitted. This is a core getClassMetaForObject change across all formats — not a juneau-marshall-hibernate module, and not a parse-into-@Entity feature. See JPA and Hibernate.

Juneau 10.0 adds two Spring-Boot-style ergonomics to the config + settings system, both additive and off-by-default so existing configs are unaffected: Config profiles — a <name>-<profile> overlay (e.g. my-stage.cfg, or my-stage.yml for YAML bases) is merged over the base config when a profile is active. Profile entries win over base, base-only keys survive, and for multiple active profiles the last one wins. Activated via Config.Builder.profiles(...) or the juneau.profiles.active key (system property / env var / config). Resolution happens at the store layer (ProfileConfigStore + ProfileMerge), so variable resolution, format handling, and live reload (a change to the base or any active profile file re-fires change listeners) all behave exactly as for a single-file config. When the Spring Boot bridge is present, juneau.profiles.active piggybacks on Environment.getActiveProfiles() for a single source of truth. Relaxed binding — a single logical config key resolves from any common environment spelling, so k8s-style env vars map cleanly: my.prop / myProp / MySection/myKey are satisfied by MY_PROP / MY_SECTION_MY_KEY. The default Settings env source is wrapped with RelaxedPropertySource (verbatim-first, so exact-match is preserved); it can wrap any other PropertySource too. See the new Config Profiles & Relaxed Binding topic page for the activation conventions, overlay/merge precedence, and the candidate-generation rules.
documents.s: Config profiles + relaxed binding (cloud-native environment config)

documents.t: Juneau 10.0 adds a new @ConfigProperties(prefix = "...") annotation (org.apache.juneau.commons.inject) — Juneau's analog of Spring Boot's @ConfigurationProperties — plus its underlying, independently-callable engine, ConfigPropertiesBinder. Where @Value resolves one configuration value onto one field, @ConfigProperties resolves an entire prefix onto every field of a POJO in one pass: @ConfigProperties(prefix = "MyService") public class MyServiceProperties { public String host = "localhost"; public int port = 8080; } Relaxed key matching by default — reuses RelaxedPropertySource.candidates(...), so MyService.host, MY_SERVICE_HOST, and my.service.host are all equivalent. Same source-chain precedence as @Value — thread-local/global test overrides, then any caller-scoped PropertySource beans, then the process-wide Settings chain (registered sources, system properties, system environment). Nested config objects — a field whose type is itself @ConfigProperties-annotated binds recursively under a sub-prefix. Coexists with @Value/@Inject on the same class — fields owned by either are never touched by the whole-object bind. Auto-registered in the BeanStore — the bound instance is retrievable via beanStore.getBean(...) or plain @Inject anywhere downstream. Current limitations: no Optional<T>/Supplier<T> field types (raw-type conversion only); validation is a no-op extension seam (ConfigPropertiesValidator.NO_OP) reserved for a future release. Pilot: RestContextProperties. As proof, RestContext's 15 same-prefix RestContext.* env-driven-default @Value fields have been collapsed into a single public @ConfigProperties(prefix = "RestContext") bean, RestContextProperties, retrievable via the new RestContext.getRestContextProperties() or from the resource's BeanStore. Every existing RestContext getter keeps its exact signature and @Rest-annotation-blending behavior — only the source of the underlying default moved. RestContext.uriAuthority/uriContext (a null-vs-empty distinction the binder's raw-type conversion can't express in v1) are unaffected and remain plain @Value fields. See the new @ConfigProperties Annotation Basics topic page, and the RestContext topic page for the pilot. @Bean factory-method fixes (juneau-rest-server / juneau-commons). Several @Bean(name=...) factory methods of the same type on a @Rest class now each register their own result. Previously they collapsed into one bean, so @Named("cache") could receive the "db" bean, and health indicators were lost. Each @Bean method is invoked exactly once: overridden methods once, and named framework types such as @Bean(name="encoders") EncoderSet are no longer invoked twice or exported to child resources. @Bean methods may now be protected, package-private or private, matching @Configuration classes. The @Bean("x") value form now matches named framework slots. New: BeanStore.invokeBeanMethod(...) and BeanAnnotation.find(MethodInfo).
documents.s: @ConfigProperties — prefix-scoped whole-object config binding, with RestContext as the pilot

documents.t: Juneau 10.0 adds a small, JDK-only SecretStore SPI (org.apache.juneau.commons.secret, @since 10.0.0) for storing and retrieving secrets by key — store / find / exists / delete. It is the secure, mutable sibling of PropertySource: values are held as char[] (never String), and are never toString()'d, logged, or dumped. InMemorySecretStore — the zero-config, ConcurrentHashMap-backed, process-local default (honest about being neither persistent nor cross-node), with defensive-copy in/out so callers can zero their own arrays. EnvVarSecretStore — a read-only store backed by System.getenv (store/delete are unsupported). SecretStoreProvider + META-INF/services — ServiceLoader discovery mirroring PropertySourceProvider; opt-in via SecretStores.fromServiceLoader(). SecretStores.resolve(beanStore) — resolves the active store from a BeanStore, defaulting to InMemorySecretStore (the BeanStore-with-drop-in-default idiom used elsewhere in the framework). Opt-in Settings bridge — SecretStorePropertySource exposes a chosen store as a PropertySource only where a consumer deliberately wires it, and implements the SensitivePropertySource marker so dump/log/toString() paths redact bridged values. Secrets stay out of the general config/$P{...}/SVL namespace by default. New opt-in module juneau-secret-macos-keychain — a KeychainSecretStore backed by the macOS security keychain CLI, honoring a ReplayCache-style FailMode (fail-open/fail-closed) for backend-unavailable behavior. It lives outside juneau-commons because it shells out to an OS process. store sends the command to security -i on stdin, so the secret never appears on a command line and a JVM started from a terminal is never left waiting on a password prompt. find reads the password from security find-generic-password -g, so secrets containing tabs, other control characters, non-ASCII text, quotes or backslashes come back exactly as stored. See the Secrets section of the Settings topic page for details.
documents.s: SecretStore SPI — the secure, mutable sibling of PropertySource

documents.t: org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery is a protocol-agnostic API for searching, sorting, projecting and paging rows of beans, in memory or over JDBC. Engines follow a context/session split: Immutable, builder-built contexts. InMemoryBeanQueryContext.create(Person.class)...build() and SqlBeanQueryContext.create(Person.class)...build() fix the columns, operators, limits and a server-side guard once. copy() derives a variant. Per-request sessions. getSession(rows) / getSession(), or createSession()...build() for per-request rules: narrow the columns, override the limits, add a guard, or pass a caller-owned JDBC Connection. A session offers find, findValues, count, stream, streamValues and resolve. Validate before run. Every query is resolved into a ResolvedQuery first. Unknown columns, disallowed operators, over-long search strings, too many clauses or sort keys, and over-deep expressions are rejected with BeanQuerySyntaxException; they are never silently dropped. defaultLimit (100) applies when limit is missing; a limit above maxLimit (1000) is clamped to it, never rejected. Counts by policy. CountPolicy (NONE, MATCHED, BOTH, IF_REQUESTED) decides which counts a Page carries. Page.total()/Page.matched() are independently-optional (see below). Safe regex. $regex is enabled by default; allowRegex(false) disables it. In memory, each call's regex matching shares one regexTimeout deadline (default 50 ms). Engine errors. Failures raise BeanQueryExecutionException (a server error), whose message names no SQL or bind values. SQL engine. Guards are parenthesized and AND-ed into every statement. There are fetch-size and query-timeout settings, and connections come from a DataSource or supplier and are released by the session. stream reads rows lazily and closes its cursor with the stream or the session. DataTables. The juneau-rest-server-datatables adapter runs on the new session API. It asks for counts with CountRequest.BOTH on the query builder and maps length=-1 to maxLimit. BeanQuery.Builder/GroupBuilder. Replace the removed BeanQueryBuilder. Fluent eq/ne/in/contains/prefix/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/regex/op/search conditions, promotable into cross-column $or/$and/$not groups via GroupBuilder. Repeated conditions on the same column built through the fluent API no longer silently overwrite each other — they merge into an implicit $and(...). One resolved search tree. Filter/FilterResolver/FilterEvaluator give the in-memory and SQL engines a single, already-validated search tree to walk instead of each parsing search strings independently. Independently-optional counts. Page.hasTotal() is gone; Page.total()/Page.matched() are OptionalLong, so a caller that did not ask for a count gets an empty OptionalLong back rather than an exception. DataTables global search box + legacy-search parity. The DataTables adapter now maps the global search box to a synthesized $or across searchable columns, each with a leaf chosen by its declared SearchType ($contains for TEXT/ID, $prefix for VERSION, $eqic for ENUM, and $eq conditionally for NUMERIC/BOOLEAN/TIMESTAMP only when the global term parses as that type, otherwise that column is silently skipped) instead of $contains for every column, and reports counts through the OptionalLong pair above. RelativeDuration literals. A signed [+-]<n>(ms|s|m|h|d) wire literal (e.g. -24h for "24 hours ago") round-trips through the builder for TIMESTAMP/duration columns (parity with a common legacy search syntax). Search language hardening. $eq/$in/$ne are now exact and case-sensitive, with a new case-insensitive $eqic counterpart; a ? single-character wildcard joins the existing *; a quoted token bypasses wildcard interpretation entirely; $$ is the literal-dollar escape; operator names are case-insensitive; $regex gains an optional flags=i|m|s argument; SearchOperator is now immutable (create(...).build(), with copy() for a pre-filled builder) with a typed extension(Class<X>) hook replacing the untyped sql(Object) hook; parse failures throw BeanQuerySyntaxException with a specific Code; a shared JSON parity corpus keeps the server (Java) and client (juneau-search.js) engines byte-for-byte identical; and SearchType.bareHelp() adds per-type search help text, including a UTC-midnight clarification for bare TIMESTAMP values. See the Porting searches from another $-operator syntax note on the topic page below for migrating a case-insensitive $eq(...) search. Postgres dialect and typed binds. PostgresDialect lives in its own module and package (juneau-beanquery-postgres, org.apache.juneau.beanquery.postgres). Search literals are parsed once per query by SearchType.parse(String) (NUMERIC to BigDecimal, BOOLEAN to Boolean, TIMESTAMP to OffsetDateTime/LocalDateTime/LocalDate) and exposed as SearchExpression.typedValue()/typedArgs(). A value that does not parse for its column type is BeanQuerySyntaxException.Code.BAD_VALUE (HTTP 400) in both the in-memory and SQL engines. SearchSqlRenderer and SqlDialect take typed Object values, and a custom operator opts in with SearchOperator.Builder.typedArgs(true). Relative-duration literals [+-]<n>(ms|s|m|h|d) work for NUMERIC and TIMESTAMP columns and resolve against a single per-query request time. ISO-8601 durations in BeanQuery. Wherever a NUMERIC or TIMESTAMP column accepts a relative literal such as -24h, it now also accepts a signed ISO-8601 duration (PT24H, -PT24H, +PT30M, P1D) with identical semantics, in the in-memory and SQL engines and in juneau-search.js; invalid ISO text is BAD_VALUE. Existing literals and bare epoch milliseconds are unchanged. Built-in SQL row mappers. SqlRowMapper.map() and SqlRowMapper.bean(Class) (records or setter beans), chosen automatically by SqlBeanQueryContext.Builder.build() when no rowMapper(...) is set. In-memory and SQL parity. A SQL dialect that does not support an operator (such as $regex), or that does not declare supportsVersionOrdering() for the VERSION range operators, rejects that query with BAD_VALUE instead of silently returning different rows. PostgresDialect compares ENUM columns as text (wildcards included), compares VERSION columns as dotted-integer tuples, renders $regex with the POSIX ~/~* operators (mirroring flags=i|m|s; Postgres and Java regex syntax differ), and makes $not match NULL cells as the in-memory engine does. BREAKING: PostgresDialect moved to org.apache.juneau.beanquery.postgres, and SearchSqlRenderer/SqlDialect.renderBare now receive typed Object values. See the Migration Guide. See the new BeanQuery Package topic page.

juneau-microservice-jetty now ships a thin convenience facade, JettyMicroservice, that collapses the Microservice + JettyConfiguration bootstrap into a single static call, plus classpath defaults for jetty.xml and juneau.cfg. End result: stand up a Jetty-backed Juneau microservice with one Maven dependency and one @Bean Servlet. public class App { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { JettyMicroservice.run(args, new RootResources()).join(); } } Bundled classpath defaults (all overridable): jetty.xml — single plain-HTTP ServerConnector on $S{availablePort,10000}. No resourceBase / WebAppContext / ResourceHandler filesystem mount is registered (no static-file serving by default). Servlets are auto-mounted by JettyServerComponent from @Bean Servlet contributions. juneau.cfg — sections for [Jetty] (port, jetty.xml reference, var resolution), [REST] (default theme), [Console] (interactive console enabled with the standard exit / restart / help / config commands), [Logging] (logDir), and [SystemProperties] (Jetty SLF4J adapter wiring). Override semantics are unchanged: a consumer-supplied jetty.xml or juneau.cfg on the working directory or earlier on the classpath wins, as does a @Bean JettyServerFactory / @Bean JettySettings in the consumer's @Configuration. The JettyMicroservice.run(...) facade has three overloads: run(String[] args, Servlet rootServlet) — interactive console enabled. run(String[] args, Servlet rootServlet, boolean startConsole) — explicit console opt-in/out. run(String[] args, WritableBeanStore beanStore, boolean startConsole, Class<?>... configurations) — power-user form for callers contributing multiple @Bean Servlets, custom MicroserviceListeners, or a parent bean store.

The legacy juneau-my-jetty-microservice template module has been removed from the reactor. Consumers should migrate to the new JettyMicroservice facade in juneau-microservice-jetty — it delivers the same zero-config developer experience without requiring the consumer to copy a template project.

org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widget.ThemeMenuItem and its $W{ThemeMenuItem} variable are gone, with no @Deprecated stage. Its links used a ?stylesheet= query parameter that nothing in the server ever read, so it never switched a page's theme. Remove it from @HtmlDocConfig(widgets, navlinks); to change the stylesheet, set @HtmlDocConfig(stylesheet) or the REST/theme config entry. See Stylesheets.

Both embedded-server microservice flavors now perform a zero-downtime graceful shutdown suitable for rolling Kubernetes deployments, sharing one identical shutdown contract. On shutdown, a shared ReadinessState flag is flipped before the listening connector stops, so GET /readyz immediately returns 503 (state=OUT_OF_SERVICE) while a load balancer / Kubernetes is still routing. GET /livez and GET /healthz stay healthy, so the orchestrator does not kill the pod mid-drain. The server then waits up to a bounded stopTimeout (default 30s) for in-flight requests to drain — Jetty via server.setStopTimeout(...), Tomcat by pausing the connector and waiting for the active request count to reach zero — with an optional shutdownSettleDelay between the readiness flip and the connector stop. New shared org.apache.juneau.rest.server.health.ReadinessState flag, consulted by HealthAggregator to gate the READY probe (liveness and the aggregate health surface are unaffected). New stopTimeout / shutdownSettleDelay knobs on both JettySettings and TomcatSettings, also configurable via juneau.cfg ([Jetty] / [Tomcat] sections, in milliseconds). Precedence: programmatic settings > config-file entry > (Jetty only: jetty.xml value) > 30s default. Bundled juneau.cfg documents the knobs and the recommended Kubernetes preStop hook + terminationGracePeriodSeconds pairing. MCP subscriptions/listen streams no longer hold the drain open. Those SSE streams never finish on their own, so a stop with any subscriber connected used to wait out the full stopTimeout (30s by default). ReadinessState gained onOutOfService(key, callback), servlets can opt in via the new ReadinessStateAware interface, and AbstractMcpRestServlet uses it to close its subscriptions (new McpSubscriptionBroker.closeAll(), a no-op by default) as soon as shutdown begins, so each stream sends its terminal frame and completes. @Bean JettySettings jettySettings() { return JettySettings.create() .stopTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(45)) .shutdownSettleDelay(Duration.ofSeconds(2)) .build(); } See the new Graceful Shutdown & Readiness Gating topic page for details, including the Jetty/Tomcat parity table and Kubernetes deployment guidance.
documents.s: Graceful shutdown + readiness gating (zero-downtime k8s rollouts)

documents.t: A new ServletFilterRegistration bean mounts a jakarta.servlet.Filter on JettyServerComponent or TomcatServerComponent before the server starts, with URL patterns, explicit dispatcher types (REQUEST, FORWARD, ASYNC, ERROR) and a defined order relative to the auto-mounted AuthFilterChain. Previously only the REQUEST dispatch was reachable and only after start-up. The AuthFilterChain auto-mount now goes through the same ordered path. The petstore Jetty runner uses it for its console boundary and no longer wraps the root servlet. On Tomcat, servlets mounted through TomcatServerComponent.addServlet are now async-capable (request.isAsyncSupported() is true), matching Jetty, so async @RestOp return types use the real async path instead of falling back to synchronous handling.
documents.s: Servlet filter registration for microservice apps

documents.t: A new juneau-microservice-test module adds @MicroserviceTest, a JUnit 5 extension that boots a whole Microservice (config + lifecycle + embedded Jetty on an ephemeral port) for a test class — the standalone-microservice analog of Spring's @SpringBootTest. Explicit SUT. Declare the system under test via @MicroserviceTest(configurations={...}) and/or a static Microservice.Builder microserviceBuilder() supplier method (no classpath scanning). The extension adds an ephemeral-Jetty Server (port 0) + JettyConfiguration automatically; Jetty for v1 (Tomcat pluggability is a follow-on). Composes the existing @TestBean substrate (no parallel injection annotation). Default Mode INJECT installs overrides via Microservice.Builder.overridingBeanStore(...) before boot, so the service reads them from startup; Mode OVERLAY pushes/pops against the booted instance. Parameter resolution for RestClient (bound to the booted root URL — the primary convenience), Microservice, WritableBeanStore, and the bound port. Fresh instance per class, stopped cleanly in teardown (restart is unsupported); stop() restores process globals so multiple @MicroserviceTest classes are isolated within a JVM. The bound port is always read from the live ServerConnector. Distinct from MockRestClient: use @MicroserviceTest for a real server/lifecycle over HTTP, MockRestClient for in-JVM single-resource tests. This also added a small public composition entry point — JuneauBeanStoreExtension.discoverOverrides(...) — so other JUnit 5 extensions can reuse the @TestBean discovery without driving that extension's own lifecycle. See the new Whole-Microservice Integration Tests (@MicroserviceTest) topic page.

Juneau now publishes a Bill of Materials and a small set of curated dependency bundles so consumers can depend on a coherent, version-aligned slice of the framework without hand-maintaining <version> tags — while keeping Juneau's explicit-over-magic configuration model (no Spring-style classpath auto-configuration). org.apache.juneau:juneau-bom (packaging pom) — import it (scope=import, type=pom) and drop explicit versions from your Juneau dependencies. Enumerates the consumer-facing Juneau modules plus the small set of starter-relevant third-party versions the bundles need (micrometer-core, opentelemetry-api, jakarta.servlet-api, jakarta.validation-api). It is not a whole-world third-party BOM, so it won't collide with a third-party BOM you import yourself. Three deployment-shape bundles (packaging pom) — depend on one and transitively pull a coherent module set plus juneau-rest-client: juneau-microservice-jetty-bundle juneau-microservice-tomcat-bundle juneau-springboot-bundle <dependencyManagement> <dependencies> <dependency> <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId> <artifactId>juneau-bom</artifactId> <version>10.0.0</version> <type>pom</type> <scope>import</scope> </dependency> </dependencies> </dependencyManagement> The bundles are dependency aggregators only — they register no configurations and perform no classpath auto-discovery. Configuration registration stays explicit via Microservice.Builder.configurations(Class<?>...). This is a deliberate design choice: per the maintainer, "I actually see auto-configuration as a weakness in Spring Boot that leads to applications with long startup times and impossible-to-understand architectures." These bundles are also distinct from the clone-and-go juneau-microservice-*-starter templates, which live as true-orphan branches of apache/juneau (microservice-jetty-starter, microservice-tomcat-starter, microservice-springboot-starter). Clone with git clone -b microservice-jetty-starter --single-branch https://github.com/apache/juneau.git my-app (replace the branch name for the other two). See Starter Projects. A reactor-consistency guard (scripts/check-bom-completeness.py, wired into the push gate) fails the build if a published module is missing from the BOM, so the enumeration can't silently drift. The binary distribution now also bundles juneau-microservice-tomcat (previously omitted). See the new Dependency Management (BOM & Bundles) topic page for usage and the full explicit-over-magic rationale.

A feasibility assessment of GraalVM native-image support for Juneau's reflection-heavy marshalling/bean core landed a CONDITIONAL GO verdict: all reflection is funnelled through one wrapper layer (org.apache.juneau.commons.reflect.*, single setAccessible() choke point) with no Unsafe/MethodHandle/bytecode generation, and the BeanContext/ClassMeta model already computes the exact member set reachability metadata needs — making a Juneau-authored metadata emitter realistic. The maintainer-approved follow-on (a BeanContext-driven reachability-metadata.json emitter targeting the juneau-marshall core first, REST server deferred) is tracked as a dedicated committed work item; native-image builds of Juneau are not yet supported. The new topic page also documents Docker image-layering guidance for Juneau apps. See GraalVM Native Image & Docker Layering.
documents.s: GraalVM native-image feasibility verdict + Docker layering guidance

documents.t: Three new modules under a top-level juneau-petstore/ aggregator together form the canonical Juneau petstore showcase application. The legacy juneau-examples-rest{,-jetty,-springboot,-jetty-ftest} family of modules has been retired in this release in favor of the petstore family — see the Breaking Changes section below.

Shared, deployment-agnostic surface consumed verbatim by both the Jetty and Spring Boot deployments. Owns: Domain beans — Pet, Order, User (plus Species/PetStatus/OrderStatus/UserStatus enums) under org.apache.juneau.petstore.dto. Plain Juneau beans, no JPA/Hibernate/Derby. In-memory PetStore service — ConcurrentHashMap-backed, lazy-loads classpath seed JSON at petstore/init/{Pets,Orders,Users}.json via Json5Parser. Auto-IDs via AtomicLong. PetStoreResource — full CRUD @Rest servlet (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE over /pets, /orders, /users). Uses org.apache.juneau.http.response.NotFound (next-gen) and @org.apache.juneau.http.Path/@Content. Spring-agnostic — extends BasicRestServlet so both deployments mount it identically. View-engine demos — the Mustache and Freemarker subtabs of the console's rendering-flavors page (/console/dev/flavors/mustache, /console/dev/flavors/freemarker) demonstrate the typed-View return path through the juneau-rest-server-view-{mustache,freemarker} bridges. Pure-classpath engines so both deployments inherit view rendering at parity. (They replace the retired PetMustacheViewResource / PetFreemarkerViewResource.) No-build React SPA demo — PetstoreUiResource mounts StaticFilesMixin to serve htdocs/petstore-ui.html, a single-page React UI that calls /petstore/pets over fetch(). Demonstrates the headless-JSON + decoupled-SPA pattern alongside the server-rendered HTML-doc UI; no Node/npm in the build and no network access needed (React and ReactDOM 18.3.1 are vendored under htdocs/vendor/, MIT-licensed, acknowledged in the root LICENSE; the app uses plain React.createElement, so there is no in-browser JSX compiler). Secure demo + StubBearerTokenValidator — the console's bearer-token demo page (/console/dev/secure, with SecureApiRest) replaces the retired PetSecureResource (/petstore-secure/*); the auth-gated CRUD subset is gated by a BearerTokenGuard (fail-closed, op-level) backed by the in-memory stub validator. Demonstrates the bearer-token + @Auth Principal pattern; resource-Javadoc cross-references AuthFilterChain for multi-mechanism deployments.

Jetty/Microservice deployment glue: App.main calls Microservice.create().configurations(JettyConfiguration.class, AppConfig.class).... RootResources extends BasicRestServletGroup — mounts every core child resource plus the Jetty-only Microservice admin trio (ConfigResource/LogsResource/ShutdownResource), sourced from the new juneau-microservice-examples module (see Breaking Changes below). Bundled jetty.xml and juneau-petstore-jetty.cfg. Starter-zip assembly — sources + cfg + jetty.xml for IDE-import use. In-module integration tests (@JettyMicroserviceTest, ephemeral port). Default URL: http://localhost:10000. Launcher: python3 scripts/start-petstore-jetty.py.

Spring Boot deployment glue: App is a @SpringBootApplication with @Bean RootResources + @Bean ServletRegistrationBean<Servlet> mounted at /*. RootResources extends BasicSpringRestServletGroup so child resources resolve as Spring beans (required for HelloResource's @Autowired HelloMessageProvider injection demo). Inherits ${spring.version} from the repo parent. application.properties configures port 5000. spring-boot-maven-plugin repackage produces a runnable fat jar. @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment=RANDOM_PORT) integration tests. Default URL: http://localhost:5000. Launcher: python3 scripts/start-petstore-springboot.py.

The core-hosted surface (CRUD, console, view demos, React SPA demo, auth-gated subset) is identical across both deployments by construction — it's shared code, not parallel copies. The deployment-specific surface (Jetty's microservice console + admin resources vs Spring Boot's @Autowired injection demo) is intentionally non-parity and documented as such.

The petstore now ships a complete admin console at /console, built on console-ui and offered as the worked example for the framework pages. See juneau-petstore. Fourteen pages (P1-P14). Each page has an FTL template and a Java builder twin (?builder), so the same page is shown both ways. Server-mode tables driven by BeanQuery: filter, sort and page the pets, orders and users on the server. Staged pet edits with the pending-changes badge (the photo field is excluded from staging). Restock async job with a job-log card that follows the job as it runs. Audit trail of console writes. Custom cards. Petstore: kpi and inventory-gauge custom cards on /console/dev/cards demonstrate adopter card types. Four rendering flavors (Builder, Html, Mustache and Freemarker) of the same pet list under /console/dev/flavors. Bearer-token demo at /console/dev/secure, next to a CSRF boundary on /console/* in both deployments. Tests. A Playwright browser harness exercises the pages, and FailLoud negative fixtures pin the error messages for mis-built pages. Retired legacy resources. PetInfoResource, PetHtmlResource, PetSecureResource, PetMustacheViewResource and PetFreemarkerViewResource (and their /petstore-info, /petstore-html, /petstore-secure and /pet-views URLs) are gone, replaced by console pages. This is a breaking change for users of the sample only; the petstore is a sample, so it is not listed under Breaking Changes below.

The retired juneau-examples-rest family (see Breaking Changes below) carried six REST-servlet demonstrations that hadn't yet been ported into petstore or consciously dropped. That gap is now closed — three demos got petstore-flavored equivalents, and three were consciously dropped: Ported to juneau-petstore-core, wired into both the Jetty and Spring Boot deployments: AboutRest (/console/about, replacing the retired PetInfoResource at /petstore-info) — utility-beans demo: BeanDescription/Hyperlink/SeeOtherRoot rendered against the petstore's own Pet domain bean. HtmlFlavorRest (/console/dev/flavors/html, replacing the retired PetHtmlResource at /petstore-html) — HTML5 bean-builder demo: a hand-built HTML5 Table fragment of all pets rendered from live petstore data. GET/PUT /petstore/pets/{id}/photo (added to PetStoreResource) — image upload/serve demo, backed by new petstore-local PetPhotoSerializer/PetPhotoParser classes (org.apache.juneau.petstore.marshall) and wired to the previously-unused Pet.photo field. Consciously dropped (not ported): ATOM-feed DTO serialization demo — generic marshalling showcase with no petstore-domain tie-in; Atom (de)serialization itself remains exhaustively covered by juneau-bean-atom's own test suite and docs. JSON-Schema DTO serialization demo — same shape as the Atom case; JSON-Schema generation is already exhaustively covered by juneau-bean-jsonschema's test suite and docs. Server-Sent-Events demo — SSE transport mechanics are already integration-tested independent of any demo resource; a petstore-flavored SSE feature (e.g. live status updates) would be net-new feature work, out of scope for a port-or-drop cleanup. The plan's remaining stretch scope — a @Remote typed-client demo and a Config API + SVL var-resolver showcase — was split out to a separate follow-on work item rather than folded in here.

org.apache.juneau.http.BeanQueryRequest is a stock @Request class (a concrete BeanQuery subclass) that binds the usual list-fetch query parameters as a single method argument and feeds a BeanQuery session directly: private static final InMemoryBeanQueryContext<Row> ROWS = InMemoryBeanQueryContext.create(Row.class).build(); @RestGet public List<Row> getList(BeanQueryRequest q) { try (var s = ROWS.getSession(rows)) { return s.find(q).rows(); } } Each getter binds one single-valued @Query whose wire name equals the property name: search, view (a column projection), sort, position, limit and opts (renamed from opt). The $-language and the key=value opts bag live inside those single strings and are decoded by the session, not on the wire. Each getter carries a @Schema description, so an operation taking a BeanQueryRequest documents all six parameters in Swagger automatically (position also declares minimum: 0). A malformed query is reported as HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error header and, with problem details on, a "code" member in the body; see Queryable rebuilt on the BeanQuery engine below. The @Request bean's constructor and setters are now verified when the operation table is built (see the Breaking Changes entry on request beans). Apps add extras by subclassing BeanQueryRequest and redeclaring a getter with its own @Query name (e.g. @Query("v") getView()). Saved-view CRUD endpoints must not take BeanQueryRequest (view there is a saved-view id, not a column projection). See the BeanQuery Package topic page. @Request getters now honor collectionFormat=multi (getAll, not last-wins) and @Query(def=) / equivalent def= on the other part annotations, including Optional<T> returns.

Juneau can now emit Content-Security-Policy response headers for the HTML it serves, including dynamic per-request nonce support. New in this release: A first-class immutable ContentSecurityPolicy HTTP header bean + fluent builder in juneau-rest-common (org.apache.juneau.http.header), with typed directive setters (defaultSrc, scriptSrc, styleSrc, imgSrc, connectSrc, fontSrc, objectSrc, baseUri, frameAncestors, reportUri/reportTo), a generic directive(name, sources...) escape hatch, source-expression helpers, report-only mode, and a ready-made nonce-based "strict starter" preset. Per-response SecureRandom nonce generation: the same nonce is injected into the emitted Content-Security-Policy header and stamped onto every inline <script>/<style> Juneau emits — the HtmlDoc template, the Swagger UI, the OpenAPI UI, and menu-item widgets. Opt-in by design: turning CSP on is a deliberate, one-line choice; existing apps are unaffected by default. See the new Content Security Policy topic page for details. This feature was inspired by an earlier proposal from Gary Gregory (@garydgregory, PR #57); the implementation shipped here is a fresh one built against the current 10.0 APIs.

LoopbackBoundary protects an app only when every request arrives under one pinned Host over plain HTTP. A new CsrfBoundary in org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter covers everything else: an app reached under a real host name, over HTTPS, behind a proxy, or under more than one name. Same-origin check with nothing pinned. On an unsafe request, Origin (with Sec-Fetch-Site as a fallback) must match the request's own scheme, host and port. A literal null origin is refused. Default ports are equated, and IPv6 literals are compared in bracketed form exactly as sent. Header token. A browser request must also carry a per-session synchronizer token in a request header (X-Csrf-Token by default). HTML form posts cannot send a header, so they are unsupported by design. Non-browser clients. A request with neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site is admitted without a token only when a browser could not have sent it cross-site without a preflight (for client authors: send JSON, or send Origin plus the token). NonBrowser.REJECT and NonBrowser.REQUIRE_TOKEN tighten that. Proxies. OriginSource.HOST_HEADER (the default) never reads X-Forwarded-*; OriginSource.CONTAINER takes the origin from the container's own forwarded-header support (Jetty ForwardedRequestCustomizer, Tomcat RemoteIpValve, Spring Boot forward-headers-strategy). DNS rebinding. allowedHosts(...) refuses any request, safe ones included, whose host is not listed. Applied by RequestBoundaryFilter, which works with either boundary. Register it at /* for REQUEST dispatches. The microservice admin samples. AdminBoundary in juneau-microservice-examples registers a CsrfBoundary over ConfigResource, LogsResource and ShutdownResource, answering loopback host names only unless others are given, and the Jetty petstore installs it. See the microservice examples entry below. Bus WebSocket handshakes. BusPolicy.boundary(...) now accepts a CsrfBoundary. A missing, null or malformed Origin is refused with HTTP 403 before the upgrade; a well-formed cross-site or mismatched Origin is refused after the upgrade with close code 4403, before any frame is sent or any bus session is touched. The handshake has no server name, so it judges the raw Host header (over HTTP/2, the request URI's authority) plus the request URI scheme, whatever OriginSource is set. Behind a proxy that rewrites Host with no container-side host rewriting, same-origin upgrades are refused; preserve Host at the proxy. BusWebSockets.register refuses any boundary type other than LoopbackBoundary and CsrfBoundary. Verified on Jetty and Tomcat; on Tomcat, RemoteIpValve forwards the scheme to the handshake but not the Host header, so a forwarded host is refused even with the valve's hostHeader set. Opt-in trusted forwarded origin. CsrfBoundary.Builder.trustedForwarding(X_FORWARDED | FORWARDED) and trustedHops(n) let a boundary judge HTTP writes and bus WebSocket handshakes against the host and protocol a proxy you operate forwards, for deployments whose container does no forwarded-host handling. Off by default with no behavior change. Host and protocol are both required, the nth entry from the right is used, the forwarded origin replaces the container's rather than adding to it, and anything missing, malformed or in disagreement with the container is refused (seven new BoundaryReason values, HTTP 403; handshakes close with 4403). X-Forwarded-Port is never read. Proxy allow-list for the forwarded origin. CsrfBoundary.Builder.trustedProxies(cidrs...) believes the forwarded header only from listed peer addresses (IPv4 and IPv6 ranges, validated at build; host bits are masked). Others carrying it are refused (FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED); others without it are judged as if forwarding were off. Off by default. HTTP where the container reports the TCP peer; WebSocket handshakes on Jetty; on Tomcat a forwarded handshake is refused while the list is set. Behavior changes in the same work: HTTP/2 requests with no Host header are judged on the container's :authority view. CsrfBoundary no longer refuses them with HOST_MISSING, and LoopbackBoundary no longer refuses them with HOST_MISMATCH. Bus WebSocket handshakes over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441 extended CONNECT, which Jetty enables by default with HTTP/2) are judged on their :authority instead of closing with 4403. Under HOST_HEADER, HTTP/2 requests are judged on the container's server name, which container forwarding support may rewrite. HTTP/1.x requests without Host are unchanged. LoopbackBoundary judges the effective method. A GET carrying ?method=DELETE or an X-HTTP-Method-Override header now takes the write checks, even when the resource it reaches would not honor the override (it now does honor it where allowedMethodHeaders is set; see the next bullet). Method overrides: all four headers honored, conflicts refused. X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-HTTP-Method and X-Method-Override are now honored under @Rest(allowedMethodHeaders) (and the global J_ALLOWED_METHOD_HEADERS), exactly as X-Method is; the setting is still empty by default, so applications that have not set it see no change. A request whose enabled override channels disagree (two different methods across ?method= and the headers, or repeated different values on one of them) is answered 400; identical repeats are fine. The method query parameter is now matched case-insensitively (?METHOD=PUT works) and read from the query string only, so a form-body method= field is no longer honored. The MCP bearer gate treats a POST claim on any of these channels as a POST. BREAKING: method overrides on safe requests are restricted. A GET, HEAD, OPTIONS or TRACE request may now be overridden (through ?method= or any of the four override headers) only to a safe method (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) or to a custom method whose operation is declared @RestOp(read=true). An override to any other method, for example GET ?method=DELETE, GET ?method=POST on an RRPC operation, or GET ?method=FOO reaching a method="*" operation, is refused with 405 Method Not Allowed and an Allow header, instead of being dispatched. Overrides on POST (for example POST ?method=PATCH for clients without PATCH) are unchanged. Defaults are unaffected: allowedMethodParams still defaults to HEAD,OPTIONS. Migration: mark read-only custom verbs @RestOp(read=true); change links that used ?method= to trigger a write into a POST (a form or a script), or call the method directly (curl -X DELETE); prefer path-based read links (/view/{file}) over ?method=VIEW, because a CSRF boundary still treats any custom-verb claim as a write. read=true on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/CONNECT, *, RRPC, or together with @Mutating fails at startup. An MCP server mounted as a mixin now answers an unauthenticated GET ?method=POST with 405 rather than 401. Every framework 405 now carries an Allow header, including the existing one for a path that matches under another method. Rejections and token-bearing pages are no-store. A rejected request is answered with Cache-Control: no-store.
