Code that stamps a token into a response (ViewTable.CSRF_ATTR, RegionTable.of(region, csrfToken), PageSpec.csrf(...)) must call RequestBoundaryFilter.markTokenBearing(response), which sets Cache-Control: private, no-store. No token in a committed response. A token is never embedded into a response that is already committed, including csrf attributes an author put on the page's body element. The page's writes then fail visibly. Breaking (unreleased API): the nested LoopbackBoundary.Reason and LoopbackBoundary.Result types are now the top-level BoundaryReason and BoundaryResult, with no aliases. Code built against a 10.0.0 snapshot needs the new names. Breaking (unreleased API): the rejection header is now X-Request-Boundary (it was X-Loopback-Boundary). See REST Security and the Views Security Model.
documents.s: CSRF protection for apps that are not on loopback (CsrfBoundary)

documents.t: Juneau 10.0 adds a coherent, discoverable Actuator-style management surface while keeping Juneau's a-la-carte composability. Every endpoint ships in two independently-mountable flavors — a composable *Mixin and a routed *Resource sharing one worker — and a convenience BasicActuatorGroup assembles them under one configurable path prefix (default /actuator, overridable via the juneau.actuator.path system property). New endpoints: /info (juneau-microservice, org.apache.juneau.microservice.management) — renders the running application's ManifestFile main attributes (build/version/git metadata). Degrades to {} when no manifest is registered. Build-time git/version stamping goes in the consumer's application-jar build (a git-commit-id + maven-jar-plugin recipe is in the topic page). /loggers (juneau-rest-server, org.apache.juneau.rest.server.management) — read all logger levels and (deny-by-default) set a level at runtime. Drives java.util.logging by default; Logback / Log4j2 backends are an explicit opt-in (see the dedicated entry below). /metrics (juneau-rest-server-metrics-micrometer) — renders a Prometheus scrape from a consumer-provided Micrometer MeterRegistry resolved from the bean store; degrades to 501 when no scrapeable registry is present. Never auto-registers a default registry. /threaddump + /heapdump (juneau-rest-server) — server-agnostic ThreadMXBean thread dump and HotSpot .hprof heap dump, both deny-by-default on security grounds (opt in via DumpsSettings). Exposure is on-by-default-with-gating: non-sensitive reads are exposed; mutating/sensitive operations (/loggers set-level, the dumps) are deny-by-default behind explicit opt-in settings beans (LoggersSettings, DumpsSettings). No auth provider is auto-wired — the consumer supplies their own guard. BasicActuatorGroup mounts only /healthz//readyz//livez and the dumps by default; /info and /loggers are off. The convenience group composes HealthMixin + DumpsMixin only — InfoMixin and LoggersMixin are deliberately left out, since an unauthenticated manifest dump (/info) and logger-topology disclosure (/loggers read) are both meaningful information leaks with no guard auto-wired. Re-enable either (or both) with an a-la-carte subclass adding @Rest(mixins={InfoMixin.class, LoggersMixin.class}) (additive to the inherited mixins). Applications that mount InfoMixin/LoggersMixin directly (not through BasicActuatorGroup) are unaffected. See the new Management Surface topic page for the endpoint catalog, the BasicActuatorGroup one-liner, the exposure policy, and the manifest-stamping recipe.

The /loggers endpoint (above) now drives a pluggable LogBackend instead of being hardwired to java.util.logging. juneau-rest-server still ships only the JUL backend (JulLogBackend, the default) so the core stays dependency-free, and a new opt-in juneau-rest-server-management-logging module adds LogbackLogBackend + Log4j2LogBackend (the backends declared provided, so they never leak transitively). Explicit selection (no classpath auto-detection, per the explicit-over-magic principle): declare the backend on the existing settings bean — LoggersSettings.create().backend(new LogbackLogBackend()).build(). Identical response shape across backends: read reports the configured level (empty string = inherited from an ancestor; ROOT key for the root logger); set is process-lifetime-only (no config-file rewrite). Level names are backend-native; an invalid name fails 400. Drives the concrete backend, not the SLF4J facade: LogbackLogBackend for SLF4J→Logback, Log4j2LogBackend for Log4j2; an slf4j-jdk14 binding is JUL, so the default backend already covers it. Custom backends implement LogBackend directly. This closes the 174b JUL-only /loggers limitation. See the extended Management Surface topic page.

@Rest(mixins=...) lets a mixin class declare its own @Rest settings that apply only to its endpoints — but the composition decision often belongs to the host. New in 10.0.0, the @Rest(mixinDefs=@Mixin(...)) attribute lets a host declare a mixin and override selected @Rest-level settings for that mixin's endpoints, in one place, without editing or subclassing the mixin: @Rest(mixinDefs=@Mixin(type=AdminResource.class, guards=AdminGuard.class)) public class ApiResource extends BasicRestServlet { ... } Additive / non-breaking. mixinDefs coexists with the existing mixins=Class<?>[]; a @Mixin(type=X.class) with no overrides is exactly equivalent to a bare mixins=X.class entry, and existing usages are untouched. Override slots mirror the composition-shaped @Rest attributes: guards, roleGuard/rolesDeclared, converters, encoders, serializers/parsers, responseProcessors, restOpArgs, partSerializer/partParser, messages, the default request/response headers + attributes, produces/consumes/defaultAccept/defaultContentType/defaultCharset, and maxInput. Precedence: the host override layers on top of the inherited host chain (list-shaped props append, replace-shaped props win) and wins over the mixin class's own declaration. @Mixin carries its own noInherit (unioned with the mixin class's @Rest(noInherit=...)) so the host override is authoritative but overridable by noInherit. Host-chosen re-mount: @Mixin(path=...)/paths={...} re-mount the mixin's endpoints under host-chosen prefix(es), reusing the existing pathToken normalization. Transitive mixins are overridden only when separately named. Internally this also normalized mixin discovery (one ResolvedMixin carrier for both bare and rich forms) and replaced the RestContext.Args boolean mixinContext flag with a typed ContextKind discriminator (Root/Child/Mixin). See Host-side overrides with @Mixin.

By default a mixin's responseProcessors apply only to the mixin's own endpoints — a host's own @RestOp methods see only the host's chain. The host-side @Mixin(mergeIntoHost=true) directive can fold all of a mixin's list-shaped attributes into the host, but it must be spelled out at every use-site. New in 10.0.0, a mixin class can declare @Rest(mergeResponseProcessorsIntoHost=true) on itself, so that a plain @Rest(mixins=ThatMixin.class) reference automatically folds only the mixin's responseProcessors into the host's own chain: @Rest(responseProcessors=FreemarkerViewRenderer.class, mergeResponseProcessorsIntoHost=true) public class FreemarkerMixin { ... } Opt-in and non-silent. Defaults to false; only a mixin that declares it changes behavior. Mixins that don't keep today's isolated scoping exactly — no change to the default for arbitrary existing mixins. Response-processor-scoped. Folds only responseProcessors — never guards, serializers, or any other list-shaped attribute (the narrower, mixin-declared counterpart to the host-side, fold-everything @Mixin(mergeIntoHost=true)). Same-class de-duplication applies. View mixins opt in. All four view-renderer mixins — FreemarkerMixin, JspMixin, MustacheMixin, ThymeleafMixin — now declare it, so a bare @Rest(mixins=FreemarkerMixin.class) (etc.) renders the host's own View returns through the engine with no mergeIntoHost or explicit responseProcessors= ceremony. See REST Server — Mixin Sub-Contexts and FreeMarker View Support.

Children are deliberately isolated from the host's resolution chain — a child's serializers, parsers, guards, part serializer, etc. resolve against its own RestContext only, never inherited from the parent. New in 10.0.0, the @Rest(childrenDefs=@Child(...)) attribute lets a host seed a curated set of settings onto a routed child's otherwise-isolated context, without editing the child class — the child-resource analog of the @Rest(mixinDefs=@Mixin(...)) attribute above: @Rest(childrenDefs=@Child(type=AdminResource.class, partSerializer=AdminPartSerializer.class, guards=AdminBearerGuard.class)) public class ApiResource extends BasicRestServlet { ... } Additive / non-breaking. childrenDefs coexists with the existing children=Class<?>[]; a @Child(type=X.class) with no seed members is exactly equivalent to a bare children=X.class entry, and if both name the same class the rich entry wins (the bare entry is upgraded in place). Two seed-semantics buckets — since children are isolated by design, a seed can't "override" an inherited chain the way a @Mixin override does; it can only add to or fill gaps in the child's own config: additive-security (guards, converters, roleGuard, rolesDeclared) — the host's contribution is added alongside the child's own (list-shaped members prepend; the two role-based members AND-stack) and can never be removed or weakened by the child; child-wins scalars (partSerializer, partParser, defaultCharset, maxInput) — the seed is a fallback that applies only when the child leaves the property unset, and the child's own explicit @Rest declaration always wins. noInherit cuts the seed too. A child's own @Rest(noInherit="<property>") suppresses the corresponding host-seeded value, for either bucket, so the child always stays in full control of its own configuration. Survives lazy materialization — a seed applies to a @Rest(lazyChildren="true") child on first request exactly as it would to an eagerly-built one. Not (yet) seedable: defaultAccept/defaultContentType were originally planned but dropped before shipping — they resolve through a shared first-wins mechanism that would make the seed win over the child's own value, the opposite of every other child-wins scalar's contract. See Host-side seeding with @Child and REST Server — Children vs Mixins.

@Rest(children=...) child resources now see the @Bean methods and non-null @Bean fields declared on their parent (the "group"), instead of only the parent's bootstrap bean store. Each RestContext now has an inheritable bean store — its own @Bean results layered over its bootstrap store — and that store is used as the parent/bootstrap store of every child. @Rest(children={PetResource.class, OrderResource.class}) public class RootResources extends BasicRestServletGroup { // One store shared by every child resource. @Bean public PetStore petStore() { return new PetStore(); } } New API: RestContext.getInheritableBeanStore() returns the store a resource exposes to its children. Transitive. Each child's inheritable store sits on top of its parent's, so a grandchild sees the beans of its parent, its grandparent, and so on up to the root (including any Spring context bridged in at the root). Child wins. A child's own @Bean of the same type and name takes precedence over the inherited one. Framework-managed beans stay per-context. Serializers, parsers, the call logger, RestChildren and similar are not exported; each child still builds its own from its own @Rest configuration. Beans flow down only. A child's beans are never visible to its parent or siblings.
documents.s: Child resources inherit their parent's @Bean group beans

documents.t: Juneau 10.0 extends its request-boundary observability to cover custom (non-request) observations, ships a single OTLP export bundle, and adds OpenTelemetry trace-id log correlation — all keeping the explicit-over-magic, off-by-default contract (no classpath auto-configuration). Custom-observation API (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.observation): a new explicit programmatic API — Observations.observe(name, tags) (try-with-resources Observation handle), an Observer that composes the existing SPIs, and non-request default methods on the two SPIs (MetricsRecorder.record(name, tags, elapsed, error) + TracerHook.startSpan(name)). Instruments an arbitrary block of work with a timer + span; reuses the exact request-path metricName/metricTags model. No @Observed annotation — Juneau has no AOP/method-interception substrate, so observation is an explicit block (consistent with the explicit-over-magic philosophy). No-backend path is zero-allocation. The Micrometer + OTel bridges override both default methods (OTel opens an INTERNAL-kind span, nested under any active request span). juneau-observability-otlp-bundle: a curated dependency bundle (under juneau-bundles) that pulls both Juneau observability bridges plus a version-aligned OTLP exporter stack — opentelemetry-exporter-otlp (+ SDK + autoconfigure) for traces and micrometer-registry-otlp for metrics — in one dependency. Metrics + traces for v1 (OTLP logs export deferred). A dependency aggregator only; you still wire the @Bean MetricsRecorder/@Bean TracerHook explicitly. Log correlation: the JUL LogEntryFormatter gains optional {traceId}/{spanId} placeholders, sourced reflectively from the active OTel Span.current() (no hard OTel dependency — they render empty when OTel is absent). MdcAsyncListener additionally folds the active trace/span id into the propagated SLF4J MDC snapshot (keys trace_id/span_id) so correlation survives the async-completion hop, gated by isMdcAsyncPropagation() and kept reflective. SLF4J→Logback/Log4j2 apps wire their own MDC pattern (JUL-only is a documented v1 limitation). This also fixed a latent multi-digit format-group bug in the LogEntryFormatter regex builder. See the extended Observability — Micrometer + OpenTelemetry topic page.
documents.s: Custom observations + one-dependency OTLP export + log correlation

documents.t: Juneau 10.0 adds a RestAuthenticator SPI (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.auth) — an ergonomic, in-resource way to resolve a request's Principal + roles so roleGuard, RoleBasedRestGuard, @Auth Principal, and req.isUserInRole(...) all work with no container-managed security and no servlet-layer filter. It complements the AuthN Filter Framework and reuses the same underlying auth implementations. Shared Authenticator contract — a new Authenticator functional interface (Optional<AuthResult> authenticate(HttpServletRequest)) is now implemented by both AuthFilter and AuthFilterChain, so every existing filter (SAML / OAuth / JWT / API-key / bearer) is reusable verbatim at the resource layer. RestAuthenticator.of(Authenticator) adapts any of them. AuthResult merge modes — AuthResult gains an immutable merge mode: of(...) = ADD (union roles, principal required — unchanged), ofRoles(...) = roles-only ADD (null principal — keeps the inherited identity), replacing(...) = REPLACE (swap identity outright). The existing of(...) factories and behavior are preserved (backward compatible). Registration & DI — resolved per RestContext with precedence registered bean › @Bean method › @Rest(authenticator=...) › RestServlet.createAuthenticator(BeanStore). Both Authenticator-into-RestAuthenticator and RestAuthenticator-into-resource injection work through the bean store. Inheritance & folding — unlike guards, authenticators inherit down the child-resource tree: a single root authenticator covers all descendants, which may augment (add roles), replace (swap identity), or opt out with @Rest(noInherit={"authenticator"}). @Rest(children = { ChildResource.class }) public class RootResource extends BasicRestServlet { @Bean public RestAuthenticator authenticator(AuthFilterChain chain) { return RestAuthenticator.of(chain); // covers root + all descendants } } See the new REST Authenticator — Resource-Level Authentication topic page.

Juneau 10.0 replaces Queryable's hand-rolled search/view/sort/paging code (ObjectSearcher/ObjectSorter/ObjectViewer/ObjectPaginator) with the shared BeanQuery engine, so one search language, one set of limits and one error model cover REST responses, DataTables server-side processing and SQL-backed queries. A new opt-in module also ships a DataTables server-side processing adapter plus browser-side helpers. Queryable on BeanQuery — the search / view / sort / position / limit / opts request parameters (bound by BeanQueryRequest) run against an InMemoryBeanQueryContext built from the response's row type (one context per element class, cached for the life of the converter; Map rows get a per-request context). Example: GET /people?search=age=$gte(18)&sort=name,age:desc&view=name,age&position=20&limit=10. Non-tabular results are returned unchanged. QueryableSettings — a bean-store-resolved per-resource bean (mirroring IntrospectableSettings) that tunes the context: defaultLimit (100), maxLimit (1000), allowRegex (on by default, allowRegex(false) opts out), regexTimeout, countPolicy, and the search-clause / sort-key / search-length / expression-depth caps. Unset settings keep the BeanQuery builder defaults. Counts — ?opts=counts=true adds X-BeanQuery-Total and X-BeanQuery-Matched response headers (each only when that count was computed). The body stays a bare list. Central error mapping — RestContext.convertThrowable maps BeanQuerySyntaxException to HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error: <CODE> header (BeanQueryRequest.ERROR_HEADER) and, with problem details on, a "code" member in the body; BeanQueryExecutionException maps to HTTP 500 with the fixed body Query execution failed. (the cause is logged, never sent to the client). The DataTables adapter uses the same contract (next bullet). juneau-rest-server-datatables module (org.apache.juneau:juneau-rest-server-datatables) — a new opt-in add-on (not bundled in juneau-distrib, mirroring the juneau-rest-server-management-logging precedent) with: DataTablesQuery (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.datatables.adapter) — maps the DataTables server-side contract onto BeanQuery: DataTablesQuery.toBeanQuery(req, ctx) builds a BeanQuery from a DataTablesRequest (per-column search, order, paging, and a global search that expands to an $or of a per-SearchType leaf — $contains/$prefix/$eqic/$eq — over every searchable, resolvable column, not just text), and DataTablesQuery.run/runArrays execute it and map the result onto the DataTables envelope. The browser posts the draw state as JSON (not DataTables' default form-encoded request) through a new JuneauDataTables.ajax(url, extra?) helper in juneau-datatables.js, or the data-juneau-datatable-ajax auto-init attribute. A malformed request (unknown column, a maxSearchClauses/maxSortKeys cap exceeded, a bad search expression) raises BeanQuerySyntaxException, which the adapter does not catch: the central mapping answers HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error: <CODE> header and the message in the body, exactly like any other Queryable endpoint. JuneauDataTables.ajax installs an xhr.dt listener that shows that server message through DataTables' normal error path (the error.dt event, then DataTable.ext.errMode) instead of a generic "Ajax error"; other failed requests keep the DataTables default. An execution failure is HTTP 500 via the central BeanQueryExecutionException mapping. See DataTables. Views runtime server-mode tables now ride the same wire format. A juneau-rest-server-views table with dataMode: "server" now gets serverSide: true and ajax: JuneauDataTables.ajax(url, {...}) (in juneau-views.js: buildOptions → buildServerAjax) instead of a hand-built GET config, so there is one wire format end to end. Breaking for existing server-mode endpoints: they must now be @RestPost methods taking @Content DataTablesRequest, not GET handlers reading query-string parameters. Column-scoped ribbon options now ride the JSON body as that column's search.value (ribbonColumnSearches), $and-merged with the user's own search on the same column (mergeColumnSearches) — fixing a bug where such filters were silently dropped. param:-scoped ribbon options (ribbonQueryParams) and the nested-table parent-scope param (applyNestedScope) stay URL query parameters, re-derived on every request through beforeSend. Client-mode tables are unchanged. A page must load juneau-datatables.js before juneau-views.js; otherwise server mode fails loudly (a warning) instead of silently falling back to GET. See DataTables. DataTablesResults<T> — the {draw,recordsTotal,recordsFiltered,data} (+ optional error) envelope bean, rendered by the negotiated serializer (no hardcoded JSON). Browser-side helpers — DataTablesColumns (generate columns:[…] from bean-property order + @Schema titles), DataTablesTable (build a DataTables-ready HTML5 Table DOM bean, with MarshallingContext overloads), and DataTablesMixin (serves a first-party juneau-datatables.js auto-init glue script). DataTables' own JS/CSS and jQuery remain caller-provided (not vendored — their license is not ASF category-A).
documents.s: Queryable rebuilt on the BeanQuery engine + juneau-rest-server-datatables (new module)

documents.t: Juneau 10.0 adds two opt-in modules that give an admin-console-style resource a themeable CSS "chrome", an enum status/domain pill component, and (for FreeMarker consumers) macro-based composition — without pulling a template engine or the DataTables add-on into juneau-rest-server core. The two modules form an acyclic dependency chain (console-ui → console-ui-freemarker); a chrome-only consumer never drags in FreeMarker or DataTables transitively. juneau-rest-server-console-ui — ConsoleChromeMixin serves a dynamically themed chrome.css (the module's shipped structural stylesheet plus a :root block built from validated --jc-* theme tokens); Theme validates every token value through a normalize-then-accept-known-safe pipeline (reject C0/C1/DEL control chars → strip CSS comments → case-insensitively reject any url( production → match an allowlist grammar for colors/fonts/lengths/gradients) rather than a denylist, so a token value can never smuggle a url()-based injection. Color/font/length tokens sink only into non-URL-capable CSS properties; the sole URL-capable sink (background-image, for --jc-page-bg/--jc-avatar-bg) is unreachable via url() anyway since the grammar structurally excludes that production. The console logo is a static chrome.css constant, not a configurable token. The reusable enum pill/badge component (<span class="tag <domain> <value>">) is rendered by the <@tag domain=... value=.../> FreeMarker macro in the console base.ftlh (see Admin Console Chrome). Console theming is FTL-only: custom palettes are authored with <@theme>/<@token> (value= for leaves, alias= for live var() references). ThemePack, ThemeSettings, ThemePackSettings, ConsoleChromeMixin.Builder.pack(...)/pageBackgroundImage(...) and the /juneau-console/assets/logo/page-bg endpoints were removed; ConsoleChromeMixin.create().theme("<stock-name>") selects a stock palette for the served chrome.css. Page Tabs and Page Subtabs — a Page Tab is 38.5px tall: a 3px accent border, 8px/10px padding, and 13px text at line-height 1.5. A Page Subtab is 30px tall. The selected Page Tab and the selected Page Subtab are bold. The box is themeable through --jc-nav-tab-padding-block, --jc-nav-tab-padding-inline, --jc-nav-tab-line-height, --jc-page-nav-child-padding-block and --jc-page-nav-child-padding-inline. <@console theme="<stock-name>"> still selects a built-in stock theme (an unknown name is rejected fail-closed); a nested <@theme name=> inside the directive overrides it. The juneau-rest-server-theme-packs module was removed. juneau-rest-server-console-ui-freemarker — ConsoleFreemarkerMixin extends FreemarkerMixin (register it typed as FreemarkerMixin, mirroring the load-bearing-return-type rule FreemarkerMixin beans already follow) augments the resolved Configuration's TemplateLoader with a second, classpath-root-rooted ClassTemplateLoader, without shadowing the consumer's own basePath-relative templates. This resolves the reserved org/apache/juneau/console/base.ftlh template (pulled in via a loader-root-absolute <#include "/org/apache/juneau/console/base.ftlh">) and its <@tag domain=... value=.../> macro — the trusted-HTML adapter for the pill component above. A consumer-supplied Configuration bean (Spring Boot autoconfig, etc.) is honored untouched, not augmented. DataTablesTable additive @Html(render=...) honoring (in the existing juneau-rest-server-datatables module) — DataTablesTable.of(MarshallingContext, String, Collection<?>, Class<?>) now resolves and applies each row property's @Html(render=...) the same way the ordinary HtmlSerializer/HtmlDocSerializer path already does, so a column whose bean property declares a custom @Html(render=...) (for example an enum rendered as a status pill) renders through it instead of as a raw enum name. This is not a purely-additive change: a bean already using @Html(render=...) for the existing serializer path now also renders through that same render when passed through this DataTablesTable overload, where it previously rendered the raw value. Map-based rows are unaffected (no BeanPropertyMeta to resolve a render from). juneau-rest-server-console-ui-freemarker — shareable-URL state and more datatables catalog keys. The views toolkit pack now includes juneau-urlstate.js (after juneau-pagestate.js), so the View Settings Copy link button and shareable-URL state work on <@page toolkit="views"> pages without loading the script by hand. <@card type="datatables"> catalogs now pass copyLink, rowActions, rowClassRules and pausePollingWhileEditing through onto the view, and selection and bulk through onto the slot; previously these keys were silently dropped on FTL-built pages. juneau-rest-server-views / TableSpec — urlState key and the day(YYYY-MM-DD) directive. A table view can now opt in to built-in shareable-URL directives with TableSpec.urlState(String...) (or urlState: {day: {}} in a catalog; the page schema validates it). day stores a calendar date in ?state= and passes it to the server as a day query parameter (rename it with TableSpec.urlStateDayParam(String param), emitted as urlState.day.param) so a resource can return that day's [start, end) window; malformed dates are ignored. Views without the key are unchanged. juneau-rest-server-console-ui-freemarker — open card-type registry. Unknown well-formed card types now pass through the server, and the JS shell fails them with E-JS-4. <@card> gains a src= attribute. A bare-URL datatables body is removed (it is now E-25), and searchType validation moves to render time (E-32). The bulk wire contract is "2" (aggregate mode, BulkResult). <@card type="datatables"> is the one table surface. QuickStat gains meter and segmented kinds. QuickStat.meter(id, label, value, max) paints a filled track with role="meter", and QuickStat.segmented(id, label).segment(...) paints a proportional bar with a text legend. Both require a non-blank label. The new statusTone(StatusTone) sets an item tone from the shared status palette; tone(QuickStat.Tone) is unchanged. Inline datatables catalogs refuse a malformed quickStats strip (E-37). This includes an off-palette tone on any item, plain tiles included. Such tones used to be dropped silently by the client. See the new Admin-Console Chrome topic page.
documents.s: Themeable admin-console chrome + FreeMarker macro composition (new modules: juneau-rest-server-console-ui, -console-ui-freemarker)

documents.t: <@console> pages now carry a versioned JSON page contract (#juneau-page, schema juneau-page.schema.json) and load one shell script, /juneau-console/juneau-console.js, which draws the header, nav (any depth, aria-current from activeNav or a segment-aware URL fallback), cards and footer. The server keeps rendering <head>. New: PageContractAssert (published test helper), ConsoleTemplateValidator (static template lint), ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder.devMode(boolean) (schema validation at render time), jcHasToolkit(name), <@footer text="…"/>, and window.JuneauConsole (contract, card, registerCard, mount, chrome, and the juneau:console-mounted event). Loud failures: template mistakes fail the render with E-1 to E-18; contract problems in the browser show a .jc-console-error banner (E-JS-1 to E-JS-12, then E-JS-14). Fix: a @Bean returning ConsoleFreemarkerMixin (rather than FreemarkerMixin) is now found; previously it silently fell back to the default mixin without the console directives. BREAKING (10.0 snapshots only): the page contract's top-level version key is renamed contractVersion, matching every other Juneau envelope contract (ModalDef, FormDef, BarSlot, ActionResult, RegionDef, the card/slot envelopes). The value is unchanged ("1"). There is no fallback: juneau-page.schema.json now requires contractVersion and forbids version, juneau-console.js reads only contractVersion (JuneauConsole.SUPPORTED_VERSIONS is now SUPPORTED_CONTRACT_VERSIONS), PageContractAssert.hasVersion(String) is renamed hasContractVersion(String), and assertPage(...) throws if a contract still carries version. Pages are generated by <@console>, so upgrading Juneau is the only step; code that hand-builds a page contract, or calls hasVersion, must be updated. Browsers that cached the previous juneau-console.js (served with a one-day max-age) show an E-JS-2 banner until the cache expires or the page is hard-reloaded. BREAKING: the FTL globals pageBody, pageTab, pageInit, pageCss, pageToolkit, pageToolkitCss, pageToolkitJs and pageThemeCss are removed (use jcHasToolkit("views")). The legacy chrome templates that did not use <@console> are removed; a <@page> whose chrome renders no <@console> is an error. The <@card> types js, json and calendar are removed (use type="html" with a body or a registered card type), as are the data-juneau-card-sidecar scripts (no directive emits them any more; the orphaned juneau-page-cards.js asset is deleted). juneau-chrome.js is absorbed into juneau-console.js. Server HTML no longer contains nav, header, footer or card wrappers; tests that matched that HTML must move to PageContractAssert.
documents.s: Console page contract and JS shell

documents.t: Console cards now declare the scripts and stylesheets they need, and <@page> loads each one once, in dependency order. See Card Asset Dependencies. New: ToolkitPack (packs with dependsOn and a VENDOR / RUNTIME kind), the built-in packs jquery, datatables, datatables-glue and datatables-buttons, <@card requires=...>, and ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder methods registerToolkitPack(ToolkitPack), cardRequires(type, packs...) and providedPacks(names...). build() fails on an unknown pack, a cycle, or a VENDOR pack depending on a RUNTIME pack. New: <@card class="..."> adds one or more CSS classes to the card's wrapper element, so a page can keep its own scope class on the card. Each name must be a plain CSS class token or the render fails. See Admin Console Chrome. New: WebJarsMixin and WebJarResolver in juneau-rest-server serve /webjars/* from the classpath. juneau-rest-server-datatables now depends on the jQuery and DataTables WebJars (DataTables 2.3.8, Buttons 3.2.6, jQuery 3.7.1). Changed: every <@card type="datatables"> loads jQuery, DataTables and juneau-datatables.js, in client and server mode. Previously the glue loaded only for server-mode cards and the page had to load jQuery and DataTables itself. A host with datatables cards composes WebJarsMixin as well as DataTablesMixin. BREAKING (10.0 snapshots only): juneau-datatables.js left the views pack. ToolkitPackRegistry.Resolved is split into vendorCss, vendorJs, runtimeCss and runtimeJs, and the resolve(names, req, boolean) overload is removed. A page that loads jQuery or DataTables through <@scripts phase="after-toolkit"> must drop those tags (they would load twice, after the glue). A copy loaded through init= or css= is skipped only when its file name matches the pack's; an app with its own copies should name the packs in providedPacks(...) or mount WebJarsMixin. Removed (10.0 snapshots only): APIs left unused once every consumer moved to card-declared packs. DataTablesMixin.JQUERY_CDN_URL, DATATABLES_JS_CDN_URL and DATATABLES_CSS_CDN_URL are gone; jQuery and DataTables now come from the WebJars. PageCapture.hasServerModeTable() is gone, because every datatables card now requires the datatables-glue pack. On ToolkitPackRegistry, the 2-arg resolve(names, req) and the register(name, cssPaths, jsPaths[, resolver]) overloads are gone; use resolve(names, req, pageUrls, template) and register(ToolkitPack). ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder.registerToolkitPack(name, cssPaths, jsPaths) and providedPacks(...) stay.

Juneau 10.0 replaces the multi-signal REST debug/logging system (@Rest(debug)/@Debug/DebugEnablement/ CallLogger) with a single, JUL-logger-level-driven mechanism. This is a hard break with no deprecation shim (unreleased 10.0 surface) — see the Breaking Changes section below and the V10 Migration Guide for the full removed-symbol mapping. One signal. A resource's own java.util.logging.Logger level is the sole control for request/response debug capture — no annotations, no per-request headers, no separate config keys. Verbosity is cumulative: INFO = basic, FINE = + headers, FINEST = + bodies (only when the body-dump gate is set — see the secure-by-default entry below), one LogRecord per request (stable emitted level: INFO). Per-operation granularity falls out of ordinary JUL parent-inheritance via a hierarchical child logger (resourceClass.getName() + "." + methodName) — elevate one method to FINEST without touching the rest. Off by default. Under stock JUL (nothing configured for the resource) no debug record is built or logged, so a running service no longer writes one line per request. The status line appears only when a level of INFO or finer is set explicitly on the resource's logger (or an enclosing logger such as its package), and FINE/FINEST add headers/bodies as before. The record is not constructed at all when it would not be emitted. Apps that relied on the per-request line appearing by default must now set the level, e.g. Logger.getLogger("com.acme.MyResource").setLevel(Level.INFO). Spring Boot propagation path. For real Logback backends, logging.level.* now propagates into JUL by default (juneau.rest.logging.propagate-levels=true), with an additive default posture (juneau.rest.logging.propagate-levels.reset-jul=false) and silent no-op fallback for non-Logback backends. New RestDebugFormatter SPI (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.logging) — a per-tier formatter interface (formatBasic/formatHeaders/formatBody) with a shipped BasicRestDebugFormatter default. It's the only public extension point; the two-phase capture pipeline underneath it is internal. Resolution precedence: resource-implements-the-interface > BeanStore-registered bean > BasicRestDebugFormatter. Secure by default (hardened). BasicRestDebugFormatter no longer dumps bodies just because a logger was raised to FINEST. See the dedicated secure-by-default entry below for the full contract. Bounded body buffering. Request/response body-caching wrappers are installed only when the resolved logger is loggable at FINEST, and buffer at most the configured cap rather than the entire stream — an improvement over the prior unbounded debug body caching. Completion-path emission for async/reactive responses. True asynchronous responses (CompletableFuture/CompletionStage) and reactive SSE/NDJSON streams now emit their single debug record on the response-completion path — after the async body and any completion-time headers have been written — instead of during the synchronous request finish. This fixes incomplete capture where an async record could be emitted before its late headers/body existed. A resolved logger/formatter/detail-tier snapshot is captured on the request thread at the async hand-off and carried across the completion hop; finish-time attributes such as Exec time are recorded on the completion path. Synchronous responses and the MockRestClient/non-async-container fallback are unchanged (still emitted during synchronous finish), and @RestEndCall still runs on the request thread. Exactly one INFO record is emitted per request on every path. Logger level controls verbosity only. REST-driven marshalling debug behavior and EchoMixin reachability are decoupled from the JUL level (see the dedicated entry below). RestRequest.isDebug() still exists, now derived and read-only (true when the resolved logger is FINE-or-finer), but the framework no longer keys any behavior off it. See the new Logging / Debugging topic page for the full model.

Two side effects that previously rode the JUL logger level are now controlled by their own explicit, non-logging switches — so raising a logger to FINE/FINEST changes verbosity only. This is an unreleased-10.0 hard break (no compatibility shim, no new echo annotation). EchoMixin is disabled by default. /echo/* now returns 404 Not Found regardless of logger level. Enable it explicitly: EchoMixin.create().enabled().build(). Enablement is tri-state — an explicit enabled(true)/ enabled(false) wins; when unset it resolves the ${juneau.echo.enabled:false} SVL fallback (system property / relaxed environment variable). Because that fallback is JVM-global, prefer per-host builder enablement and pair it with the host's inherited @Rest(guards=...) chain. This closes an accidental attack-surface expansion where raising a logger to FINE silently un-hid a request-reflecting endpoint. Marshalling debug behavior has a dedicated cascading setting. Serializer/parser debug behavior (richer/ stack-prefixed serialization exceptions and retained/quoted parse input in error messages) is now driven by debugMarshalling, a String on all eight REST annotation types (@Rest, @RestOp, and the six HTTP-method annotations) defaulting OFF at every level. Blank "" means inherit (op inherits resource, which resolves ${juneau.debugMarshalling:false}); query at runtime via RestRequest.isDebugMarshalling(). A serializer/parser configured with its own marshall-layer Context.debug remains independent — the REST layer never clobbers it. See Logging / Debugging and the Ops / Introspection Mixin Pack topic pages.
documents.s: Decoupled EchoMixin reachability and marshalling debug from log level

documents.t: BasicRestDebugFormatter is hardened so that raising a resource/operation logger to FINE/FINEST can never, by itself, leak plaintext credentials or hand a remote client a log-forging channel. This is an unreleased-10.0 hard break in the debug formatter's output — there is no compatibility shim. Two reusable primitives land in juneau-rest-common (a sanitize(...) log-forging escaper and the RestDebugBodyScrubber SPI); the formatter changes land in juneau-rest-server. No body dumps by default. Request/response bodies are never dumped unless an operator explicitly sets the JUNEAU_REST_DEBUG_ALLOW_DUMP_BODIES environment variable (environment-only, no system-property fallback, read once/cached, trim-then-parse truthy kill-switch semantics). With the gate unset, FINEST emits a suppression placeholder + byte count instead of body content. Even opted in, bodies render only at FINEST and only for renderable text content (via the new isBodyRenderable(String) predicate); non-renderable/binary content and non-identity Content-Encoding yield a distinct placeholder. RestDebugBodyScrubber SPI (org.apache.juneau.http) — an optional, gate-subordinate, fail-closed transform (String scrub(String contentType, String body), registered via bodyScrubber(...)) that chooses scrubbed-vs-raw body text once dumping is permitted; a throw or null result falls closed to a placeholder, never the raw body. All header values masked against a widened set. Every value of every credential-bearing header (not just the first) is masked with [REDACTED], using a widened formatter-local set (the shared RedactedHeaders.DEFAULT plus X-Auth-Token, X-Authorization, WWW-Authenticate, Referer, Location) matched with separator-normalized folding (so X-Auth-Token/X_Auth_Token/XAuthToken all match). RedactedHeaders.DEFAULT is unchanged. New additive addRedactedHeaders(...) knob alongside the replacing redactedHeaders(...). Log-forging sanitization. The request method/URI (including the 404/unrouted path), header names/values, and any dumped body text are escaped (CR/LF, NEL, line/paragraph/bidi separators, C0/C1 controls → \r/\n/\uXXXX; TAB preserved), so a client cannot inject a newline to forge a second log line or a fake status banner. Bounded output. New maxHeaders (100), maxHeaderScan (1000), maxFieldLength (1024), and maxUriLength (2048) knobs bound header and URI output; the existing bodyCap() remains the single body cap. Finish-path containment. A formatter or scrubber that throws during request completion can no longer escape and fail a completed request — only a fixed diagnostic token is logged (never the secret, message, or stack). See the Logging / Debugging topic page for the full model and the operator opt-in danger callout.

Juneau 10.0 adds always-on, end-to-end request correlation on the REST server. A per-request requestId is resolved during session build — before any @RestStartCall hook — so it covers every code path that produces a debug record, including 404s and early-error paths, and gives the debug formatter's statusLine a synchronous RestRequest.getRequestId() to read. Mint-or-honor. An inbound X-Request-Id request header is honored when present; otherwise a fresh time-ordered Uuid7 is minted. The resolved id is echoed on the X-Request-Id response header. Exactly one requestId LogContext scope is opened per request and closed after the debug record is emitted (emit-before-close), so every record on the request thread — the cumulative debug record and any handler-emitted records — carries the structured requestId field, and the rendered message is prefixed [requestId=<id>] . The id also rides the async-completion snapshot, so true-async completion records correlate identically. RequestIdSettings bean (public write-surface, resolved by RestContext via a getBean → @Bean-factory → default ladder): validator(Predicate<String>) defaults to sanitize-and-accept (strip log-forging sequences, accept the bounded remainder — not reject-and-remint), plus attributeKey(String) and idSupplier(Supplier<String>). RequestIdFilter reconciled to a thin façade. Its apply() is now idempotent with respect to the already-resolved session id (honor, never double-mint); its per-instance builder knobs are documented no-ops — request-id behavior is configured on RequestIdSettings. Auth non-influence. X-Request-Id has zero influence on authentication/authorization outcomes; configuring an auth guard to read it is an anti-pattern (regression-tested). See the Logging / Debugging topic page.

A new org.apache.juneau.commons.http.SafePathTemplate centralizes the same-origin/non-templated URL check and the MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5000 poll floor. The views toolkit's region and polling definitions call it, and the client-side runtime re-implements the same rule as defense-in-depth.

AsyncJobRegistry.tryCreate(IdempotencyKey) and create(IdempotencyKey) register a job under the key's value; submitting again with a key that is already registered returns the existing job instead of creating a second one, so a double-click, an impatient re-submit or a browser retry collapses to one job. Atomic. The lookup-or-create is atomic — concurrent submits with one key yield exactly one job. Finished jobs replay. A key whose job has finished returns that terminal job and its result (the same replay-on-duplicate contract as IdempotencyKey) rather than triggering a second run. This holds until the job is swept after the 60-second retention window; after that the key is forgotten and the same key starts a fresh job. Duplicates are free. A repeat request creates nothing, so it does not count against MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS.

Async job streams (/juneau-jobs/{jobId}/stream) now tag each progress event with an SSE id and resume from Last-Event-ID (or ?lastEventId=). A fresh attach no longer replays earlier progress. The job-log card asks for the full history itself. Live-only default (BREAKING). A fresh attach with no resume value no longer replays buffered progress. This affects every EventSource(streamUrl) client, including third-party callers of the HTTP API. Add ?lastEventId=0 to get the whole history. New lastEventId query parameter on GET /juneau-jobs/{jobId}/stream. A non-empty Last-Event-ID header beats it, so a browser's own reconnect resumes where it left off. 400 for a bad or past-the-end resume value. The status checks run in the order 404, then 400, then 429. An ended job still sends its result on every attach, fresh attaches included. Job-log card: connects with ?lastEventId=0 and no longer de-duplicates lines by count. See Async Jobs.
documents.s: Async job streams resume from Last-Event-ID (BREAKING)

documents.t: The View Settings dialog is reworked so that saved choices actually take effect on load. Applied on load. Stored View Settings (columns, search membership, sort, page size, wrap, density, auto-refresh) are restored when the page loads, not only when the dialog opens. This fixes a hidden column reappearing after a reload, in both client and server data modes. Ordered Sort tab. Sort is a priority list of column and direction entries, and an untouched Apply keeps the view's defaultOrder instead of persisting an ascending sort over every column. Auto-refresh. The Options tab gains an auto-refresh interval (Off, 30 s, 1 m, 5 m, 15 m), stored as autoRefreshMs. Per-view tabs. columnConfig: {tabs: [...]} restricts the dialog to a subset of columns, search, sort and options. Accessibility. Dialog tabs carry aria-selected/aria-controls with arrow-key navigation, every row control's label names its column, and a polite live region announces search results and a dismissed, unapplied search. Copy link button beside the gear, shown for the primary (or only) view table. Column search popover shows a per-type help line (the text of SearchType.bareHelp()). BREAKING: the columnSearchToggle ribbon type is removed. The ribbon ignores an unknown type silently, so an adopter just loses the button; per-column search is the search icon in each header cell. BREAKING: the saved View Settings schemaVersion is now 2, and NS.config.readViewSettings returns {settings, reset}. A saved blob at version 1, or with the old string-array sort, is discarded with a one-time notice; saved-view blobs at version 1 are rejected too. A stored blob is ignored for tables without columnConfig. BREAKING: NS.config.defaultSortMembership is removed. BREAKING: the Options blob gains autoRefreshMs (old blobs read as Off), and isPollSuspended now also returns true while the View Settings dialog is open, which pauses any existing pausePollingWhileEditing view. See the new Datatable View Settings topic page.

New run-view region: a multi-step run summary driven by a small, versioned event stream, with <@card type="run-view">, RunViewMixin, and readers that turn test-report files into events. New module: juneau-run-report (package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.runreport) holds RunEvent, the grammar checks (RunViewChecks) and the report readers. It does not depend on the REST server, so a producer can use it alone; juneau-rest-server-views depends on it. Events: RunEvent factories for step, end, suite, test, replace, note and done (contractVersion "1"). The client reduces them to a failures-first summary, a step list, and per-suite strips of test blocks with tooltips; counts stay exact past the retention caps. Sources: RunViewLog (in memory) and FileRunViewSource (a growing JSON Lines file, with 410 Gone after truncation). Implement RunViewSource for anything else. Endpoint: RunViewMixin serves /juneau-run-view/{runId}/events; RunViewEndpoints gives the same logic for custom paths. Report readers: ReportReaders.forKind(...) reads Surefire, JUnit XML, pytest, Jest JSON and Playwright JSON reports without throwing on bad input, and ReportResult.toEvents(step) feeds the region. Re-run steps: steps named <id>.2, <id>.3 (titled (attempt N)) collapse under the latest attempt, behind an "N earlier attempts" toggle that starts collapsed. Client: juneau-run-view.js joins the views toolkit pack and publishes JuneauViews.runView. poll: false regions take events through append, so any transport (such as SSE) works. Errors: the region reports E-RV-1 to E-RV-9; the console shell adds E-JS-14. The console shell's unknown-card-type message now lists html|datatables|run-view. See the new Run View Region topic page.

New terminal region: a command's raw output rendered by xterm.js, colours, redraws and all, with <@card type="terminal">, TerminalMixin, and a launcher that runs commands under a PTY. New module: juneau-rest-server-terminal (opt-in). It depends on juneau-rest-server-views and the xterm.js WebJar org.webjars.npm:xterm__xterm 6.0.0. Endpoints: TerminalMixin serves /juneau-terminal/{id}/bytes (raw bytes by offset, with Term-* headers) and /raw; TerminalEndpoints gives the same logic for custom paths. Sources: FileTerminalSource (a growing log with a .size sidecar) and MemoryTerminalSource (a ring buffer). Launcher: TerminalProcess runs a command under juneau_run.py --pty and serves its log and events. juneau_run.py: new --pty, --size COLSxROWS and --events PATH options, plus --input stdin and --prompts stdio to pass input or the job's prompt channel through. Non-PTY runs are unchanged. Prompts: TerminalProcess.start(..., TerminalPrompts) relays the job's prompt lines and sends answers back with answer(jsonLine); closing it cancels the job. Run view: step, suite and test events gain an optional rawOffset; rawHref takes {offset} and onBlockClick gets offset. rawLine, {line} and info.line are gone. The contract version stays "1". Console UI: the terminal card type and the xterm and terminal toolkit packs. terminal is now a reserved card type name. It replaces the console-output card. xterm options: the client takes an allowlisted terminal object (convertEol, scrollback, fontFamily) in mount and on the terminal card; other keys are ignored. Server-built cards set it through the new TerminalDef.terminal(Map) builder method or the card body, and the server rejects unknown keys and bad values. See the new Terminal Region topic page.

New build tooling: juneau_run.py, a stdlib-only Python wrapper that runs Maven, pytest, Playwright, Gradle, npm and Bazel commands, parses their output into steps and test counts, and draws a board console view. Juneau's own test.py, push.py and release.py run on it. It is attached to org.apache.juneau:juneau-run as a py (the engine), a zip (bootstrap.py, the juneau_scripts toolkit, the pytest plugin and the Playwright reporter) and a py with classifier pytest. It is build tooling, so juneau-bom does not manage it. Console view: --console full|board|none (or JUNEAU_RUN_CONSOLE), one row per step with a progress bar, counts and a summary line, and JUNEAU_RUN_DETAIL (summary, actionable, modules, all) for how much a finished step keeps. --full-log and --board-log write the raw output and the rows. Run history: per-step timings and test counts under ~/.cache/juneau-run/history, shared by branches and worktrees of one repository, give percents, estimates and an Overall line (JUNEAU_RUN_HISTORY, JUNEAU_RUN_HISTORY_DIR, JUNEAU_RUN_HISTORY_KEY). Run-protocol markers: RUN_MARKERS=1 prints ##run <json> events for a runner UI, and RUN_ARTIFACTS keeps copies of the test reports. Maven rows: one block per module. A single-project build (a one-module tree, or -pl without --also-make) draws one module and counts 1/1 on success. A build that stops before test (goals up to test-compile, or -DskipTests) still draws its module bar, counting modules as they compile, with no test totals. Pytest plugin: -p juneau_run_pytest is added to pytest runs (opt out with JUNEAU_RUN_PYTEST_PLUGIN=0), so the bar has one block per test file and shows the running file. Without the plugin, the bar keeps one block per test. Playwright reporter: added through PW_TEST_REPORTER beside the config's reporters (opt out with JUNEAU_RUN_PLAYWRIGHT_REPORTER=0). It gives one block per test file, counts a retried test once, writes <step>-playwright.json, and off a terminal sets PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never. PTY mode: --pty, --size, --events, --input stdin and --prompts stdio; this is what TerminalProcess runs (see the Terminal region section above). Cancelling: each tool runs in its own process group. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM sends SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL after a grace period, so forked JVMs and browsers don't outlive the run; the run ends as cancelled (exit 130). Script toolkit: juneau_scripts gives push and release scripts git helpers, a session with exit codes, tool runners, resumable steps, locks, notifications and prompts, loaded through the vendored bootstrap.py. Juneau build rows: test.py draws Compile, Java tests, Python tests and Browser tests (always shown, marked skipped with the reason when not run); push.py adds Prechecks, Tags, BOM, Timing, Install, Commit and Push. Wrapping: every line of a wrapped bar holds the same number of cells as the first. Expected tests: a running row shows the expected test total from previous runs, e.g. 41,200 / ~83,000 tests. Steadier estimates: the estimated total time changes only when a new estimate differs by more than 15 seconds or 10%, whichever is larger, and is rounded to 5, 15 or 30 seconds by size. The overall ~X left figure behaves the same way. See the new juneau-run topic page.

Two new console card types. Both load their script on demand through a toolkit pack, so pages that don't use them load nothing new. chart card: line, bar and donut charts drawn as inline SVG by juneau-charts.js, from a src= endpoint or inline data, with optional refreshMs, click-through, a data-table view and an open kind registry (JuneauCharts.register). Built from Java with the new ChartDef builder. job-log card: a form that starts an AsyncJobsMixin job, streams its progress lines, shows the outcome, offers Cancel, and reconnects after a reload. A dropped stream resumes after the last line shown, using the server's Last-Event-ID support (see "Async job streams resume from Last-Event-ID" above). Built from Java with CardSpec.of("job-log", id). Reserved: job-log is now a reserved card type. See the new Chart Cards and Job-Log Card topic pages.

A job can now be started for one table row, from the row or from its detail panel, with a key the server binds to that row. JuneauViews.jobs: run (submit, stream from the start, settle, cancel, with onStart / onProgress / onResult / onEnd hooks and an optional paint: "none"), fetchKey, active, pending and cancel. It allows one job per row, takes the row id only from the row's stamp, and substitutes {id} only. "jobs" joins NS.HOOK_NAMESPACES. helpers.jobButton: a button that runs a row job through JuneauViews.jobs. JobKeyLedger and RowJobSubmit: server-side keys bound to an action, a row id and the caller, issued by a key endpoint, verified on submit, and spent once their job exists. A key for one row is refused for another with 409 write-guard:idempotency-binding-mismatch; a spent key replays its job or answers write-guard:idempotency-key-spent, so a replay never starts a second job. Job-log region: the job-log card now runs inside a row-detail region (populate: 'job-log', built from Java with JobLogRegion). It gains submit.envelope / submit.action, hidden fields, source: 'row.<field>' presets and output, which writes a result value into the card or panel. A datatables card with a job-log region loads the joblog pack by itself, through the new CardTypeHandler.requiredPacks(JsonMap). window.JuneauJobLog.mount mounts one programmatically. JobLogChecks holds the validation both paths share. New errors E-JS-109 to E-JS-113. A panel re-attached after a collapse can cancel its job. RegionDef.config: populator-owned configuration, emitted only when set and delivered to the populator as ctx.declared.config, including from a datatables card's detail.region. A busy row refuses ordinary row actions: a row action activated on a row that already has a pending or running job (a JuneauViews.jobs run or another row action's job) is refused with row-job-running and sends nothing, instead of starting a second concurrent job for the row. It runs normally once the job ends. Marker re-applied after redraws: a row's data-juneau-job marker, row-action jobs included, is put back on the new <tr> after every table draw, and cleared from whichever <tr> is drawn when the job ends. Poll held while a panel runs a job: while an expanded detail panel hosts a running row job, the table's timer reload is held and the staleness pill shows Paused, whether or not the view sets pausePollingWhileEditing. User reloads, sorts, filters and page changes still draw. Fix: in-panel elements resolve their parent row. hookContextOf, and with it NS.rowActions.contextOf, now resolves an element inside a detail panel to the panel's parent row and its data, instead of a child row with empty data. A row-detail region's visibleWhen therefore tests the parent row's data, as documented. An element in a nested table's own row still resolves that row. Fix: console-card detail regions project lazy. A datatables card's detail.region now carries the same lazy value as the builder path (false unless the region is a tab body), so the two produce the same sidecar. Petstore: the Jobs page gains a species table whose detail panel restocks that species, and a "Groom again" button on each groom run. See the new Row Jobs topic page and Job-Log Card.
documents.s: Row jobs and the row-aware job-log card (juneau-rest-server-views, juneau-rest-server-console-ui)

documents.t: Three Java copies of logic that the views JS owns are removed, and the JS is the single implementation: CalendarLayout removed. Calendar lane and chip layout is computed by juneau-calendar.js only. CalendarDef and the calendar card are unchanged. RegionDef.serializeParams(...) / resolvedDataUrl() removed. Region data URLs are built client-side by juneau-regions.js. Saved views removed. SavedViewsMixin, SavedViewStore, InMemorySavedViewStore and SavedViewQuotaException are gone, along with the server persistence provider in juneau-config.js (createServerProvider, data-juneau-saved-views). Column configuration persists to localStorage only. Built-in operator help text moved to JS. Built-in SearchOperators no longer carry help on the wire. The column-search popover reads built-in help from JuneauViews.search.SearchOperators.help(name). Custom operators still supply their own help. Ribbon behavior: Client-mode tables now apply column-scoped ribbon options. Previously only server-mode tables did, so client-mode adopters needed their own bridge script. Ribbon values are BeanQuery $-expressions ($eq(DROPPED), $in(Waiting,"Partially reviewed")), never regular expressions. A regex-looking value is passed to the search engine as written and matches nothing useful. New default setting. Use default: true on an option, or default: '<memberId>' on an optionGroup, to choose the initial selection when nothing is persisted. A stored choice always wins. Nothing auto-selects without default. opt is no longer comma-joined across ribbon contributions. The last contribution wins. Parity corpus. ribbon-corpus.json (views test resources) is the contract between the JS encoder and the Java DataTables request decoder. RibbonCorpus_Test (Java) and RibbonCorpus_Parity_Test (JS) both bind to it. Any change to ribbon encoding must update the corpus in the same change. Migration: replace regex ribbon values with the equivalent $eq/$in. Replace any page script that auto-applied a ribbon's first option with default.
documents.s: Console views cleanup and ribbon parity corpus (BREAKING)

documents.t: RibbonItem.id(String): a ribbon item, including a refresh() item, can now carry an id. The id is emitted on the item's ribbon entry and is rejected on divider and export items. Ribbon optionGroup title: the group title is now rendered as role="group" with aria-label, so assistive technology announces it. No visible caption is drawn. Render.meta(String, Object): the value may now be a Number or Boolean, which stays a JSON number or boolean (for example meta("places", 2)). It was String-only. Column.href(...) implies render("linked"): a column with an href and no render now emits the linked renderer, in both Java (Column.toCatalogMap()) and FreeMarker (DatatablesCardType). An explicit render always wins. Migration: Column.toCatalogMap() used to throw IllegalArgumentException for an href without render("linked"). That throw is gone, so a test that expected it must change, and render("linked") may be dropped. RowDetail region is optional: RowDetail.toMap() no longer requires a region. A detail with none is a header-only panel whose title and icon are filled from the endpoint's fields, and its entry carries no region key. openConfirmOnlyDialog passes the row to a confirm renderer: a per-row action's confirmRenderer now receives rows (the one row), labelField and rowIdField, the same way the bulk path passes them, so it can name the row it guards. A ribbon-hosted dialog has no row, so rows is empty. Migration: a custom confirmRenderer that assumed rows was always empty or absent for a single-row action must handle a one-element rows. Same-origin path checks (stricter): a card src must be a relative or root-relative same-origin path, so an absolute https://this-host/... src is now rejected at page build. Same-origin path checks now reject a backslash anywhere (including in the query, for example /search?q=C:\x), a leading or trailing space or control character, any C0 control character, and DEL. Badge src and href must be same-origin paths. Migration: change an absolute card src to a root-relative path. PageSpec.card(...) runs the card type's handler (behaviour change): a builder-API card of an adopter (non-reserved) type is now built the way <@card> builds it. Its body map is the authored body, the type's registered CardTypeHandler validates it and returns the fragment the card carries, and an invalid body fails the render with the <@card> message. Markup passed to card(spec, markup) is the card's body, as the content of <@card> is: JSON5 markup is parsed by the handler and is not emitted as a <template>, its subscribes / publishes keys are wired onto the card (refused when the CardSpec sets them too), and markup is emitted as the card's template only when the handler captures it. As in <@card>, the body may not set a base key (id, type, title, src, template, ref), a card takes at most one of a body map, non-blank markup, template or src, and sanitize is refused before the handler runs. An unregistered type still passes its body through as-is. Previously such a card was seeded as written, with no validation, and its markup was always emitted as a template. Migration: a builder card that carried the handler's output (for example by calling toFragment itself) must carry the authored body instead.
documents.s: Console views API gap fixes (juneau-rest-server-views, juneau-rest-server-console-ui-freemarker)

documents.t: image/jpeg accepted: the example ImageParser and the petstore PetPhotoParser now consume image/jpeg as well as image/png and image/jpg.

RestRequest.timeout(Duration) is now honored by every transport (bug fix) — previously only JavaHttpTransport applied the per-request timeout; the Apache HttpClient 4.5/5, OkHttp, Jetty and mock transports silently ignored it. Each now uses its native per-request mechanism (HttpClient 4.5 RequestConfig socket/connect timeouts, HttpClient 5 request-scoped response timeout, OkHttp per-call read timeout, Jetty response-header wait, and a simulated handler deadline in MockHttpTransport) and throws a TransportException on expiry. A null timeout leaves existing behaviour unchanged; zero or negative durations are rejected with IllegalArgumentException by RestRequest.timeout(...) on every transport. Apache HttpClient 5 transport: credentials on cross-origin redirects with a caller-supplied client — with a caller-supplied CloseableHttpClient, the transport passes a per-request context that removes Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and X-API-Key from a redirect hop to another origin (scheme, host or port) and from every later hop, whatever RedirectStrategy the client uses (including LaxRedirectStrategy); the client's own redirect settings are unchanged. On a proxied route that is not tunnelled (a plain http target through an HTTP proxy), Proxy-Authorization is kept, because it authenticates to the proxy that every hop goes through. An Authorization the client's CredentialsProvider adds for the other origin is removed too. Clients from HttpClients.createMinimal() now work with the transport. Apache HttpClient 5 transport: cross-origin redirects followed with credentials stripped on the client it creates (behaviour change) — when the transport creates its own HttpClient, a redirect to another origin on a request carrying Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization or X-API-Key is now followed with those headers removed from that hop and every later hop, as on the other transports, using the same per-request context. Previously HttpClient's DefaultRedirectStrategy refused the redirect and the 3xx response was returned. Same-origin redirects keep the headers; the redirect cap, circular-redirect check, POST-to-GET rewrite and SSRF-guarded requests are unchanged.

The next-generation RestClient's debug logging pipeline (RestClientDebugPipeline / BasicRestClientDebugFormatter) now gets the same stable-emission and secret-hardening treatment the server side's RestDebugFormatter got above — ported onto the client's parallel classes, reusing the same juneau-rest-common primitives (DebugTextSanitizer, RestDebugBodyScrubber). This is an unreleased-10.0 hard break in the client debug formatter's output — there is no compatibility shim. Stable-INFO emission. Every debug LogRecord — on both the normal response-close path and the transport-exception synthetic-response path — is now always stamped Level.INFO; the resolved tier (FINE/ FINEST) continues to control message detail only, not the emitted record level. No body dumps by default. Request/response bodies are never dumped unless an operator explicitly sets the same JUNEAU_REST_DEBUG_ALLOW_DUMP_BODIES environment variable the server uses (byte-identical name and trim-then-parse truthy semantics — one env var now gates both sides). With the gate unset, FINEST emits a suppression placeholder + byte count instead of body content, replacing the previous unconditional UTF-8 + hex dump. Even opted in, bodies render only for renderable text content (via a duplicated isBodyRenderable(String) predicate on RestClientDebugFormatter, resolved independently per request/response side) and only for an identity Content-Encoding; non-renderable/binary content and non-identity encodings yield a distinct "not rendered" placeholder. RestDebugBodyScrubber opt-in, registered via the new bodyScrubber(...) builder method on BasicRestClientDebugFormatter — gate-subordinate and fail-closed, same contract as the server side: a throw or null result falls closed to a placeholder, never the raw body. Widened, formatter-local header redaction, matching the server's added set (X-Auth-Token, X-Authorization, WWW-Authenticate, Referer, Location, atop the shared RedactedHeaders.DEFAULT), matched with separator-normalized folding (X-Auth-Token/X_Auth_Token/XAuthToken all match). Log-forging sanitization. The request method/URI, header names/values, and any dumped body text are escaped (CR/LF and other control characters → \r/\n/\uXXXX), so a server cannot inject a newline into a response header/body to forge a second physical log line. Out of scope for this port (client-specific rationale): the server's maxHeaders/maxHeaderScan/maxFieldLength/ maxUriLength bounding knobs have no client-side analog, since the client's header source is already a finite, bounded list rather than an adversarial unbounded servlet input. See the Logging and Debugging topic page for the full model.
documents.s: Secure-by-default NG REST client debug hardening (RestClientDebugFormatter)

documents.t: RestClient now auto-participates in end-to-end request correlation, pairing with the server's always-on requestId resolver above. Auto-send / mint. Every outgoing request carries an X-Request-Id header; if the caller hasn't set one, the client mints a time-ordered Uuid7. A caller-supplied header (builder-global or per-request) is honored, never overwritten. RestClient.Builder.sendRequestId(false) opts out of auto-sending. Pre-call setter + getters. RestRequest.requestId(String) sets the id for one call; RestRequest.getRequestId() reads the sent id; RestResponse.getRequestId() exposes the id the server echoed back. Effective-id logging. RestClientDebugPipeline stamps each emitted LogRecord with a structured requestId field (echoed id when present, else the sent id) via LogRecordContext.attachIfAbsent(...), and BasicRestClientDebugFormatter prepends a [requestId=<id>] marker to the rendered message — matching the server's statusLine prefix so a request reads identically on both sides. Shared constants. The X-Request-Id header name and max length live in a shared RequestIdConstants in juneau-rest-common, consumed by both client and server. See the Logging and Debugging topic page.

Juneau 10.0 significantly expands what the REST proxy annotation family (@Remote, @RemoteOp, and the verb annotations @RemoteGet / @RemotePost / @RemotePut / @RemoteDelete / @RemotePatch) can express declaratively. These additions originally landed on the next-generation proxy engine only (RestClient.remote(...) → RemoteClient); a later classic/next-gen parity pass brought the classic getRemote(...) engine up to the same level for every member below except the method/interface interceptors() policy attribute and the declarative @Multipart marker, which remain next-generation-only (see each bullet for the current per-member status). Constant part values — @Remote (interface) and @RemoteOp / verb annotations (method) gain headers / queryData / formData members that emit always-applied constant headers, query parameters, and form-data fields on every call, with no dummy parameter. Method-level constants take precedence over interface-level ones, caller-supplied values still compose, and all values resolve through VarResolver.DEFAULT. Honored by both engines. (Constant path values are out of scope; @Remote(headerList=…) remains classic-only.) @Content(def=…) honored — the next-gen engine now applies both the parameter-level body default (when the body argument is null) and a param-less, method-level constant body, matching the classic engine. Per-part serializers — @HttpPartMarshalling(serializer=…) is now wired for outgoing query / header / path / form-data parts, with precedence parameter › method › interface and a fallback to the default OpenApiSerializer when absent. (Serializer side only; the parser member is not consumed by the next-gen engine.) Declarative call policy — @Remote and @RemoteOp / verb annotations gain interceptors(), timeout(), retries(), retryNonIdempotent(), and throwOnError(). Interceptors apply as a union (builder → interface → method); timeout/retries/throwOnError scalars follow method › interface › builder-default precedence. Auto-retries are conservatively safe: triggered only by connection failures or 429/5xx, with exponential backoff, and gated to idempotent verbs (POST/PATCH require opt-in), repeatable bodies, and buffered (non-streaming) return modes only. timeout() / retries() / retryNonIdempotent() / throwOnError() are honored by both engines; interceptors() remains next-generation-only — the classic engine explicitly rejects it (with a one-time warning) because the classic and next-generation RestCallInterceptor SPI types are nominally incompatible. Dynamic URL & base override — a new @Url parameter annotation (org.apache.juneau.http.Url) supplies the whole request URL at call time (absolute replaces and bypasses the client root URL; relative resolves against it), plus a declarative baseUrl() attribute on @Remote / @RemoteOp / verb annotations that substitutes the authority+root while preserving the path and {var} templating. Precedence: @Url › method baseUrl › interface baseUrl › client rootUrl. @Url / baseUrl() are honored by both engines — the classic getRemote(...) engine resolves them the same way. Declarative multipart — a new method-level @Multipart marker (org.apache.juneau.http.remote.Multipart) plus a @Part parameter annotation (org.apache.juneau.http.Part, with name/value/fileName/contentType) build a multipart/form-data request from annotated parameters. Text, byte[], File, InputStream, Reader, HttpBody, and bean part sources are accepted; file/stream/reader/bean parts stream rather than buffer. A method is either multipart or single-@Content (validated at proxy-build time); hand-assembling a MultipartBody as a @Content body remains available as an escape hatch. Next-generation-only; the classic engine has no equivalent multipart-assembly support. Per-method format selection — contentType() and accept() attributes on @Remote / @RemoteOp / verb annotations drive marshaller selection (not just header values). contentType selects the matching request serializer and emits a single clean Content-Type; accept sets the Accept header and acts as a fallback parser (the response Content-Type stays authoritative). A no-match media type falls back to the default marshaller but still sends the overridden label (vendor types). Precedence: method › interface › client default; the dedicated attribute beats a constant header. Honored by both engines. Streaming efficiency — POJO and Reader request bodies now stream straight to the wire instead of being buffered, and Reader / InputStream return types hand the caller a lazy stream over the live response whose connection is released on close. See the expanded Declarative Remote-Proxy Features section of the Next-Generation REST Client topic page for full examples and precedence rules.

The next-generation REST client's HTTP transports now transparently retry a request exactly once when a pooled keep-alive connection is torn down by the server before any response bytes are received (an immediate EOF / connection reset) — a common source of intermittent failures against servers that idle-close persistent connections. The retry is gated on provable safety: an idempotent HTTP method (GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE) with an absent or repeatable body (TransportRequest.isSafeToReplay()). A POST or any other non-idempotent request is never replayed, so a request cannot double-execute a side effect. JettyHttpTransport and ApacheHc45Transport gained this in an earlier 10.0.0 change; JavaHttpTransport (the default, JDK HttpClient-backed transport) now matches them. The JDK client self-retries only body-less GETs on such a failure, so the transport-level retry closes the gap for the other idempotent methods (e.g. PUT / DELETE). A shared predicate, TransportException.isStaleConnectionFailure(Throwable), recognizes the failure signature across transports (EOFException / ClosedChannelException / a connection-reset SocketException / the JDK's "HTTP/1.1 header parser received no bytes" message).

Juneau 10.0 introduces a public low-level streaming surface that complements the POJO databind path with cursor-based push and pull primitives, layered: RecordReader / RecordWriter — whole-value record cursor (canRead() / read(Class) / write(Object)). Format-neutral, works on every Juneau format. TokenReader / TokenWriter — fine-grained structural cursor (next(), startObject(), fieldName(...), etc.). For formats whose wire encoding is already token-shaped: JSON, JSON5, JSONL, JSON5L, CBOR, MsgPack. TokenReader extends RecordReader and TokenWriter extends RecordWriter, so token-capable formats inherit record-stream semantics for free; record-only formats expose only the record surface so the type system enforces "no nested structure visible at the cursor." Capability is expressed through role interfaces in org.apache.juneau.marshall.stream and detected with instanceof (there is no capability enum): RecordReadable / RecordWritable — readRecords(input) / writeRecords(output); implemented by every streaming format. TokenReadable / TokenWritable — readTokens(input) / writeTokens(output); implemented by json, json5, jsonl, json5l, cbor, msgpack. (These extend the record roles.) ArrayRecordReadable / ArrayRecordWritable — readArrayRecords(input) / writeArrayRecords(output); implemented by json, json5, cbor, msgpack, bson, parquet, yaml, xml, html. A cursor-quality signal (isRecordStreaming() / isArrayRecordStreaming()) distinguishes a true O(1) streaming cursor from a buffered one. Writer-only formats (jsonschema, jcs, soap-xml) implement only the *Writable roles. Naturally-multi-record formats (jsonl, json5l, csv, sse) expose readRecords/writeRecords as a true multi-record cursor: N read calls yield N records; N write calls produce wire output equivalent to serialize(List.of(records)). Opt-in readArrayRecords / writeArrayRecords for streaming the elements of a top-level wire array on JSON / JSON5 / CBOR (actually streaming, O(1) memory in array length), plus MsgPack / BSON / Parquet / YAML / XML / HTML (buffered). MsgPack offers a count-overload writeArrayRecords(output, expectedCount) that writes the length-prefix header up front and serializes each element directly to the output stream — no per-element buffering. Mismatch between declared count and actual write count throws on close. XML and HTML expose readArrayRecords(input, rootElementName) for caller-specified array root elements. REST integration​ TokenReader, RecordReader, TokenWriter, RecordWriter and concrete subtypes (e.g. JsonlTokenReader) are first-class @RestOp-method parameter types. Two-layer resolution: declared parameter type filters eligible parsers/serializers; HTTP Content-Type / Accept negotiates within that filter. Mismatch returns HTTP 415. See the new REST Streaming Integration topic page. Documentation​ A full topic-page family lives under "2.50. Token / Record Streaming" in the Marshalling section: Basics, Record Streaming, Token Streaming, Array-Record Streaming, and REST Streaming Integration. The streaming surface is purely structural — object swaps and @Schema annotations apply only on the POJO databind path, never at the token layer. Both surfaces are additive; the existing POJO ↔ document API remains the primary, recommended path.

Juneau 10.0 adds JSON5L — a new line-delimited format combining the relaxed JSON5 dialect with JSONL's one-document-per-line framing. It ships as a new org.apache.juneau.marshall.json5l package (Json5lSerializer / Json5lParser / sessions / Json5lTokenReader), a Json5l marshaller, and a @Json5lConfig annotation. Strict by default, sugar opt-in — the serializer emits strict RFC-8259 JSON per line by default (byte-identical to JsonlSerializer), keeping output maximally portable. Json5lSerializer.create().json5Sugar() switches the per-line output to JSON5 sugar (single-quoted strings, unquoted field names where safe). Full JSON5 parse leniency — the parser accepts the full JSON5 dialect on each line (comments, unquoted/single-quoted keys, trailing commas, relaxed numbers). Because JSON5 is a strict superset of JSON, it also reads plain JSONL input unchanged.
