There is no RestContext.Builder.validate(true), no juneau.validation.enabled=true system property, and no resource-level boolean attribute that enables validation across every operation in a class. Granular per-parameter opt-in is the only opt-in surface. No silent enablement via classpath presence. Even if jakarta.validation-api and hibernate-validator are on the classpath, validation does not run unless the user has opted in via @Valid (or one of the equivalent FQN markers — see below). Graceful degradation. If @Valid is present but no Jakarta Validation provider is reachable at runtime, the integration silently skips validation, emits a one-shot WARNING log per JVM, and lets the request continue with the bean unchanged. The off-by-default behavior is preserved even in misconfigured deployments. Tests verify the contract. RestValidation_OffByDefault_Test exercises the "violating bean, no @Valid marker → reaches handler" and "violating bean, @Valid marker → blocked with 400" pair against the same @Content parameter, against per-method granularity, and against cascading @Valid on a nested property. None of those tests rely on classpath inspection.

The integration recognises three opt-in markers, all detected by fully-qualified name (FQN) so no compile-time dependency on the marker packages is required: Marker Source Notes @jakarta.validation.Valid Jakarta Bean Validation 3.x Recommended. Standard marker for cascading and root-bean validation. @javax.validation.Valid Bean Validation 2.x (legacy javax.* namespace) Recognised for migration friendliness. Most modern stacks have moved to jakarta.*. @org.springframework.validation.annotation.Validated Spring Framework Recognised for migration friendliness. Group support is not yet honored — the marker triggers default-group validation only. The marker can sit on a @Content, @FormData, or @Request-bound parameter: @RestPost("/orders") public Order create(@Content @Valid OrderRequest in) { ... } @RestPost("/signup") public Result signup(@Request @Valid SignupRequest req) { ... } @RestPost("/upload") public Result upload(@FormData(name="*") @Valid UploadMetadata meta) { ... }

When validation fails, the integration throws a ValidationException (BadRequest subclass, status 400) carrying an immutable List<ValidationViolation>. The response shape depends on whether RFC 7807 problem details are enabled for the operation (see RFC 7807 / 9457 Problem Details).

Content-Type: application/json: { "status": 400, "errors": [ { "path": "customerId", "message": "must not be blank", "constraint": "NotBlank" }, { "path": "quantity", "message": "must be greater than 0", "constraint": "Positive" } ] } The top-level shape mirrors Spring MVC's MethodArgumentNotValidException payload for migration friendliness — status and errors[] at the root, one violation per array element.

Content-Type: application/problem+json: { "type": null, "title": "Bad Request", "status": 400, "detail": "1 violation(s) found.", "errors": [ { "path": "customerId", "message": "must not be blank", "constraint": "NotBlank" } ] } The errors[] array is an extension member (RFC 7807 §3.2) — the canonical members (type, title, status, detail) describe the failure category and the extension carries the per-violation breakdown.

ValidationViolation carries an optional invalidValue field which is omitted by default for privacy reasons (the offending value may be PII, an API key, a partial credit card number, or otherwise sensitive). Handlers that need to surface the value — e.g. an internal debugging endpoint — can include it explicitly by constructing the violation with the value setter. The renderer honors a non-null value verbatim and omits a null one.

juneau-rest-server's pom.xml declares the Jakarta Validation API in provided scope: <dependency> <groupId>jakarta.validation</groupId> <artifactId>jakarta.validation-api</artifactId> <version>3.0.2</version> <scope>provided</scope> </dependency> Consumers who never write @Valid pay no transitive cost — no Jakarta Validation, no Hibernate Validator, no Jakarta EL pulled in automatically. Consumers who opt in supply the runtime provider on their own classpath: <!-- in the consumer's pom.xml --> <dependency> <groupId>org.hibernate.validator</groupId> <artifactId>hibernate-validator</artifactId> <version>8.0.3.Final</version> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>org.glassfish.expressly</groupId> <artifactId>expressly</artifactId> <version>5.0.0</version> </dependency> Hibernate Validator is the reference implementation of Bean Validation 3.0 and is the recommended provider. Jakarta Expression Language (Expressly) is required for dynamic message interpolation — without it, Hibernate Validator throws on the first .validate() call with HV000183.

If a parameter carries @Valid but no Jakarta Validation provider is reachable at runtime (the API JAR is on the classpath but the engine isn't), the integration silently skips validation and emits a one-shot WARNING log per JVM: WARNING: Jakarta Bean Validation was requested via @Valid on a REST argument, but no jakarta.validation.Validator bean is registered and no runtime provider (e.g. org.hibernate.validator:hibernate-validator + jakarta.el implementation) is on the classpath. Validation will be silently skipped for this and subsequent requests. Add a provider dependency or register a Validator bean to enable validation. The request continues through the handler with the bean unmodified — the off-by-default contract is preserved. This matches the FQN-detection precedent established by JSR-330 / Spring-Lite: feature presence is signaled by the consumer (via the marker annotation) but the engine is a runtime resolution that fails open, not a startup-time hard requirement.

The integration consults, in order: A user-supplied jakarta.validation.Validator bean visible from the resource's BeanStore. Typically contributed via a @Bean factory on the resource class: @Rest(path="/orders") public class OrderResource { @Bean public Validator validator() { return Validation.byDefaultProvider() .configure() .messageInterpolator(new ParameterMessageInterpolator()) // no jakarta.el .buildValidatorFactory() .getValidator(); } } Use this when the deployment needs custom message interpolators, group sequences, a non-default ConstraintValidatorFactory, or a parameter-message interpolator that doesn't require jakarta.el at runtime. A lazily-built JVM-wide default obtained from Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory(). Cached after the first successful build so the factory cost is paid at most once per JVM, regardless of how many @Rest resources opt in. null — the graceful-degradation path described above.

User-defined constraints work transparently — the integration delegates entirely to the underlying jakarta.validation engine for constraint discovery: @Target(ElementType.FIELD) @Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME) @Constraint(validatedBy = SkuValidator.class) public @interface Sku { String message() default "must match SKU-NNNN format"; Class<?>[] groups() default {}; Class<? extends Payload>[] payload() default {}; } public class SkuValidator implements ConstraintValidator<Sku, String> { public boolean isValid(String value, ConstraintValidatorContext ctx) { return value != null && value.matches("SKU-\\d{4}"); } } public class OrderItem { @Sku public String sku; @Min(1) public int qty; } A @Valid OrderItem parameter will surface a Sku-named constraint in errors[].constraint alongside the built-in Min from jakarta.validation.constraints.Min.

@Valid on a nested property tells the validator to recurse into that property and re-evaluate its constraints — but only if the parent's @Valid has triggered validation in the first place. The cascade still respects the off-by-default contract: if the parent has no @Valid, the nested @Valid alone does not trigger validation. public class Address { @Pattern(regexp="\\d{5}") public String zip; } public class Customer { @NotBlank public String name; @Valid public List<Address> addresses; // cascades only if Customer has @Valid above } @RestPost("/customer") public String create(@Valid @Content Customer c) { return "ok:" + c.name; } A bad zip surfaces at path addresses[0].zip in the violation list, proving the recursion happened.

Class Package Notes ValidationException org.apache.juneau.rest.server.validation BadRequest (400) subclass. Carries List<ValidationViolation>. ValidationViolation org.apache.juneau.rest.server.validation path, message, constraint, optional invalidValue. BeanValidator org.apache.juneau.rest.server.validation Static dispatcher. isValidationRequested(ParameterInfo), validate(T bean, BeanStore). The arg-resolver wiring lives in ContentArg, FormDataArg, and RequestBeanArg — each computes its per-parameter boolean validate flag once at construction time and conditionally invokes BeanValidator.validate(...) per request only when the flag is true.

The following are explicit non-goals for the initial integration. Each can be added in a follow-on release without breaking the v1 contract. Method-level validation. Constraints on @RestOp return values (@Valid on the return type) and @Validated on the resource class (which would imply method-parameter validation across every operation in the class). The v1 integration validates parameter beans only. Schema-driven validation. JSON-Schema constraints on the request body — that lives in JsonSchemaGenerator territory. Group support. @Validated(Group.class) recognition for selective group validation. The marker is detected but the group classes are not yet passed through to validator.validate(bean, groups...). Messages.properties bridge. Cross-bundle composition between Juneau's Messages and Jakarta's ValidationMessages.properties. The two bundles don't compose automatically; document and configure separately. Per-resource / per-method validate=true switch. A coarse-grained opt-in attribute on @Rest and @RestOp that enables validation for every parameter on the targeted scope without per-parameter @Valid markers. The v1 integration is @Valid-only on the parameter.

RFC 7807 / 9457 Problem Details — the problem-details response shape that the validation integration plugs into for the application/problem+json path. Bean Validation 3.0 specification — the underlying Jakarta API. Hibernate Validator 8.0 reference — the recommended provider.

TokenReader, TokenWriter, RecordReader, and RecordWriter are first-class @RestOp-method parameter types. Declare one in your method signature and the framework picks the matching parser/serializer based on the request Content-Type / response Accept and hands you the cursor. See the per-format capability matrix for which formats can satisfy a RecordReader / TokenReader / RecordWriter / TokenWriter parameter.

@Rest(parsers = JsonParser.class) public class MyResource { @RestPost public String process(RecordReader r) throws Exception { Bean b = r.read(Bean.class); return b.name; } } Concrete cursor types work too — declaring JsonlTokenReader means only JsonlParser is eligible: @Rest(parsers = JsonlParser.class, defaultAccept = "application/jsonl") public class JsonlIngest { @RestPost public int countRecords(JsonlTokenReader r) throws Exception { int n = 0; while (r.canRead()) { r.read(Bean.class); n++; } return n; } }

Declaring a writer parameter flips the response into "user owns the body" mode — the framework will not later serialize a return value over the same stream: @RestGet public void exportLargeArray(RecordWriter w) throws IOException { for (Bean b : sourceOfBeans()) { w.write(b); } // close() is the framework's responsibility on return. }

Cursor parameter resolution uses two layers: Declared type filters eligible parsers/serializers. A RecordReader parameter accepts any parser that is a RecordReadable; a TokenReader parameter accepts only parsers that are a TokenReadable; a concrete JsonlTokenReader parameter accepts only parsers whose readTokens(...) returns a JsonlTokenReader. Capability is detected with instanceof against the role interface — there is no capability enum. HTTP Content-Type / Accept negotiates among the eligible set. Standard Juneau media-type matching applies. Mismatch returns HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type (or 406 Not Acceptable on the writer side): The matched parser/serializer does not implement the required role interface (RecordReadable / TokenReadable / ArrayRecordReadable and their *Writable mirrors). The matched cursor type isn't assignable to the declared parameter. No parser/serializer matched the requested media type at all.

@Rest(parsers = {JsonParser.class, CborParser.class}, defaultAccept = "application/json") public class MultiFormat { @RestPost public String process(TokenReader r) throws Exception { Bean b = r.read(Bean.class); return r.getClass().getSimpleName() + ":" + b.name; // → "JsonTokenReader:..." for application/json // → "CborTokenReader:..." for application/cbor } }

The four arg resolvers are registered in DefaultConfig.restOpArgs: RecordReaderArg TokenReaderArg RecordWriterArg TokenWriterArg Reader-side input is getReader() for ReaderParser, getInputStream() for binary parsers. Writer-side output is getNegotiatedWriter() / getNegotiatedOutputStream() similarly.
Token-Streaming Basics Record Streaming Token Streaming Array-Record Streaming

juneau-rest-server-views is the browser-side toolkit behind the console's table cards: a server-driven table view with search, sort, paging, a column chooser, saved View Settings, row actions, bulk mutation, cell popovers, row-detail regions, async-job streaming and shareable links. The server describes a view with plain beans and annotations; a first-party JavaScript runtime (juneau-views.js and its companions) draws it. Most adopters never touch the view beans directly. You author a <@card type="datatables"> catalog in a FreeMarker template (see Building a Console Page) and the chrome lifts it into the view contract for you. This section documents what that catalog can express, the security model behind it, and the JuneauViews JavaScript API for pages that need to go further. Page Covers Catalog and Columns The datatables catalog, Column, search types and operators, FieldFormat, FieldSpan. Row Actions and Bulk Mutation RowAction, SelectionDef, BulkMutateDef, ActionResult, IdempotencyKey, WritePermit. Renderers and Cell Popovers Render, built-in renderer ids, CellPopover, custom renderers. Security Model Sink allowlists, CSRF and loopback boundary, same-origin rules. JavaScript API window.JuneauViews namespaces and the asset load order. View Settings and Shareable Links The View Settings dialog, page-state persistence, Copy link and ?state=. Datatable View Settings Dialog tabs and columnConfig.tabs, the schemaVersion guard, settings applied on load, ordered Sort, auto-refresh, Copy link. Regions RegionDef, populators, row-detail regions, page-slot regions. Async Jobs AsyncJobsMixin, AsyncJobRegistry, SSE progress and cancel. Icons and Sprites JuneauViews.icons, the bundled symbol sprites, overriding icons. Run View Region RunViewMixin, RunViewLog, FileRunViewSource, the report readers, the run-view card and region.

Module Mixin / class Serves juneau-rest-server-views ViewsMixin /juneau-views.js, -renders.js, -icons.js, -search.js, -pagestate.js, -urlstate.js, -ribbon.js, -regions.js, -helpers.js, -config.js, -run-view.js, the CSS, and the symbol sprites. juneau-rest-server-views AsyncJobsMixin /juneau-jobs/{jobId}/stream and /juneau-jobs/{jobId}/cancel. juneau-rest-server-datatables DataTablesMixin /juneau-datatables.js, the browser glue for server-side processing. juneau-rest-server WebJarsMixin /webjars/*: the jQuery and DataTables WebJars. The host must compose DataTablesMixin and WebJarsMixin Every datatables card loads juneau-datatables.js (from DataTablesMixin) and jQuery and DataTables (from WebJarsMixin) before juneau-views.js, in client and server mode. If the host composes neither, those URLs 404 and the table fails loudly. See Card Asset Dependencies. @Rest( path="/console", mixins={ViewsMixin.class, ConsoleChromeMixin.class, DataTablesMixin.class, WebJarsMixin.class} ) public class ConsoleResource extends BasicRestServlet {}

The toolkit has three independent, versioned wire contracts, plus the page contract owned by the chrome. Each one is checked separately, and a mismatch fails loudly rather than degrading silently. Contract Key Current Owner Constant Page contract (JSON island #juneau-page) contractVersion "1" PageCapture / juneau-console.js PageCapture writes it; see Admin-Console Chrome View metadata (VIEW_META sidecar) contractVersion "5" ViewsMixin ViewsMixin.CONTRACT_VERSION Card slot envelope (SLOT_META) contractVersion "1" ViewsMixin ViewsMixin.SLOT_CONTRACT_VERSION Bar envelope contractVersion "1" ViewsMixin ViewsMixin.BAR_CONTRACT_VERSION Regions carry their own RegionDef.CONTRACT_VERSION ("1"), independent of all of the above. ViewsMixin.HEADER_CONTRACT_VERSION is also "1". ActionResult and BulkMutateDef carry their own CONTRACT_VERSION ("1" each) for the action-result and bulk-mutate wire shapes.

You do not write any of these numbers by hand. When a <@card type="datatables"> catalog is lifted into the contract, the chrome injects the current VIEW_META and slot versions for you; a catalog should omit contractVersion entirely. A body that is itself a pre-built slot envelope (a top-level view object) is rejected at render time; author the catalog form and let the chrome add the envelope. note ConsoleTemplateValidator still reports a literal view.contractVersion that differs from the runtime's (view-contract-version), but such a body no longer renders, so the safe practice is simply to omit the key.
Building a Console Page Admin-Console Chrome DataTables Server-Side Processing BeanQuery
A view table can offer per-row actions (a row menu), row selection, and, as an independent opt-in, bulk mutation. All of the types below live in org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views.

A RowAction is one row-menu item. On activation juneau-views.js submits the declared endpoint with the declared method as a JSON request carrying the process's CSRF token. Field Meaning id Required. Stable action id. label, icon Menu text and an optional glyph name resolved by the icon registry. endpoint The URL to submit to. May carry {property} tokens filled in from the row. method POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. confirm Optional confirmation prompt. form Optional form-source URL supplying input fields; may carry {property} tokens. Blank means a confirm-only action. present page, dialog or inline (RowAction.Present). onSuccess redraw, mergeRow or navigate (RowAction.OnSuccess). enabledWhen Row-state rules that must all match for the action to render enabled. visibleWhen Row-state rules that must all match for the action to be offered at all. RowAction ack = RowAction.create("ack") .label("Acknowledge") .endpoint("servlet:/incidents/{id}/ack") .method(RowAction.Method.POST) .confirm("Acknowledge this incident?") .present(RowAction.Present.DIALOG) .onSuccess(RowAction.OnSuccess.MERGE_ROW) .enabledWhen("state", Op.NE, "resolved", "Already resolved"); Points worth knowing: RowAction.Method contains only the four non-safe methods, so a mutating action bound to GET cannot be expressed. On the server, mutating operations are checked for the same rule at startup. A {property} token that cannot be resolved from the row refuses the submission instead of sending a malformed request. A value with no token is used exactly as written. enabledWhen is presentation only. A gated action is shown disabled with the given reason. The first matching rule wins, and a field the row does not carry fails closed. Op is EQ, NE, PRESENT or ABSENT. Prefer disabled, and hide only when the action is irrelevant to the row. visibleWhen removes the action from that row's menu and pills when its rules do not all match; it is presentation only, and a field the row does not carry fails closed (the action is hidden).

An action endpoint answers with an ActionResult (contractVersion "1"), which the runtime renders into the row's own outcome banner. outcome Meaning success The write happened. failure The write failed. refusal The server declined, with a refusalCode. unknown The outcome could not be determined. cancelled A cancelled operation that had no effect. cancelled-after-effect Cancelled, but some effect had already happened. The result can also carry replay (the duplicate of an earlier submit), a message, the updated row for mergeRow, and a resultForm hint.

IdempotencyKey is a server-minted key for a row-action submit, bound at mint time to the (action, targetId) pair it was issued for. The modal mints it when it opens, so a double-click, an impatient re-submit and a browser retry all carry the same key and collapse to one effect. IdempotencyKey key = IdempotencyKey.mint("ack", incidentId); // At submit: a key bound to a different (action, target) is a refusal, never a replayed success. if (! recorded.matches(submittedAction, submittedTargetId)) return ActionResult.refusal("write-guard:idempotency-binding-mismatch"); The value is 32 random bytes from SecureRandom, hex-encoded. IdempotencyKey.mintSelfTargeted(action) covers a row-less dialog opened from a ribbon, where the key's target is its own value.

Selection and bulk mutation are two separate opt-ins. SelectionDef adds a checkbox column, and optionally a select-all header, to a table. It does nothing else: it cannot surface a bulk-mutate control, so a table can be "selectable for export" while categorically excluding bulk writes. Selection is keyed by a stable row id (SelectionDef.create(rowIdField)), never a DOM index, so a sort, page change or poll refresh cannot retarget a selection. BulkMutateDef is the bulk-mutate opt-in. It has no zero-argument form. SelectionDef selection = SelectionDef.create("id").selectAll(true); WritePermit permit = WritePermit.forCapability("incident:bulk-ack"); // mint only after YOUR write gate passes BulkMutateDef bulk = BulkMutateDef.create(permit, selection) .actions(RowAction.create("ack") .endpoint("servlet:/incidents/{id}/ack") .method(RowAction.Method.POST)); A WritePermit is a proof-of-authorization token, not an enforcement seam. Your own write gate must have approved the capability before you mint one; omitting it is a compile error. A bulk action runs in one of two modes, chosen per action with RowAction.bulkMode(RowAction.BulkMode). The default, BulkMode.PER_ROW (wire token perRow), runs N independent per-row submissions of the same single-action path, at most four in flight at a time, each with its own CSRF POST, in-flight marker and ActionResult. BulkMode.AGGREGATE (wire token aggregate) sends a single request carrying every selected id. Either way the run ends in one summary toast, ids that succeeded or were not found leave the selection, and ids that failed stay selected so the user can retry. An aggregate action POSTs a BulkRequest as JSON to the action's endpoint: ids (the stable row ids) and idempotencyKey, a client-generated token unique to that submit. The endpoint answers with a BulkResult: a contractVersion ("1", its own contract, independent of the view, ActionResult and BulkMutateDef versions) and three lists, succeeded (ids), notFound (ids that no longer exist) and failed (an id plus a message each). The outcome is reported per id, so a partial failure is never hidden behind an overall success. A transport error, a non-2xx status, or a body that is not a BulkResult of the expected version is reported as a whole-run failure and leaves the selection intact. The server is responsible for making an aggregate endpoint idempotent on idempotencyKey (a retried submit with the same key should return the same BulkResult rather than apply twice); the framework only generates and sends the key. Source: BulkRequest, BulkResult and RowAction.BulkMode in juneau-rest-server-views; the petstore's ChangesPageBuilders and ChangesRest pair an aggregate Discard with a perRow Apply (see Pending Changes). The bulk action list is wire data with its own BulkMutateDef.CONTRACT_VERSION ("1"), independent of the view metadata version.

RowAction, SelectionDef and BulkMutateDef are the wire-contract and server-side types. SelectionDef is stamped by ViewTable as plain HTML attributes on the emitted <table> (ViewTable.SELECT_ATTR, ROW_ID_FIELD_ATTR, SELECT_ALL_ATTR), not as JSON. The <@card type="datatables"> catalog lift documented on Catalog and Columns currently copies a fixed list of keys and does not include rowActions, selection or bulk. A page that needs these features today builds its table with the ViewDef / ViewTable API rather than the FreeMarker catalog. This may change; confirm against the release you are on. See also Security Model for the CSRF and loopback rules every action submit passes through.
documents.s: How the beans reach the page

documents.t: A row action normally returns a terminal ActionResult. When the write is asynchronous, the same POST instead returns an AsyncJobRef, and the runtime streams the job's progress to the browser over Server-Sent Events. Nothing about the RowAction declaration changes; the runtime switches to the streaming path purely because the 2xx body contains a streamUrl.

Compose AsyncJobsMixin and supply a registry: @Rest(path="/console", mixins={ViewsMixin.class, AsyncJobsMixin.class}) public class ConsoleResource extends BasicRestServlet implements AsyncJobsMixin { private final AsyncJobRegistry jobs = new AsyncJobRegistry(); @Override public AsyncJobRegistry asyncJobRegistry() { return jobs; } } The mixin serves two operations under AsyncJobsMixin.JOBS_PREFIX (/juneau-jobs): Operation Path Behavior GET /juneau-jobs/{jobId}/stream Streams progress events, each with an SSE id, then sends one result event carrying the terminal ActionResult, and closes. A fresh attach is live-only; a Last-Event-ID header or lastEventId query parameter resumes from a position (see Resuming a stream). Unknown id is 404; a bad resume value is 400; a job at its subscriber cap is 429. POST /juneau-jobs/{jobId}/cancel Cancels the job.

@RestPost(path="/incidents/{id}/reindex") public AsyncJobRef reindex(@Path("id") String id) { var job = jobs.create(); // or jobs.create(IdempotencyKey) to de-duplicate executor.submit(() -> { job.progress("Starting...\n"); // ... do the work ... job.complete(ActionResult.ok()); }); return AsyncJobRef.of(job); } The table-row action banner attaches live-only, so it shows "Working…" until the next progress line or the result. A line written straight after create(), like the "Starting..." above, is usually written before the browser attaches and is then never shown. AsyncJobRef carries jobId, streamUrl and cancelUrl. The URLs are servlet:-relative and @Uri-annotated so every response serializer resolves them against the current request. AsyncJobRegistry.create() throws IllegalStateException when the concurrency cap is reached; tryCreate() returns an empty Optional instead. create(IdempotencyKey) and tryCreate(IdempotencyKey) return the existing job for a key that is already registered, including a finished one within its retention window, so a double-click or retry collapses to one job.
documents.s: Starting a job from an action

documents.t: The progress event built from the job's i-th buffered progress line is always sent with SSE id i+1; the result event has no id. The job keeps every progress line for its whole life, so an id always names the same line. The stream picks its start position from a resume value, in this order: The Last-Event-ID header, if it is non-empty after trimming spaces and tabs. A browser's EventSource sends it by itself when it reconnects a dropped stream, to the same URL. Otherwise the lastEventId query parameter, if it is non-empty after trimming. ?lastEventId=0 asks for the whole history; the Job Log card always connects this way. Otherwise there is no value, and the attach is live-only: only progress written after the client attached is sent. A value k means "the events with ids 1..k were delivered", so the stream continues with id k+1. The value must be 1 to 10 ASCII digits (so +1, -1, 1.0 or 0x2 are refused). Any k from 0 up to the number of progress lines written so far is valid; k equal to that number resumes with nothing to replay. Only a malformed value or a k past that number is refused, with 400 and no body. The checks run in the order 404 (unknown job), then 400 (bad resume value), then 429 (subscriber cap), so a bad value cannot reveal whether a job exists and never holds a subscriber slot. A job that has already ended still sends its result on every attach: a fresh attach gets only the result, and a resume gets the remaining progress and then the result.

The job id is the access control. It is a 256-bit SecureRandom value, hex-encoded. A browser EventSource cannot set a CSRF header, which is why the id must be unguessable rather than CSRF-gated. An unknown id is indistinguishable from any other miss, so the id space cannot be enumerated. Treat the stream URL as a secret. The caps are enforced on the server. AsyncJobRegistry.MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS is 8, the hard per-job timeout AsyncJobRegistry.HARD_TIMEOUT is 120 seconds (configurable through the AsyncJobRegistry(Duration) constructor), each job caps its streamed output at AsyncJob.maxOutputBytes() and its concurrent subscribers at AsyncJob.maxSubscribers(). A job over its output cap is terminated with a failure. Single process. Job state lives in the process heap. A restart drops every in-flight job, exactly as it invalidates every CSRF token. A job whose timeout fires or that is cancelled after it had an effect reports cancelled-after-effect; call AsyncJob.markEffectStarted() when the irreversible part begins so the outcome is reported truthfully. See Row Actions and Bulk Mutation for ActionResult and IdempotencyKey.

A table card is authored as a JSON5 catalog in the body of <@card type="datatables">. The chrome parses it, lifts it into the view contract and stamps the current contract versions (see Contract versions). You never hand-author the version numbers. <@card type="datatables" id="pets" title="Pets"> { dataUrl: '/console/pets/data', dataMode: 'server', defaultOrder: [[0, 'asc']], columns: [ { key: 'name', label: 'Name', searchType: 'text' }, { key: 'status', label: 'Status', searchType: 'enum' }, { key: 'price', label: 'Price', searchType: 'numeric', searchOperators: ['eq', 'gt', 'lt', 'between'] } ] } </@card>

dataUrl and columns are required; a catalog missing either fails the render with an IllegalArgumentException naming the card. Each column is an object. Key Meaning dataUrl Same-origin URL the table fetches its rows from. Must be a path, not an absolute cross-origin URL. columns[].key (or data) The row-data property this column reads. columns[].label (or title) The header text. columns[].searchType Makes the column searchable. One of the SearchType wire tokens below. A column without it is not searchable. columns[].searchOperators Optional allow-list narrowing the operators offered for the column. columns[].customOperators Optional [{name, help}] list of extra operators, with the help text the header popup shows. defaultOrder, ribbon, dataMode, rowType, pollIntervalMs, columnConfig, cleanAddress, primary Copied verbatim onto the view metadata when present. The dataMode: "server" setting selects server-side processing, driven by juneau-datatables.js. The host must compose DataTablesMixin; see the module table. The data endpoint behind dataUrl is an ordinary REST operation that answers a DataTables request. See DataTables Server-Side Processing for the endpoint and BeanQuery for the query language it executes.

Column (in org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views) pairs a column name with a SearchType and an optional SearchOperatorSet. The search types come from org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery.SearchType: searchType Matches text Case-insensitive contains. id Case-insensitive contains, intended for identifiers. numeric Exact number; range operators and relative offsets such as -24h. version Prefix match on dotted versions. timestamp Exact instant, with range operators and relative offsets. enum One value, case-insensitive. boolean true or false. When a column names no operator set it inherits the table-level set, SearchOperatorSet.standard() by default. Column.effectiveOperators() reports the resolved list, and Column.searchMeta() produces the search block that goes on the wire (the token plus each operator with its help text). Column price = Column.create("price") .label("Price") .searchType(SearchType.NUMERIC);

FieldFormat says how a text value is painted into a slot. It is the main sanitization choice for long-form text, used by regions and detail fields. Constant Wire token Behavior TEXT text textContent. The default and omitted from the wire. MARKDOWN markdown Parsed as markdown and copied node by node through an allowlist. Never innerHTML. SANITIZED_HTML sanitizedHtml Rich HTML the caller has already sanitized; painted through a wider second allowlist. SANITIZED_HTML is not a raw-HTML sink. The runtime parses the value into an inert document and copies only allowlisted elements and attributes, so event-handler attributes, style and srcdoc cannot survive. The contract is still caller-sanitizes-first. See Security Model.

FieldSpan is a closed vocabulary (ONE, the default, and FULL, every column the grid is currently rendering) that sets how many grid columns a detail field occupies. It maps to a framework class; an author never supplies a CSS value.

Row actions, selection and bulk mutation are documented on their own page. Note that the catalog lift copies only the keys in the table above. The action, selection and bulk beans are the wire-contract types for those features; check that page for how they reach a page today.
documents.s: Authoring surface for actions and selection

documents.t: juneau-icons.js is a dependency-free icon registry. It maps an icon name to inline SVG that references one in-document symbol sprite, using symbol ids of the form juneau-sym-{stem}.

Every chrome glyph resolves through up to three sprite layers; the first hit wins. Layer Source per-icon override A small sprite of a few names you want to change. replacement Your own full or partial icon set. shipped Juneau's own set, juneau-symbols.svg (ViewsMixin.SYMBOLS_SVG_PATH). All three use the same juneau-sym-{stem} symbol ids. A name present in none of them draws nothing. Configure the layers once per page, before the chrome first draws, with attributes on the script tag: <script src="/console/juneau-icons.js" data-juneau-icon-replacement="/my-set.svg" data-juneau-icon-override="/my-overrides.svg"></script> or with an equivalent script call: JuneauViews.icons.sprites({ replacementUrl: "/my-set.svg", overrideUrl: "/my-overrides.svg" }); sprites(...) returns a Promise reporting, per layer, whether it loaded, failed or was absent, and per stem which layer won. The page paints whether or not you await it. A layer that fails to load (including a blocked cross-origin fetch) is skipped and the other layers fill in. A call after first paint is ignored.

The optional Material Symbols Outlined sprite is served at ViewsMixin.SYMBOLS_MATERIAL_SVG_PATH. Select it as the replacement layer with JuneauViews.icons.pack("material") or data-juneau-icon-pack="material". Stems the Material file does not carry fall back to the shipped glyph. An explicit replacementUrl wins over the pack.

JuneauViews.icons.registerIcon("petstore-paw", "<svg viewBox='0 0 24 24'>...</svg>"); JuneauViews.icons.resolveIcon("petstore-paw"); // markup, or null when unknown registerIcon adds an icon that your application draws itself; it does not change a chrome stem. To change a built-in chrome glyph, put the replacement on the override sprite. A RowAction.icon and any catalog icon name resolve through this registry.

Failed loads, unknown ids and late registrations warn only when dev mode is on: set JuneauViews.dev = true or add data-juneau-dev to the icons script tag. Production is silent and falls back to the shipped glyph.

The runtime publishes everything on one global, window.JuneauViews. Each script adds its own members to that object and none replaces another's, so the load order below is a contract rather than a preference.

The views toolkit pack (ToolkitPackRegistry) emits these scripts in this order. A <@page toolkit="views"> page gets them automatically; a hand-built page must reproduce the order. # Script (constant on ViewsMixin) Adds 1 juneau-renders.js (RENDERS_JS_PATH) registerRenderer, resolveRenderer, the built-in renderers. 2 juneau-icons.js (ICONS_JS_PATH) icons. 3 juneau-search.js (SEARCH_JS_PATH) search, the column search-expression engine. 4 juneau-pagestate.js (PAGESTATE_JS_PATH) pageState. 5 juneau-urlstate.js (URLSTATE_JS_PATH) urlState, shareable-URL state and the View Settings Copy link button. 6 juneau-ribbon.js (RIBBON_JS_PATH) ribbon. 7 juneau-views.js (VIEWS_JS_PATH) The core: init and the table runtime. 8 juneau-config.js (CONFIG_JS_PATH) config, persistence, persistenceProviders, setPersistenceProvider; the View Settings dialog. 9 juneau-regions.js (REGIONS_JS_PATH) regions. Must come after juneau-views.js. 10 juneau-helpers.js (HELPERS_JS_PATH) helpers, including the field grid. Stylesheets are juneau-views.css and juneau-config.css. jQuery, DataTables and juneau-datatables.js are not part of the views pack; a datatables card loads them before it (see Card Asset Dependencies). A page with the calendar widget lists toolkit="views,calendar" so juneau-views.js still loads before juneau-calendar.js. The scripts are classpath resources under org/apache/juneau/views/.

Member What it is JuneauViews.registerRenderer(id, def) / resolveRenderer(id) The cell-renderer registry. See Renderers. JuneauViews.icons registerIcon, resolveIcon, loadSymbolSprite, pack, sprites, stems, nameToStem. See Icons. JuneauViews.pageState A small keyed store: get, set, remove, table(...), page(...) scopes, useStore(impl), resetStore(). JuneauViews.urlState encode, decode, readFromSearch, buildSearch, buildShareUrl, copy, resolveOpenState. JuneauViews.regions register, resolve, mount, initRegion, activateRegion, teardownRegion, ready, defaultPopulate. See Regions. JuneauViews.config View Settings support, including config.dtIndex. JuneauViews.ribbon The ribbon filter functions the view runtime calls. JuneauViews.search The search-expression parser and matcher. JuneauViews.helpers Shared builders, including the field grid. JuneauViews.init Slot mounting (mountTableSlot); what the console shell calls for a datatables card. JuneauViews.dev Set true to turn on development-mode warnings.

pageState is backed by localStorage when available and a no-op store otherwise. Use pageState.page(ns) for page-level keys and pageState.table(id) for per-table keys. useStore({getItem, setItem, removeItem}) installs an alternate store, for example a server-backed one. const prefs = JuneauViews.pageState.page("petstore"); prefs.set("lastTab", "orders"); prefs.get("lastTab");

A console page hands a datatables card to JuneauViews.regions.mount on DOMContentLoaded, so views scripts may load after the shell. See Admin-Console Chrome for the window.JuneauConsole API and the juneau:console-mounted event.

A region is an empty, framework-owned container whose body is drawn by a named JavaScript function (a populator) instead of server-emitted markup. The framework owns the container, its identity, its lifecycle and its cancellation; the populator owns everything inside it. There are exactly three region types, the RegionDef constants: Constant Where it lives TYPE_ROW_DETAIL (row-detail) Inside a table row's expandable detail panel. TYPE_CARD_BODY (card-body) In the body of a card. TYPE_TAB_BODY (tab-body) In a tab's body; lazy by default.

RegionDef (in org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views) is the server-side descriptor. RegionDef.CONTRACT_VERSION is "1" and is independent of the view, action, bulk and slot versions. Field Meaning id Unique within the host. populate Name of the client populator, or null for the built-in default. A name, not a function, so a server-side allowlist can constrain it. type One of the three types above. Usually set by the enclosing host. dataUrl Same-origin path the declarative default fetches from. null means no declared fetch. params Request parameters appended to dataUrl. Values may not be nested maps and keys may not collide with dataUrl's own query string. renderer The JuneauViews.helpers function the default populate paints with, for example field-grid. lazy Defer the first populate until visible. Defaults to false for row-detail and card-body, true for tab-body (effectiveLazy()). refreshMs Auto-refresh interval. A value below RegionDef.MIN_REFRESH_MS is clamped up to it (5000 ms on the client). fields The field catalog for card and tab regions (RegionDef.Field: label, render, href, format, span, actions). A row-detail region must not declare one. titleFields Title keys the chrome's title painter may read. Blank entries are rejected. allowedPopulators Extra populator names allowed in addition to the built-ins. config Structured configuration owned by the populator: nested maps and lists are allowed. It is never appended to dataUrl or sent to the server, and is emitted only when non-empty, so a region without it has the same sidecar as before. The populator reads it as ctx.declared.config. RegionDef.validate() is fail-closed. It rejects a blank id, a disallowed or blank populator, an unknown type, a cross-origin dataUrl, a nested-map param, a colliding param key, a config that isn't JSON-serializable, a blank title field, and a field catalog on a row-detail region or an empty one where field-grid requires it. Field renderers must be built-in ids; see Security Model.

RegionTable.of(RegionDef) produces the empty container <div class='juneau-region'> carrying identity, type and the handshake stamp. RegionTable.sidecar(hostId, regions) emits the per-host JSON sidecar; a row-detail host whose subtree is cloned per row uses RegionTable.detailSidecar(regions), which has no id to avoid collisions across open panels. In a row-detail region pass no CSRF token, since the enclosing table already stamped one. RegionTable.of(region, csrfToken) stamps the token into the response, so a host that uses it must call RequestBoundaryFilter.markTokenBearing(response) (Cache-Control: private, no-store); otherwise a shared cache can serve one session's token to another. See REST Security.

JuneauViews.regions.register("pet-history", function populate(ctx, container) { // container is empty, in the document, and yours. // Return nothing, a cleanup function, a Promise, or a Promise of a cleanup function. const p = document.createElement("p"); p.textContent = "Loaded " + ctx.declared.dataUrl; container.append(p); return function cleanup() { /* unsubscribe */ }; }); The ctx carries an abort signal that fires on teardown, a scoped emit and on for the page-wide message bus, and the declared values from the RegionDef (ctx.declared, with config present only when the region declares one). A region sees only its own ctx, so the framework can sweep all of a region's subscriptions when it tears down. A page with no regions pays nothing; the bus is created at first enrolment. The runtime requires AbortController, and refuses to populate when it is missing rather than degrading without a signal. A declared region may name a populator only if the name is a built-in or is listed in allowedPopulators. In an author-written page slot, JuneauViews.regions.mount(hookup) takes a map of element id to populator name and enrols one region per entry: JuneauViews.regions.mount({ "history-slot": "pet-history" }); It returns a thenable of the region handles. A missing element id, a blank name or an unregistered populator fails loudly and enrols nothing.

A region with no populate uses the built-in default, which fetches dataUrl (with params) and paints the result through the named renderer, typically field-grid with the declared fields. This is the declarative path: no JavaScript required.

run-view and terminal are built-in populators that are not allowed by default. Each draws a live pane that runs its own polling loop, so it ignores the region's dataUrl and refreshMs. RunViewDef.toRegion() and TerminalDef.toRegion() opt in for you; a RegionDef you build yourself must call allowPopulators("run-view") or allowPopulators("terminal"). See Run View Region and Terminal Region.

job-log runs a job for the row whose detail panel holds the region: a small form, a key fetched for that row, and the job's streamed log. It comes from the console's joblog asset pack (juneau-joblog.js), not from the views runtime, so it is a console-page feature. Its config is the job-log card's body plus submit.keyUrl, checked by JobLogChecks. JobLogRegion.toRegion() builds the region with type row-detail, populate job-log, the populator allowed, and the config; a datatables card declares the same thing as detail.region with populate: 'job-log'. See Job-Log Card and Row Jobs.

A table that polls redraws its rows on every tick, and a redraw closes any open detail panel. So while an expanded panel hosts a row job that is running (or still being submitted), the timer's reload is held for that table and the staleness pill shows Paused. This applies to every view, whether or not it sets pausePollingWhileEditing. Only the timer is held: a user reload, a sort, a filter or a page change still redraws, and re-expanding the row re-attaches the region to the running job with its log replayed from the start. A collapsed row's job and a job on a row that isn't drawn don't hold the poll. Neither does a row action's job, even with its row's panel open: it streams into the row, not the panel. When the job ends or the panel collapses, the next tick redraws as usual.
documents.s: Polling while a panel runs a job

documents.t: A Render (in org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views) names how a column's value is painted into its cell. It has an id that selects a renderer, an optional meta map of string parameters, and an optional popover.

The ids in SinkRenderAllowlist.BUILTIN_IDS are the renderers the runtime ships: date, datetime, ts-zulu, bool, linked, truncate, json, decimal, tag, progress, pill, code. linked builds an href from a template whose {property} tokens are filled from the row. Each substituted value is escaped, and the resulting URL is scheme-checked by the sink allowlist (see Security Model). pill and tag render status chips using the same pill styling as <@tag> in the chrome. A pill never emits role="button". edit:<actionId> shows the value with a pencil that turns the cell into an input (text, number or select, via the input and options meta). Enter or leaving the field saves through the named row action, sending the edited column as fields; Escape or an unchanged value cancels without a request. A failed save keeps the input open with the error beside it. The pencil follows the action's visibleWhen and enabledWhen. It is a cell renderer only and is not on the sink allowlist. Dates render through Intl.DateTimeFormat in the browser, so they follow the user's locale.

Register a renderer before the view mounts. The definition is either a bare function (treated as the display facet) or an object with display, sort, filter, type and class facets: JuneauViews.registerRenderer("stars", { display: function (cellData, rowData, meta) { const n = Number(cellData) || 0; return "★".repeat(n); // display returns a markup string: escape anything that came from data }, sort: function (cellData) { return Number(cellData) || 0; } }); JuneauViews.registerRenderer(id, def) and JuneauViews.resolveRenderer(id) are defined in juneau-renders.js, which loads first in the views pack. A column that names an unknown renderer id logs a warning and falls back to the raw value. Because the display facet returns markup, a custom renderer must escape every value that came from row data; the built-ins all do. Custom renderers apply to table cells. Field-grid fill sinks (the detail and region fields named by a RegionDef.Field.render) accept only the frozen built-in ids, and SinkRenderAllowlist.assertAllowed rejects anything else; see Security Model.

A CellPopover turns a cell into a trigger for a small popover. Set it on a Render through its popover field. Type Field Meaning CellPopover title The popover heading. CellPopover fields The PopoverField list to show. PopoverField data The row property to show. PopoverField title The label for that line. PopoverField render A Render for the value, restricted to SinkRenderAllowlist.POPOVER_TEXT_IDS (date, bool, decimal, datetime, ts-zulu). Popover fields are deliberately limited to text-only renderers: a popover cannot host a link, a code block or other interactive markup. Render r = Render.of("truncate") .popover(CellPopover.of(PopoverField.of("createdAt").title("Created").render("date")).title("Details"));
The views toolkit is built so that an author mistake fails closed instead of opening an injection or CSRF hole. This page collects the rules in one place.

Every value the runtime paints goes through one of a small number of sinks: Sink Rule Plain text (FieldFormat.TEXT) textContent. FieldFormat.MARKDOWN Parsed and copied node by node through an allowlist. Never innerHTML. FieldFormat.SANITIZED_HTML Parsed with DOMParser into an inert document; allowlisted elements and attributes are copied with createElement. Never serialized back to a string, so the mutation-XSS class cannot arise. Links (href, src) Scheme-checked. javascript:, data: and vbscript: are rejected by prefix, and a second colon-fallback rule rejects any value with a colon that is not an allowlisted absolute prefix (http:, https:, mailto: for href; http:, https: for src). The colon-fallback is the load-bearing rule: it still catches obfuscated spellings. SANITIZED_HTML does not relieve you of sanitizing: the contract is caller-sanitizes-first, with the runtime's allowlist as a second layer.

Table-cell renderers are looked up in the client registry; an unknown id warns and falls back to the raw value. Field-grid fill sinks are stricter. SinkRenderAllowlist accepts only its frozen built-in ids (date, datetime, ts-zulu, bool, linked, truncate, json, decimal, tag, progress, pill, code), and CellPopover fields are further limited to SinkRenderAllowlist.POPOVER_TEXT_IDS (date, bool, decimal, datetime, ts-zulu). A pill on a fill sink is display only and never emits role="button".

A region names a client-side populator function. PopulatorAllowlist validates RegionDef.populate against the region's allowedPopulators, so a catalog cannot name an arbitrary function; a blank populator name is rejected at validation time. A region's dataUrl must also be a same-origin path: no scheme, no leading //, and no .. segment (RegionDef.isSafeDetailEndpoint).

Row actions and bulk actions are state-changing requests. They are protected by two cooperating pieces in org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter. SynchronizerToken is a server-held secret minted in process memory, written into the pages the process serves (ViewTable stamps it as data-juneau-csrf), and required back in a request header on every state-changing request. It is deliberately not a double-submit cookie: cookies are scoped by host and ignore the port, so on a loopback port any other local server could plant a value the application would accept. Never put the token in a cookie or accept one read from a cookie. A restart invalidates every token already embedded in an open page. LoopbackBoundary decides whether a request came from the page this process served: Check Applies to Rejection Host equals the configured authority every request 421 Origin is exactly http://<authority> state-changing requests 403 Sec-Fetch-Site absent or same-origin state-changing requests 403 Content-Type base type is application/json state-changing requests 415 CSRF header equals the process's SynchronizerToken state-changing requests 403 This proves the request came from your own page. It does not prove the user meant it. Intent needs a separate mechanism, such as a typed confirmation, an arming gate, or a per-action phrase naming the target. The views toolkit keeps those concerns apart on purpose: see WritePermit on Row Actions and Bulk Mutation. A rejected request is answered with a JSON body, Cache-Control: no-store, and an X-Request-Boundary header naming the reason (for example CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING); page scripts match on that header. LoopbackBoundary is for an app pinned to one loopback address. An app reached under a real host name, over HTTPS or behind a proxy uses CsrfBoundary, which the views toolkit works with unchanged. Its checks, the proxy recipes and the rules for non-browser clients are in REST Security. HTML form posts are not supported under either boundary, because a form cannot send the token header. Any host that stamps a token into a response (a view host using ViewTable.CSRF_ATTR, RegionTable.of(region, csrfToken) or PageSpec.csrf(...)) must call RequestBoundaryFilter.markTokenBearing(response) before it writes the body, which sets Cache-Control: private, no-store. Otherwise a shared cache can serve one session's token to another. A token is never embedded into a response that is already committed, because the response can no longer be marked non-cacheable. That includes csrf attributes an author put on the page's body element. The page still loads, and its row actions and other writes then fail visibly instead of sending a request the server would refuse. Because RowAction.Method excludes safe methods and the server rejects a @Mutating operation bound to one at startup, a mutating action cannot be declared on GET.
The async-job registry enforces server-side caps that are security controls, not tuning knobs; see Async Jobs.
Admin-Console Chrome, the theme-token validation that excludes url() productions
A view table lets each user adjust how a table looks and keep those choices, and lets them share what they are looking at. These are two separate facilities that persist in different places.

The View Settings dialog (provided by juneau-config.js) has four tabs: View, Search, Sort and Options. It lets the user change the visible columns, their labels, format and order, which columns are searchable and sortable, the page size and wrapping. Apply commits the settings to the page-state store, keyed per table, so several tables on one page never overwrite each other. A reload restores them. Settings are stored through JuneauViews.pageState (see JavaScript API), not in the address bar. The dialog starts from the catalog defaults, and the saved blob is overlaid on top of them. Saved view names have a maximum length, and Default is a reserved name. For the dialog's tabs, the schemaVersion guard, settings applied on load, the Sort tab, auto-refresh and the Copy link button, see Datatable View Settings. To keep settings somewhere other than browser localStorage, install a store with JuneauViews.pageState.useStore({getItem, setItem, removeItem}), or supply a persistence provider through JuneauViews.setPersistenceProvider(provider).

Copy link builds a URL for what the user is currently looking at: the selected tab, the active filters and the sort. The state is one readable ?state= query parameter, placed directly in the address bar. JuneauViews.urlState.buildShareUrl(location, state) always includes ?state=, even when the clean-address option is on. JuneauViews.urlState.copy(navigator, text) writes to the clipboard and resolves true or false; it never throws where the Clipboard API is absent or denied. The catalog's cleanAddress key keeps the live address bar free of ?state=; Copy link still produces the full URL. The view's urlState key (TableSpec.urlState(String...), or urlState: {day: {}} in a catalog) enables built-in directives. day carries day(YYYY-MM-DD) in ?state= and restricts the table to rows whose date falls in that calendar day's [start, end) window; a malformed or impossible date is ignored. The server resource receives the value as a day query parameter by default; to use another name, call TableSpec.urlStateDayParam("on") (or set urlState: {day: {param: "on"}} in a catalog), and the request carries on instead. Views without the key behave as before.

When a page opens with ?state=, that state wins over the browser store for tab, filters and sort. It does not replace the recipient's saved View Settings: those are a separate store facet that the URL codec never touches. So a shared link shows the sender's filters and sort, laid out with the recipient's own column choices. Hand-built pages The views toolkit pack includes juneau-urlstate.js, so <@page toolkit="views"> pages get Copy link automatically. A hand-built page that uses Copy link must load ViewsMixin.URLSTATE_JS_PATH itself, after juneau-pagestate.js.

A row job is an async job started for one table row, from the row itself or from its expanded detail panel. The browser side is JuneauViews.jobs in juneau-views.js, with helpers.jobButton as a ready-made button and the console's job-log region as a declarative form. The server side is JobKeyLedger and RowJobSubmit (package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views), which bind each submit key to the row it was issued for. The job itself is an ordinary async job.

const handle = JuneauViews.jobs.run({ el: button, // inside the row or its detail panel endpoint: "/ops/species/{id}/restock", action: "restock-species", envelope: "action", keyUrl: "/ops/species/{id}/key", fields: { count: 3 }, trigger: button, hooks: { onProgress: line => log.append(line), onEnd: ({ state, result, error }) => console.info(state, result, error) } }); await handle.done; Option Meaning el Required. An element inside the row, or inside the row's detail panel. It names the row, its table and its CSRF token. endpoint Required. A same-origin path template. {id} is replaced with the row id, URL-encoded; any other {token} is refused. method POST (default) or PUT. action The action id. Required with envelope: "action"; also names the job on the bus and in the row marker. When the view declares a row action with this id, only its label is used. envelope "flat" (default) sends {action, ...fields, idempotencyKey}; "action" sends {action, targetId, idempotencyKey, fields}. idempotencyKey A key to send. Otherwise give keyUrl. keyUrl A same-origin key-endpoint template ({id} only). The key is fetched and checked before the submit. fields The values to send, already resolved. In the flat envelope action, targetId and idempotencyKey are reserved, and a null value is dropped. trigger An element disabled from the call until the job ends. paint "row" (default) paints progress and the outcome in the row's actions cell; "none" paints nothing and leaves it to the hooks. hooks onStart(ref), onProgress(line), onResult(actionResult), onEnd({state, result, error}). A hook that throws is logged (E-JS-113) and the job carries on. signal An AbortSignal. Aborting stops the request or closes the stream; it doesn't cancel a job the server has already started. run returns a frozen handle: done (a Promise of {state, result, error}), cancel() (posts to the job's cancelUrl; the outcome still arrives as the result) and job (the job ref once it has started, else null). state is succeeded, failed or cancelled from the job's outcome; refused when the submit or the result was a refusal; or error for a transport failure, an untrusted stream URL or a browser without EventSource. A refusal before anything is sent carries error.reason, from the same vocabulary as row-action refusals: row-job-running, no-row-id, missing-token, unresolved-endpoint, key-refused and the endpoint refusals. The submit's answer is settled like this: Response Result 202 and an AsyncJobRef The stream opens from the start of the job's log (lastEventId=0), tolerating the browser's own reconnects. Its streamUrl and cancelUrl must be same-origin. 2xx and an ActionResult A synchronous result: onResult, then onEnd. No stream. 4xx/5xx and an ActionResult (such as a 409 refusal) onResult with the refusal or failure, then onEnd with refused or failed. Anything else, or no answer onEnd with error.

run finds the row from el: the detail panel's parent row when el is inside a panel, else the closest tr[data-juneau-row-id] of a view table. The row id comes from that stamp only, never from a field or from row data, and a panel and row that disagree, or a blank id, refuse no-row-id with nothing sent. A call outside any row is allowed only without a row-bound key (not envelope: "action" with a keyUrl). One job per row. A second run for a row whose job is still pending or running is refused with row-job-running; helpers.jobButton and the job-log region share that rule, so they can't both run on one row. While the job runs the row carries data-juneau-job and its row-action triggers are disabled. A table redraw replaces the row's <tr>, so the marker is put back on the new row after every draw, and taken off whichever <tr> is drawn when the job ends. The same applies to row-action jobs. An ordinary row action (rowActions.run, the row menu, a cell pill or a detail button) activated on a row whose job is pending or running is refused the same way: it shows the row-job-running refusal in the row's actions cell and sends nothing, and it runs normally once the job ends. While an expanded panel hosts the row's job, the table's poll waits; see Regions.

JuneauViews.jobs.fetchKey({el, keyUrl, action}) posts {} to the key URL with the same CSRF header and credentials as a write, and resolves to the key. It accepts only an answer of the form: { "contractVersion": "1", "action": "restock-species", "targetId": "DOG", "idempotencyKey": "<64 hex chars>" } where action and targetId are the ones asked for. Anything else is refused with E-JS-109. The check catches a misconfigured key endpoint; the server's verify is the security boundary. A key lives until the server answers. It is fetched when first needed, reused after a failure with no answer (so a retry dedups on the server), and dropped on any answer, including a refusal. The next run gets a fresh key. A key-refusal is not retried with a fresh key automatically, since that could start a second job. JuneauViews.jobs.active(el, action) returns the ref of the row's running job for action, or null. JuneauViews.jobs.pending(el, action) returns, for a job still being keyed or submitted, a Promise of its ref once it starts (or null if it ends first). A view that is rebuilt, such as a detail panel collapsed and expanded again, uses these to re-attach instead of starting a second job.

JuneauViews.jobs.cancel(el, action) cancels the running job on el's row (a panel element maps to its row), and returns a Promise<boolean>. It is true once the cancel request was answered ok, and false when it was refused or failed. action filters as in active; null means "this row's job, whatever its action". It takes no URL. The request goes to the cancelUrl the server returned when the job started, with the row's CSRF token, and only if that URL is same-origin. Rewriting the ref that active or handle.job returns does not redirect it. false with nothing sent when the element is not in a row, the row has no job or the action doesn't match, the job is still pending (it has no job id yet), the CSRF token is blank, or the cancel URL is missing or untrusted. Concurrent cancels share one request. The card's Cancel button, a re-attached panel, a progress banner's Cancel and handle.cancel() all send through the same path. An accepted cancel is not cached, so a later call sends again; the server answers a repeat idempotently. The outcome arrives on the stream, as cancelled, cancelled-after-effect or, if the job finished first, succeeded. The row stays busy (marker, row-job-running refusals, poll hold) until that result. Painting. handle.cancel() and jobs.cancel paint a failed cancel into the row's actions cell only for a paint: "row" job; a paint: "none" job reports failure itself.

JuneauViews.regions.register("regroom", function (ctx, container) { container.appendChild(ctx.helpers.jobButton({ label: "Groom again", endpoint: "/ops/groom-runs/{id}/regroom", action: "regroom", envelope: "action", keyUrl: "/ops/groom-runs/{id}/key" })); }); helpers.jobButton(spec) builds a helpers.button from label and appearance (and tone, icon). A click calls JuneauViews.jobs.run with the rest of spec, and the button as both el and trigger. spec.fields may be an object or a function read at click. JuneauViews.jobs is looked up at click, so script order doesn't matter; when it is missing the click logs E-JS-111 and sends nothing.

A row job needs two endpoints: a key endpoint, and the submit endpoint that verifies the key. private final JobKeyLedger jobKeys = JobKeyLedger.create(); @RestPost(path="/species/{id}/key") public Map<String,Object> restockKey(@Path("id") String id, RestRequest req) { var s = species(id); // 404 for a row the caller can't see return JobKeyLedger.response(jobKeys.issue("restock-species", s.name(), actor(req))); } @RestPost(path="/species/{id}/restock") public Object restock(@Path("id") String id, @Content JsonMap body, RestRequest req, RestResponse res) { var s = species(id); var submit = RowJobSubmit.parse(body); if (! submit.targetId().equals(s.name())) return refused(res, RowJobSubmit.bindingRefusal()); synchronized (jobKeys) { // verify reads the claim; claim records it var grant = submit.verify(jobKeys, "restock-species", actor(req)); if (grant.isEmpty()) return refused(res, RowJobSubmit.bindingRefusal()); // 409, RowJobSubmit.REFUSAL_STATUS var key = grant.get().key(); var claimed = grant.get().jobId(); if (claimed.isPresent()) return replay(res, claimed.get()); // the recorded job, or 409 SPENT_CODE var count = count(submit.fields()); // validated after the replay check var job = registry.tryCreate(key).orElse(null); if (job == null) return limitReached(res); // 429 app:job-limit jobKeys.claim(key, job.id()); pool.execute(() -> run(job, s, count)); res.setStatus(202); return AsyncJobRef.of(job); } } The verify goes inside the lock, and the lock is the ledger's own monitor (its methods are synchronized). Two concurrent first submits of one key both pass a verify done outside the lock with no jobId; tryCreate then hands both the same job, and both would start it. Verifying inside the lock means the second sees the first's claim and replays it. JobKeyLedger is an in-memory record of issued keys, bounded and swept on access, in the same single-process spirit as AsyncJobRegistry. issue(action, targetId[, principal]) mints a 256-bit IdempotencyKey bound to the action, the row id and, when given, the caller. response(key) is the key endpoint's body. verify(value, action, targetId[, principal]) returns a Grant only for a known, unexpired key issued for exactly that binding, compared in constant time. An unknown, expired, evicted or mismatched key all return empty and get the same refusal, write-guard:idempotency-binding-mismatch, so the answer never says that a key exists for some other row. claim(key, jobId) marks the key spent once its job is created; it is idempotent for the same job. A later verify returns the grant with that jobId, and the endpoint answers with the job's ref while the registry still holds it, or with 409 write-guard:idempotency-key-spent (SPENT_CODE) after the registry has reaped it. A spent key never starts a second job. Keys expire after ttl (default 30 minutes). Each principal holds at most maxPerPrincipal (default 64) unspent keys per action, so a client minting in a loop only evicts its own oldest keys; maxEntries (default 10,000) is a global backstop. Without authentication every user shares one principal. clock(Clock) is for tests. RowJobSubmit is the action envelope. parse(body) reads {action, targetId, idempotencyKey, fields} (a missing fields is {}) and answers 400 for a blank action, targetId or key, or a fields that isn't an object. verify(ledger, expectedAction[, principal]) checks the action, then the ledger. bindingRefusal() is the standard refusal for a failed verify, sent with REFUSAL_STATUS (409). A flat-envelope row endpoint calls ledger.verify(key, action, pathId) directly. Rules for the endpoints: Resolve the caller the same way on both (for example ConsoleWrites.actor(req)), because the key is bound to it. The key endpoint applies the same authorization as the action. A key alone doesn't let anyone act (CSRF and the session still apply), but keys for rows the caller can't act on leak a capability, and an early refusal gives a clearer message. Answer 404 for a row the caller can't see. It is a POST behind CSRF, because minting writes ledger state. Act on the verified targetId. When the row id is in the path, check that it equals targetId. Field values, including hidden and row-sourced presets, are request data the user can edit; never authorize on them or take the row from them. Keep row endpoints ledger-only. An endpoint that also accepted a self-targeted key (targetId equal to the key) would be only as strong as that weaker mode. Serve dialogs and row jobs from separate endpoints.

Code When E-JS-109 fetchKey: the key endpoint refused, or its answer's contractVersion, action, targetId or key doesn't match. E-JS-111 helpers.jobButton was clicked without JuneauViews.jobs. E-JS-113 A hook passed to run threw. The job carries on.

The run-view region shows the progress and result of a multi-step run: a summary card with a headline and failures first, a list of steps with their state and duration, and a strip of colour blocks per test suite that you can hover or focus for a tooltip. It reads a stream of small, versioned events from an endpoint, or from events your own code hands to it, and reduces them to one model on the client. You can show one in three ways: Where How A console page card <@card type="run-view" id="run">{ contractVersion: '1', runView: {...} }</@card> A views page region RunViewDef.forMixin(...).toRegion() in a RegionTable A table row detail A datatables catalog detail.region with populate: 'run-view' and params The event types and the report readers live in their own small module, juneau-run-report (package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.runreport: RunEvent, RunViewChecks, ReportReaders and the readers), which has no dependency on the REST server. A producer such as a build tool can depend on it alone. The rest of the server half ships in juneau-rest-server-views (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views), which depends on juneau-run-report; the client half is juneau-run-view.js, part of the views toolkit pack. It pairs naturally with the Terminal Region: the run view summarizes, the terminal holds the raw output, and a test block can link to the terminal offset it came from.

The contract version is "1". The client accepts one event, an array of events, or a page: { "contractVersion": "1", "events": [ { "ev": "step", "seq": 1, "id": "build", "title": "mvn package" } ], "next": "k3x9ab.1", "more": false, "terminal": false } Page member Rules contractVersion Required. Exactly "1"; anything else is fatal (E-RV-2). events Required, may be empty. Ascending seq. At most 2,000 per page from the bundled endpoint. next Required. An opaque token (^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,128}$) the client sends back as ?after=. more Required. true when the source holds more events right now; the client re-fetches at once. terminal Optional, default false. true means the source will never produce another event. The client stops polling when it sees terminal: true with more: false. Every event carries ev and, in a page, a strictly increasing seq (gaps are fine). An unknown ev and unknown members are ignored silently, so the contract can grow. A malformed known event is dropped and reported once per batch (E-RV-3). Strings over their limit are truncated with a trailing … on the client and rejected by the Java factories. ev Members Meaning step id (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$), title (1-200), optional n, status (running or waiting), rawOffset A step starts, or an open step is updated. end id, status (ok, fail, skip), optional ms, exit The step finishes. exit is shown in the step tooltip only. suite step, fw, suite (1-512), counts {pass, fail, skip}, optional rawOffset A live placeholder result for a whole suite, before per-test detail exists. test step, fw, suite, name (1-512), status (pass, fail, skip, error), optional ms, msg (2,000), trace (8,000), rawOffset One test result. replace step Discard the step's suites and tests so a fresh, authoritative set can follow. note level (info, warn, error), text (1-1,000), optional href, step A notable event, shown under its step or under the run. done status (ok, fail, cancelled) The run finished. fw is the test framework key (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31}$). The counts line labels the built-in keys surefire (Surefire), junit-xml (JUnit), pytest (pytest), jest (Jest) and playwright (Playwright); any other key is displayed as itself.

The client applies events in seq order and skips any event at or below the last applied seq, so a replayed page is harmless. A step with a new id appends a step. With a known, open id it updates the title, ordinal, status and rawOffset (a waiting step becoming running is a second step event). For an ended step it is dropped. An end for an unknown step is dropped; a second end replaces the first. Suites are keyed by (step, fw, suite). A suite event creates a placeholder with counts; the first test for the key converts it to a detailed suite and discards the placeholder counts. replace removes all suites and tests of a step. Which suites the user expanded survives it. A step still open when a done exists is shown as fail if the run failed, otherwise skip.

A step cannot reopen once it has ended, so a producer that runs a step again sends it as a new step: the first run keeps the plain id and later runs take <id>.2, <id>.3 and so on, titled <title> (attempt 2), <title> (attempt 3). The client recognizes this naming, and shows only the latest attempt in the step list. The earlier attempts sit under it behind an N earlier attempts toggle (1 earlier attempt for a single one), collapsed by default. A step id counts as an attempt only when the step it extends (build for build.2) exists; a title ending in (attempt N) is recognized the same way when the ids do not follow the pattern. Expanding the toggle lists the earlier attempts, oldest first, each as an ordinary step. The toggle stays open as later attempts arrive, and picking a failure from the summary list opens it when that failure belongs to an earlier attempt. [ { "ev": "step", "id": "build", "title": "mvn package" }, { "ev": "end", "id": "build", "status": "fail" }, { "ev": "step", "id": "build.2", "title": "mvn package (attempt 2)" } ] This shows one step, mvn package (attempt 2), with a collapsed 1 earlier attempt toggle under it. Counts and the failures list still include every attempt. The run status is derived, not sent: Condition Status Headline No events yet empty Waiting for events… Page terminal with no done stopped Stopped No done, a step waiting and none running waiting Waiting at title No done running Running done is ok ok Passed done is fail fail Failed at title done is cancelled cancelled Cancelled

RunViewMixin serves GET /juneau-run-view/{runId}/events?after=<token>. Implement runViewSource to resolve the run id, and return an empty Optional for an id the caller may not read (the endpoint answers 404, never a distinguishable 403): @Rest public class Runs extends BasicRestServlet implements RunViewMixin { static final Map<String,RunViewSource> SOURCES = new ConcurrentHashMap<>(); @Override public Optional<RunViewSource> runViewSource(String runId, RestRequest req) { return Optional.ofNullable(SOURCES.get(runId)); } } RunViewEndpoints gives the same logic for custom paths. An unknown or stale after token answers 410 Gone, and the client then reloads the stream from the start with no banner.

RunViewLog is a thread-safe in-memory source that the producer appends to: RunViewLog log = RunViewLog.create(); Runs.SOURCES.put("42", log); log.append(RunEvent.step("build", "mvn package")); log.append(RunEvent.suite("build", "surefire", "FooTest", 12, 0, 0)); log.append(RunEvent.end("build", RunEvent.EndStatus.OK)); log.append(RunEvent.done(RunEvent.DoneStatus.OK)); log.close(); // the final page carries terminal: true append numbers the event and returns it; appendAll takes a batch. The log holds at most RunViewLog.DEFAULT_MAX_EVENTS (200,000) events. reset() empties it and starts a new epoch, so clients holding an old token get 410. FileRunViewSource pages one growing JSON Lines file, one event per line. The line number is the seq, so write events without one. Only complete lines are read, and a truncated or replaced file answers 410: RunViewSource src = FileRunViewSource.create(root.resolve("run-42.jsonl")) .terminal(() -> run.isFinished()) .build(); The application supplies the Path; nothing in a request ever becomes a path. Keep one instance per file. Implement RunViewSource for anything else.

The readers in juneau-run-report turn test-report files into events, and work without the region. A reader never throws for bad input: a missing, unreadable, oversize, malformed or truncated file yields the tests it could recover plus a warning. Kind passed to ReportReaders.forKind Reader fw surefire SurefireReportReader (a directory of TEST-*.xml, or one file) surefire junitxml JUnitXmlReportReader junit-xml pytest JUnitXmlReportReader("pytest") pytest jest-json JestJsonReportReader jest playwright-json PlaywrightJsonReportReader playwright forKind returns null for an unknown kind. The XML readers stream the file with external entities and DTDs disabled. ReportLimits.DEFAULT caps a file at 32 MiB and a report at 100,000 tests, with names clipped to 512 characters, messages to 2,000 and traces to 8,000. ReportResult result = ReportReaders.forKind("surefire").read(reportsDir, ReportLimits.DEFAULT); for (RunEvent e : result.toEvents("build")) log.append(e); toEvents(step) returns replace, one test per test, then one warn note per warning (such as report truncated: unexpected end of file after 4120 tests). A result with warnings and no recovered tests returns only the notes, so the step keeps its live suite placeholders. Warning text names files, never absolute paths.

RunViewDef def = RunViewDef.forMixin("run", "", "42") // id, mount path, run id .title("Run 42") .refreshMs(2000) .rawHref("#raw-O{offset}"); RegionTable.of(def.validate().toRegion()); Option Meaning eventsUrl Same-origin events URL; {id} is replaced by the row id in a row detail. Required unless poll is false. refreshMs Poll interval, at least 1000. poll false skips polling; you feed events through the JavaScript API. compact Smaller layout for a row detail: a three-failure list and a one-line summary when clean. title Accessible name of the region; default "Run". rawHref Template for block links, containing {offset} once, such as #raw-O{offset}. onBlockClick Function called when a test block is clicked, or activated with Enter or Space. JavaScript API only; see Block clicks.

<@card type="run-view" id="run" title="Run">{ contractVersion: '1', runView: { eventsUrl: '/juneau-run-view/42/events', rawHref: '#raw-O{offset}' } }</@card> The keys of runView are exactly those above. id= is required; src= and template= are rejected.
